| The presets | `delver-mirror`, `delver-smoke` (`mtgz/az/__init__.py`) | 54.6 |
| Gates | `tests/cards_legacy.rs`, `tests/constructed.rs`, `az.rs` `legacy_registry_and_identities`, `tests/measure_delver.rs`, `FUZZ_POOL=delver`, the search smoke's `delver` spec, `tests/test_delver.py`, the rulings | 54.7 |

### 54.2 The IR: two cards, one schema

Prismari Charm parsed already (mtg-bot claims it in its roto pool): `ModalChooseOne` of
`Sequence(Surveil 2, DrawCards 1)`, `DealDamageToEachTarget` (amount 1, one `TargetSpec` of 1..2 any
targets) and `Bounce` (target nonland permanent). Murktide Regent did not: three of its four lines
failed. mtg-bot's `cards/parser/legacy_creatures.py` (parameterized recognizers, hooked into the
creature builder before the U/B bucket's) adds `Delve` on a creature (`has_delve`); "This creature
enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each <types> card exiled with it"
(`CardPrinting.enters_with_counter_per_card_exiled_with_it`, an object predicate:
`ObjectOr(HasPrintedCardType Instant, HasPrintedCardType Sorcery)`); "Whenever a <types> card leaves
your graveyard, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature" (`Event.LEAVES_GRAVEYARD`, subjects `player` =
the graveyard's owner and `card`; the predicate `Subject(card, ...) & Controlled(player)`). The Python
engine plays neither ability (data for this engine, as companion was: a permanent entering with
either raises `NotImplementedError`; mtg-bot SEARCH_LIMITATIONS, "Legacy pool" 1). The pool `legacy`
is in no other pool; the cube, roto, EoE and `all` pools' claimed printings and IR are unchanged
(compared card by card with the branch point).

**One schema for both files.** mtg-bot builds a schema from the printings it encodes, so a
legacy-only export would carry another schema than the cube's, and the `card_ir` crate (generated
from one schema, checking every document's hash) could not read both. `mtg_bot cards export-ir --pool
cube legacy` builds one schema over both pools' printings and writes `powerlsv.ir.json`,
`legacy.ir.json` and `powerlsv.schema.json`: schema `181ba4b8a1e7...` (before `7100f8436556...`:
one class more, `DealDamageToEachTarget`, one field, one `Event` member). `powerlsv.ir.json`'s 546
cards are byte for byte the cube-only export's (the card list and order unchanged; only
`schema_sha256` differs); `card_ir/src/generated.rs` regenerated (25 lines). The lowering's
exhaustive destructuring made the new field a compile error until it was lowered.

### 54.3 The rules

| Text | Rule | How |
|---|---|---|
| Delve on a creature spell | 702.66 | the existing delve (18, 51) of any spell with `CardDef::delve`: at most the generic part of the total cost, cards only, exiled after the mana abilities |
| "enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each instant and sorcery card exiled with it" | 607.2q (the cards exiled to pay the cost of the spell that became the permanent: linked to an ability *printed on it* that exiles cards while paying), 614.1c | `CardDef::counters_per_exiled` (a filter on a card's own characteristics, `deck_filter_ok`). As delve exiles a card for such a spell, `Mark::ExiledToPay(card)` goes on the spell (`record_exiled_to_pay`: graveyard picks and delve's mana sources alike); as the spell resolves into a permanent, the marked cards still in exile as the same objects (400.7) that match the filter are counted (`exiled_to_pay_count`) and it enters with that many (`Game::entering_exiled`, `entering`). Not cast (reanimated, put onto the battlefield): none. A copy of the spell: none (707.10: no cost was paid for it). A card with its own escape (printed too) would be a blocker, not a silent zero |
| "Whenever an instant or sorcery card leaves your graveyard, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature" | 603.10a (abilities that trigger when a card leaves a graveyard look back in time), 603.2 | `EventKind::LeavesGraveyard` (subjects: the owner, the card), recorded in `move_card` before the card moves, whatever zone it goes to (exile, hand, library, stack, battlefield), cards only (108.2), and only in games with such a card (`SEEN_GY_LEAVE`); a `Subject` predicate on it reads the card in the graveyard (`card_matches`), where other events read permanents and spells only. One trigger per card (not "one or more") |
| "deals 1 damage to each of one or two targets" | 115.3 (distinct), 608.2b | `DealDamageToEachTarget` lowers to `Op::DealDamage` over one requirement of 1..2 |

Readings taken (the ambiguities resolved):

* **A Regent's own delve doesn't trigger it**: the cards leave the graveyard while it is a spell
  (601.2h); its triggered ability works on the battlefield (113.6). A second Regent's delve triggers
  one already on the battlefield once per instant or sorcery card, the triggers going on the stack
  above the second Regent as it becomes cast (603.3).
* **"Exiled with it" is the spell's delve only**: Underworld Breach's escape (an alternative cost
  granted to the card, not printed on it) exiles cards to pay its cost too, but 607.2q links only an
  ability printed on the permanent spell, so those cards don't count (tested). Instants exiled by
  another Regent's delve are in exile but weren't exiled with this one (tested).
* **A card that leaves exile before the Regent resolves** isn't counted (a new object, 400.7); no card
  of the mirror can do that.
* **"Your graveyard"** is the graveyard of the trigger's controller: a card is in its owner's
  graveyard (404.2), so the owner is compared with the controller (a stolen Regent would count its
  new controller's).
* **"Instant and sorcery card"** reads each card's printed types (it is in exile, or in the
  graveyard): `HasPrintedCardType`, as the cube's graveyard filters.

### 54.4 Constructed decks and the spec

`"constructed": true` (read before the other keys: it picks the card table the names are looked up
in) needs explicit decklists (`decks: {"p0": [...], "p1": [...]}`, sideboards optional) and checks CR
100.2a and 100.4a (`az::constructed::check`): at least 60 cards (`MIN_DECK`; more is legal), at most
four of a card other than basic lands (supertype basic and a land) over the deck and the sideboard
together (`MAX_COPIES`), a sideboard of at most 15 (`MAX_SIDEBOARD`), cards only (no token, no face),
and **at most 64 cards** (`MAX_DECK`, the engine's limit, not the CR's: every card of a deck may end up
in one zone, and a hand, a library list and a graveyard have 64 action slots each, section 11:
`act::HAND_N`, `LIBRARY_N`, `GRAVEYARD_N`, the bound derived from them; a 65-card deck is refused at
the spec with that reason rather than reaching an out-of-range slot mid-game).
Best-of-three is an error (constructed sideboarding is not built, 54.8), so are pools and random,
evaluation and drafted decks (limited's). Without the key every spec is what it was: the cube's card
table (in which "Murktide Regent" is an unknown card) and limited's 40 (section 42), untouched. The
evaluation spec of a decklist spec is the spec (`eval_json`, `mtgz.az.evaldecks.eval_spec`), so the
yardstick, random and Elo games play the mirror too.

**60-card games needed nothing new**: `Game::with_sideboards` took decks of any size (the card slots
are 0..59 and 60..119); the play-or-draw choice (103.1), the London mulligan (103.5) and the turn cap
(a draw after `max_turns`) are tested with the 60s (`constructed.rs`); the action ranges fit (a
graveyard holds at most its owner's 60 cards, under the 64 `GRAVEYARD` slots; the library, hand and
pile lists under 64); the encoding's library size / 40 squashes as it did.

### 54.5 Hidden information: open decklists

Best-of-one keeps open decklists (section 10): each player knows both 75s, the cards in play are the
60s; hidden are the hands, library order and face-down cards. `Game::determinize` deals the
opponent's hidden cards again from their own cards, so in every world the opponent's 60 card slots
hold exactly their decklist, the multiset of their hidden cards is the decklist minus every card of
theirs the viewer has seen (public zones, cards known exactly, clouds), what the viewer knows stays,
and its encoding and legal actions don't change. Tested on 408 worlds of 12 heuristic games
(`determinize_samples_the_opponents_unseen_cards_from_their_decklist`: the opponent's hand differs
from the real one in 262) and by `FUZZ_POOL=delver`'s checks (54.7). Sideboards stay outside the game
(the preset passes none).

### 54.6 The preset and its measurements

**`delver-mirror`** (`mtgz/az/__init__.py`) is `mtg-3` (22.8: the last best-of-one run) on the
mirror's spec (`decklists.mirror_spec`: `{"max_turns": 60, "mulligans": true, "constructed": true,
"decks": {"p0": <the 60>, "p1": <the 60>}}`, no sideboards), with `eval_spec` the same spec: the token
network 128 x 4 (4 heads, feed-forward 256) on layout v4, CUDA inference (one worker, 2 groups, 8
search threads) and training, 768 games in flight, 600 games an iteration, 64 / 16 simulations
(`p_full` 0.25), mana payments at 4 (`sims_minor`), completed-Q targets, value_q 0.9, lr 1e-3, batch
512, reuse 2, window 6 (growing), a 12 GB window budget, `max_steps` 20,000; the yardsticks the M7c
heuristic (21.4: the Elo anchor, 1000) playing the same deck, 100 games at 32 simulations, and random,
50; Elo against the 2 previous checkpoints, 20 games each, in one driver. **`delver-smoke`**:
`mtg-smoke` on that spec (CPU, a 32 x 1 network, 3 tiny iterations).

  shape with red: the target any spell or permanent, the colour checked on resolution), Meltdown ({X}:
  "destroy each artifact with mana value X or less", 30), Price of Progress (damage to each player by
  the nonbasic lands they control, counted on resolution), Rough // Tumble (a split card, 25 and 709:
  2 damage to each creature without flying, 6 to each with flying).
* **Constructed best-of-three** (`"constructed"` with `"format": "bo3"` is refused) needs: sideboarding
  bounds of constructed play in `MatchPool::new` (today a spec decklist keeps its size exactly, 42.2):
  a deck of 60..=75 cards from the 75 (at least 60, 100.2a; the sideboard the rest, at most 15, 100.4a;
  the four-card limit holds by construction since the pool is the legal 75); the pool list fits (29
  distinct names of 64 `LIBRARY` entries; counts at most 4 of 31); the information model (36.11) with
  open 75s: no first picks, both pools known, the opponent's chosen deck hidden between games

  heuristic keeps its deck (`PASS`); the fuzzer's matches and the search smoke's match spec for the

* **The yardstick's limits in this deck** (54.6): the heuristic mulligans by land count only, always

## 55. The declared mulligan in the encoding

Branch `mull-declared` (from main at 05e37bb). The London mulligan's declarations (CR 103.5) are
public, and one of them was not in the network's input. The fix fills two of layout v4's spare
globals: layout v4 is unchanged (33,652 floats, `mtgz/az/layout_v4.json` unchanged), checkpoints of
every v4 run load as they are, and the rules engine is untouched (the behaviour digests without
encodings are equal). The opening sequence was audited for gaps of the same kind (55.4).

### 55.1 The gap

In turn order each player who has not kept declares keep (`PASS`) or mulligan (`YES`); then every
player who declared a mulligan takes it (section 5). `Game::mulligan_declare` sets
`Player::mulligan_declared` for a mulligan and `Player::kept` for a keep; `mulligan_run` takes the
mulligans once both have declared (the flag cleared, `mulligans` + 1, seven new cards) and the
bottoms follow. The encoding had per player `mulligans` / 4 (per-player global 12) and `kept` (13),
not the declaration. So after the starting player declared a mulligan, the next position (the
other player's declaration) encoded, outside the decision's context block, **exactly** as the
position before the declaration (measured on main's encoding: 240 of 240 cases, three specs, 40
seeds, both viewers): the same hands, the same counts, `kept` 0; only the context's decider (and,
for the decider, its option count) differed. "Keep" set `kept`. Two consequences:

1. The search's first leaf after the starting player's "Mulligan" read like the undecided root,
   with the hand it would throw away, while "Keep" was visible: the mulligan's cost (a card) was
   in that leaf's input only through the order (below). This matters most for the Delver mirror (`runs/delver1`, 54.9), whose early
   networks mulligan to zero, and for the cube's `mtg` and `team_draft` play.
2. The second player declared without the first player's declaration in the state (public in real
   play).

The declaration was inferable, but only through the order: at the second player's declaration the
starting player has always either kept or declared (a player at seven mulligans keeps without a
decision), so `kept` = 0 there means a declared mulligan. A network had to learn that conjunction
(the kind `Mulligan`, the decider not the starting player, `g[18]`, and the starting player's
`kept`); a fresh one does not know it. Only that one state is affected: the second player's own
declaration of a mulligan is taken at once (the next position shows `mulligans` + 1), and nothing
else is decided while a declaration waits.

### 55.2 The fix: two spare globals

Where a float was free (22.6-22.7: a change to a width, offset, segment or identity is layout v5;
a field in a spare float keeps v4):

| Block | Used | Free |
|---|---|---|
| per-player globals (`g[24 + 40 side..]`) | 0-37, v4's 38-39 | none |
| globals | 0-23, the per-player 24-103, day and night 104-105, the rooms 106-123, `CHOOSER` 124 | **125-127** |
| context (256) | 0-245 (`ctx::END`) | 246-255, the decision's, not the game's |
| match (32) | 0-26 (`mtch::END`) | 27-31, the match's |

`glob::MULLIGAN_DECLARED` = 125: `g[125 + side]` (viewer first, as the rooms' `9 side`) is that
player's `mulligan_declared`, for both viewers (public); 127 stays spare. A const assert keeps 125-126
clear of the rooms and the chooser and inside the 128 globals. `layout_v4.json` describes the
segments and bags only (every other float is a global), so it is unchanged, and `NUM_FEATURES`,
the action ids and every other feature's meaning and offset are main's. The flag is 1 only in the
state of 55.1; every other state encodes bit for bit as before (55.3, 55.5).

**What a v4 checkpoint sees.** The token network reads the globals through one linear map
(`TokenNet.g`: 160 inputs, the 128 globals and the match block) into the global token. Inputs 125
and 126 were always 0 in training, so AdamW never moved their weight columns but for weight decay
(delver1: 1e-4 at lr 1e-3, a factor 1 - 1e-7 a step): they are still their initialisation. A checkpoint loads
and plays unchanged; in the declared state it adds an untrained direction to the global token
(measured in 55.6) until training gives the input a meaning.

**`Game::view_of`** (testkit: the observable view the hidden-information checks compare across
worlds) also left the mulligan state out: `mulligans`, `kept` and `mulligan_declared` are in it now
(Keep and Mulligan looked the same there). No behaviour or encoding depends on it.

### 55.3 Tests

`tests/az.rs`, on three specs (the cube's random best-of-one decks, a best-of-three match's first
game, the Delver mirror):

* `cr_103_5_a_declared_mulligan_is_encoded`: for both viewers, after the starting player's
  "Mulligan" the encoding differs from the one before the declaration outside the context block in
  exactly the declared flag (main: no float), and from "Keep" in exactly `kept` and the flag; the
  views of Keep and Mulligan differ.
* `cr_103_5_the_second_player_sees_the_declaration_and_it_clears`: the second player's decision
  shows the opponent's declaration, in round 1 and round 2; when both declare the mulligans are taken
  at once (seven new cards each, counts 1), the flags are clear through the bottoms, before round 2's
  declaration and after the starting player's second mulligan.
* `cr_103_5_the_declared_flags_follow_the_game`: in every sampled opening state, both viewers, the
  flags are the players' `mulligan_declared`, set only at the second player's declaration after the
  starting player's mulligan.
* `the_declared_mulligan_survives_clones_and_determinize`: a clone and a game rebuilt from its
  seed and replayed encode equally; `determinize` for either viewer keeps the flag and the viewer's
  encoding, and every world takes the declared mulligan when the other player keeps; two worlds of
  the starting player after the same declaration encode equally (zero-core's child signature).
* `opening_encodings_but_the_declaration_are_unchanged`: the encodings of every state of 40 seeded
  openings per spec (the play-or-draw choice to turn 1, both viewers), with globals 125-126 masked,
  hash to the values recorded on main at 05e37bb (cube 6f267cb231046dd1, bo3 03550aad88c4a965,
  delver cb3395e062b2fd8f): the flag changed no other float.
* `the_opening_encodes_no_hidden_information` (55.4).

Without the flag's line in `encode_globals`, the first four fail and the fifth passes; without the
`view_of` change, the first fails. Six tests in all, `az.rs` 15 -> 21.

### 55.4 The opening audit

Every decision before turn 1 (`Task::PlayDraw`, `RevealCompanion`, `DrawHands`, `MulliganDeclare`,
`MulliganRun`, `MulliganBottom`, `Opening`; sideboarding comes between the games of a match, 36.2),
for what each outcome leaves in the encoding and what the other player sees:

| Decision | Outcome in the encoding | Hidden from the other player |
|---|---|---|
| play or draw (103.1) | `g[18]` the viewer starts, `g[124]` the viewer chose | nothing hidden yet (the hands are drawn after it) |
| companion reveal (103.2b) | the companion segments, `glob::COMPANION`; a decline changes nothing (no companion) | whether asked: the deck and sideboard, public with open decklists; asked always with hidden decks (35.5, 36.11); options only for the decider |
| opening hands (103.5) | hand sizes; the viewer's own hand | the cards (keyed `KEY_DRAW`, private) |
| keep or mulligan (103.5) | `kept`; **the declaration (new)**; `mulligans` once taken | the hand |
| bottoms (103.5) | hand and library sizes; `ctx::BOTTOMS_LEFT` (public) | which card (a private choice: `scramble`) |
| opening-hand actions (103.6: Gemstone Caverns) | the permanent, the exiled card (public); a decline changes nothing | whether its card is in the hand: asked whenever the deck (with hidden decks: the known pool) holds one |

Findings:

* **No other public outcome is missing.** A probe over 400 seeded openings per spec (every legal
  action at every opening decision, both viewers) found the encoding unchanged outside the context
  only for outcomes that change no game state: declining a companion or an opening-hand action
  before the other player's turn to decide, and choosing to play first when the next decision comes
  before the hands are drawn (best-of-three: the reveal is always asked). Then `g[18]` already read 1
  for the chooser while the choice was pending (`turn.starting` is provisional until then); the
  pending kind `PlayDraw` tells the two apart, and no other decision comes between, unlike 55.1.
* **No private information in the opponent's encoding or view**: the new test
  `the_opening_encodes_no_hidden_information` checks, in every sampled opening state of the three
  specs (40 games each: 4,476 worlds), that both players' encodings and views are the same in every
  world `determinize` makes for them, and that two worlds of the decider played with the same action
  encode equally while the keys, the next decider and its options agree (692 pairs). The gap of 55.1
  was a missing public fact, not a leak.
* Not changed, recorded: when Gemstone Caverns' question (asked whenever the deck holds one) has
  only `PASS` (none in the hand), `auto_single` answers it with a public `KEY_AUTO`, so a search's
  tree branches on whether the hand holds one; that is section 10's general treatment of a
  single-option decision, not the encoding (the Delver mirror has no opening-hand card). The
  spectator / UI view (`az/view.rs`, JSON) shows `mulligans` but not `kept` or a declaration; no
  network or check reads it.

### 55.5 Behaviour digests

`DIGEST_ENCODING=0` (the behaviour alone): combined digest **5f0579aa50453818 before (05e37bb) and
after**: no game plays differently. With the encodings, 804002969bdd0938 before (every game equal to
`tests/data/digests.txt`) and **0052143696be4ce3** after, re-recorded with `DIGEST_WRITE=1`: 11 of the
2,500 games differ (r 147, 291, 376, 472, 555, 984, 1106, 1494, 1681, 1902, 1983), exactly the games
whose hashed encodings (every 10th decision) include a state with a declared mulligan (a probe listed
them).

## 56. One shared work queue for remote self-play (M6)

Branch `shared-queue` (from main 44e9dd5, rebased onto a21b977), zero-core pinned at
`feat/shared-queue` (from core main 3c26d9f; its `zero/workqueue.py`, docs/az.md 5.3 and 11.6):
first at 213a9c0 (the branch's b333920 / cc314f2 before the rebase - **runs/delver1's code from its
iteration 30**, 56.4), then at 9453e18 (the batch-bound rule, 56.5). The requirements of 2026-10-28
(the user and the main session): one pull model for single-game and co-training runs, per-machine
in-flight caps from measured throughput so that a game starts and finishes within about one
iteration, the desktop never starved, a backing-off remote giving its work back, the invariants of
52 kept, an optional "keep playing while the desktop trains". The engine is main's: this branch
changes the pin, a preset, two tests and this file.

### 56.1 Why: both of 52's designs, measured

* **Single-game ("the desktop's quota + the Mac's extras", 52.1).** `runs/delver1` (`log.txt`,
  `metrics.jsonl`, the `net` column of `data/iter_*/*.npz`: the checkpoint that searched each row):
  with `--games 100` and 768 desktop / 1,536 Mac games in flight the rows were 3-4 iterations stale
  (iteration 13's desktop shard: nets 4-12, 20% from net 4, 8% from the newest); with `--games 400`
  the desktop's quota set a 25-40 minute iteration while the Mac finished 4,120 games / 348k samples,
  more than the 20 GB window holds (296k), and training took 9 minutes with both machines idle. At
  today's settings (`--games 150 --conc 192`, 2 Mac workers of 768) iteration 22's rows: the
  desktop's mean lag 0.77 checkpoints (max 3, 86% within one), **the Mac's 1.44 (max 4, 59% within
  one)**; an iteration of ~5 minutes takes 150 desktop + ~700 Mac games (~72k samples, of which the
  window keeps 296k of 360-495k). The Mac idles through every training phase and backs off during
  the evaluations (iteration 25: 206 s). (54.11 has the run's throughput.)
* **Co-training (a shared queue already, 52.1).** td1's iteration 7: the Mac's 3 workers, each
  allowed 960 outstanding, drained the queue; the desktop's GPU played 0 of 1,812 matches, the Mac
  ran at 6.9k leaves/s and spent 366 s backing off for the remote evaluation's lock holding those
  matches (requeued only after 3,600 s of running time); the iteration took 62 minutes against
  28-38 without the Mac. In iteration 6 the split was 2,083 Mac / 520 desktop at 19.2k leaves/s.

### 56.2 The design (zero-core `feat/shared-queue`: docs/az.md 5.3, 11.6)

* **The queue and the caps.** An iteration needs `units`: a single-game run's `games` - **the
  finished games of the iteration across every machine** - or a co-training run's matches (its
  `games` events x the matches per event). Each consumer - the desktop's driver and every Mac
  worker - takes work as it has room under its in-flight cap, `cap = inflight x rate x (lead + P)`,
  `P = (units - sum rate x lead) / total rate`: its measured throughput (leaves per running second
  over the leaves per finished game, an EWMA; so a worker whose games outlast a phase is measured
  too) times its share of the iteration's running time (`lead`: a remote's head start before the
  desktop's phase), bounded by a few games per group and its slots (`conc`). The caps sum to
  `inflight x units`: one iteration's worth with `selfplay_remote_inflight` 1 (the default), so a game
  takes about one iteration. A worker backing off or offline is no consumer: its cap is 0 and the
  others' grow at once (the desktop alone: the whole quota, up to its slots). Before a measurement
  the rates follow the slots, a remote at a quarter of that until its first measurement; a restart
  takes them from the last metrics row (delver1's first row on this code: from its 52-design
  `selfplay.remote`).
* **Batch-bound consumers** (zero-core fac4a70, 56.5): a consumer whose inference is CUDA / MPS -
  the desktop's driver - keeps its **slots** while its games take at most
  `selfplay_remote_batch_inflight` (2) iterations, `cap = max(inflight x share, min(slots,
  batch_inflight x share))` with `share = rate x (lead + P)`: its throughput grows with its games in
  flight, so the share alone starved it (56.4). The CPU workers keep the share exactly.
* **Single-game: an exact shared quota.** Both machines play rolling `queue_only` drivers fed one
  setup of the run's spec per game they may start. A finished game counts only once the desktop's
  quota accepts it (its own at once, a worker's in answer to its `fin` line); the iteration ends at
  exactly `games`; games finishing beyond the quota wait with their samples for the next iteration
  (the driver hands out each game's rows and samples together: `workqueue.split_games` cuts them
  per game). A worker holds no share of the quota, so a back-off, a sleep or a death leaves the rest
  to the desktop; a worker that dies with accepted games not yet in a shard gives them back while the
  desktop still plays.
* **Co-training: the desktop's share in reserve.** The coordinator keeps the local resolver
  driver's room under its cap queued for it; a worker takes only what is queued beyond that, up to
  its own cap. A worker backing off for `selfplay_remote_giveback` (30) s gives its outstanding
  matches back (requeued at the front, a late second copy dropped); a match outstanding longer than
  `selfplay_remote_overdue` (3) x its worker's expected latency (at least 120 s, at most
  `selfplay_remote_timeout`) is requeued. The events and their exact quota are the coordinator's as
  before.
* **Linger** (`selfplay_remote_linger` 1, opt-in, default off): the workers play on with their
  checkpoint while the desktop trains and evaluates; those games count for the next iteration, one
  checkpoint behind it.
* **Kept**: same-phase shards (a shard of phase i only into `data/iter_i/`), the exact quota (now of
  both machines), `pending_max` (its default formula too), duplicate drops, requeue on a session's
  or worker's death, the head start (the remote's phase begins when the checkpoint is written) and
  the mirrors (`~/mtgz-selfplay/<run>`, `<run>.resolver`), the back-off modes and busy markers; a run
  without a remote plays exactly as before (zero-core's shards byte for byte, 56.7).
* **Settings and compatibility.** New: `selfplay_remote_inflight` (1.0), `selfplay_remote_giveback`
  (30), `selfplay_remote_overdue` (3), `selfplay_remote_linger` (0), `selfplay_remote_batch` ('auto':
  by the device; 'local', 'remote', 'all', 'none') and `selfplay_remote_batch_inflight` (2.0); kept:
  `selfplay_remote_procs`, `selfplay_remote_wait`, `selfplay_remote_timeout` (3,600: now the ceiling
  of the overdue limit, saved so in every run's config). Every `runs/*/config.json` loads (delver1, td1, mtg1-5, and
  Kingdom Builder Zero's 21 by their keys); a saved config gets the new settings' defaults. **An
  existing run's `games`** means the total of both machines from its first iteration on this code:
  the cleanest reading (one number for an iteration's data, with or without the Mac; a run without a
  remote is unchanged), so delver1 changed `--games` to 800 at its re-pin (56.4). The first
  design's "the desktop's quota + extras" is gone.

### 56.3 mtgz

* The pin; **`mtg-4-mac`** = mtg-4 + the Mac (its 600 matches are the total now: mtg-4's data per
  iteration, sooner), 52's `games=200` dropped (`tests/test_drafted.py`).
* `tests/test_mac_remote.py`'s worker test plays self-play under a `cap` of 3 and accepts the games
  it reports (`fin`): the shards hold the accepted games, the worker's `end` counts them.
* The Mac's remote spec is unchanged: its `conc` 768 per worker is now the caps' ceiling (`hi`), not
  the in-flight; 4 groups of 192 slots, 12 threads, 4 inference workers, CPU inference (not
  batch-bound: `auto` leaves its caps the throughput share). At delver1's caps (325-370 per worker,
  56.4) a group's batches hold ~85 games instead of 192, and the Mac's leaves per running second
  fell from 27.8-29.7k to 24.7-26.7k (-10 to -15%): whether 2 groups win that back is for a Mac
  measurement (56.11).

  that starts small measures a small rate, which gives a small cap again; it only settles where the

  at 5.2-5.3k leaves/s against 6.1-6.8k with all 192.
* **The Mac's CPU workers are not.** Their rate is their cores': 24.7-26.7k leaves per running
  second at 325-370 in flight each against 27.8-29.7k at 768 (-10 to -15%: some batch effect, 4
  groups of ~85 games against 192), so the throughput share is the right cap for them; they make
  ~82% of the data.

### 56.5 The fix: a batch-bound consumer keeps its slots (zero-core fac4a70)

**The rule** (docs/az.md 5.3): a consumer whose inference is batched on CUDA / MPS (run setting
`selfplay_remote_batch` 'auto', the default; 'local', 'remote', 'all', 'none' choose explicitly)
has the cap

```
cap = clamp(ceil(max(inflight x share, min(slots, batch_inflight x share))), lo, hi)      share = rate x (lead + P)
```

`batch_inflight` = run setting `selfplay_remote_batch_inflight` (default 2.0; 1 = as the others).
By Little's law a consumer's in-flight over its rate is its games' latency, so `batch_inflight x
share` is the in-flight at which its games last `batch_inflight` horizons: the desktop holds its
slots while its games finish within 2 iterations, and a batch-bound consumer too slow for that even
at its floor falls to `lo` like any other (no GPU fills the data with stale rows). `slots` = its
driver's `conc` (a co-training resolver driver's `hi` adds a queue beyond its slots, where a match
only waits; the rule never fills it). A consumer that is not batch-bound - the Mac's CPU workers -
keeps the throughput share exactly, and a run without a remote is untouched.

**Why this one.** The task's two options were a floor sized for efficient batches, or letting a
consumer whose rate rises with its cap grow toward its slots while the staleness stays within ~1
iteration. This is both: the floor is the slots the run's `conc` sized for the GPU (`conc / groups`
games per batch), and `batch_inflight` is the staleness guard - one line of the caps' model, with
the consumer's kind from its device. Rejected: a fixed floor (no guard against a consumer too slow
for the iterations); the stopped agent's draft (`wip/shared-queue-capfix` e2a4672, unverified, kept
for reference): a per-consumer latency controller with an elasticity estimated from phases at
different caps, six new constants and another model for the CPU workers too - noisy when the games'
length changes between iterations (as delver1's did, 56.4), able to learn the curve only by moving
the cap, and changing the throughput-bound workers' caps, which were right. **The cost**: the
desktop's rows may lag up to 2 checkpoints instead of ~1 (at its slots its games are ~1.15 phases,
56.10); with it ~20% of the data, the run's mean lag moves by a few hundredths.

**Simulated** (zero-core `tests/test_workqueue.py`, delver1's consumers: the desktop's games
180-200 s at any in-flight, each Mac worker 1.85 games/s at any in-flight, 800 games): the cap of
213a9c0 settles at 111-116 of 192 whether it starts at 75 or 181, the desktop at ~0.6 games/s;
batch-bound it is at 192 one phase later and stays, at 0.96 games/s (1.6x), its games 1.14 phases,
the phase 191 -> 175 s; the Mac workers' caps stay one phase of their throughput. A batch-bound
worker whose games take 1,400 s against ~200-s phases falls to its floor.

### 56.6 Choosing `games` for a run

* **`games` is the total of both machines per iteration** (56.2): the same data per iteration with
  or without the Mac; the Mac makes it sooner.
* **The batch-bound desktop keeps its slots while it plays at least `slots / batch_inflight` games
  an iteration** (its latency in phases is its in-flight over its games per phase): `games >= slots
  / (batch_inflight x its share of the throughput)`. delver1: 192 / (2 x ~0.2) ~ 480, so its 800
  leave a margin of ~1.7x; below that the desktop holds fewer than its slots (twice its share: still
  not the spiral). A Mac back-off only raises the desktop's share.
* **The staleness does not depend on `games`** (the caps scale with the phase: ~0.6 mean lag at 800
  as at 600). What `games` sets is the iteration's length - checkpoints per hour against the data
  each is trained on - and the window's depth: delver1's 20 GB hold ~296k samples, ~6 iterations of
  800 games (~46k samples each at today's ~220-260 decisions a game).
* **A co-training run's units are its events' matches**; its `games` stays the primary's event quota.

**The stragglers** (lag 3-5: 0.9% of delver1's rows, 56.4) are the long tail of game length - a game
three times the mean outlasts three phases whatever its consumer's cap - on both machines alike. A
cap (dropping or down-weighting rows older than N checkpoints) would touch the training window's
path (net_data) or need a weight column; at 0.9% of the rows, whose value targets are still the
games' real outcomes, it is not worth it now: not done.

### 56.11 Limits and open questions

* **`inflight` 1 sizes the mean game to one iteration**: 6.7% of delver1's rows are 2 checkpoints
  behind, 0.9% 3-5 (the long games, 56.6); `selfplay_remote_inflight` 0.5-0.75 makes it strict at
  some throughput. The caps follow the rates a phase late (an EWMA); a remote that starts unmeasured
  plays at a quarter of its guessed share for one phase.
* **Batch-bound is the device's word**, not measured: a CUDA consumer that is in fact
  throughput-bound (a GPU saturated below its slots) would hold up to twice its share in flight for
  nothing (the toy's CPU driver forced batch-bound: mean lag 0.41-0.65 against 0.29-0.44);
  `selfplay_remote_batch 'none'` or `selfplay_remote_batch_inflight 1` turns it off.
* **The Mac's workers lost 10-15% of their leaves/s** at their caps (4 groups of ~85 games): 2
  groups might win it back; not measured (no ssh jobs on the Mac from this branch's session).
* **A back-off is seen at a worker's next status line** (it checks its locks in a phase only): the
  first seconds of a phase count it as taking work.
* **A shard lost after the phase** (late past `selfplay_remote_wait`, a failed copy) leaves the
  iteration short by its games (`short` in the metrics, logged); a worker dying mid-phase is
  covered (its accepted games are played again here).
* **Linger** is single-switch for both modes, measured on the toy only; on delver1 it would turn the
  Mac's ~65 s of training-time idling into ~250 games of the next iteration at lag 1.
* **Co-training with a CUDA resolver and the Mac** is tested on the toy and the CPU (56.7, 56.8)
  only; 56.9 has the commands.
* **An engine panic in the delver mirror** (found by dv_local's worker, 56.8; not the queue's):
  `Game::stack_action` asserts that a stack item's slot is below `STACK_N` (32,
  engine/src/decision.rs:373), and a stack of 39+ items with a target below slot 31 panicked the
  worker's search (`stack slot 38 out of range`, game 348 of setup "8883:348", driver seed
  7777778, the network of iteration 3 of a `delver-smoke` run). The queue handled it (the worker's
  accepted games played here, the quota exact, the worker restarted); on delver1 a Mac worker would
  do the same, while a panic in the desktop's driver fails the run (its supervisor restarts it). Not
  in delver1's log so far, not in the 4 x 400-game search smoke; not fixed here (an engine change,
  its own tier).
* **Not reproducible**, as 52.8 (more so: which games the quota accepts first depends on timing).

## 57. The evaluation move rule: completed Q instead of visit counts; Elo against recent iterations (delver1)

`runs/delver1` (54.9) evaluates at `eval_sims` 32, where the prior's favourite collects most of the
visits even where the search found it worse, so "the most visited option" mostly plays the prior.
An experiment (zero-core branch `exp/select-rule`, this repo's `exp/select-rule` 102083d,
`tools/exp_select.py`; zero-core docs/az.md 12.1) found that choosing the evaluation move by the
**completed-Q improved policy** - the argmax of the 'cq' training target's logits, Gumbel AlphaZero's
final-move rule - won 57-61% against the heuristic where visit counts won 42-52%. The user's
decision (2026-10-28): an opt-in rule, today's the default everywhere; delver1's evaluation switches
at its next re-pin; self-play later, by a forked A/B run. With it, two changes to delver1's Elo: its
checkpoints play the ones 1, 2, 4 and 8 iterations back instead of 8 and 16, and no more games
against the random bot (won 98-100% since iteration 8: no information).

### 57.1 What was built (zero-core `feat/select-rule`, on main as `feat/select-rule-on-queue`)

zero-core docs/search.md 3.3 (the rule in the driver), docs/az.md 5.4 (the settings, the pools) and
12 (the experiment, the checks). Run settings, every default today's behaviour bit for bit:

| Setting | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `eval_select`, `eval_select_min_visits` | visits, 0 | every evaluation seat's move: 'visits' = argmax (N, P0); 'cq' = argmax of ln P0 + (c_visit + max N) c_scale completedQ (`cq_c_visit`, `cq_c_scale`: 50, 1) among the options with at least `eval_select_min_visits` visits (when none has that many, the most visited ones). The yardstick, random and Elo matches, here or on the `eval_remote` (its config is the run's), co-training's evaluations; `mtgz.az.h2h` / `mtgz.az.replays` take a checkpoint's run's rule unless `--select` says otherwise |
| `selfplay_select`, `selfplay_select_min_visits` | visits, 0 | the same for self-play's moves after `temp_moves` (the recorded targets stay `policy_target`'s); for a forked A/B, not delver1's re-pin |
| `elo_offsets` | '' | '1,2,4,8': each evaluated checkpoint k plays k-1, k-2, k-4, k-8 (raw iterations: every iteration writes a checkpoint) whatever `eval_every`; `elo_opponents` unused. '' = the evaluations-back offsets (with `eval_every` 8 and `elo_opponents` 2: k-8, k-16) |
| `eval_random_games` | 50 (delver1) | 0 now works without random rows anywhere (Elo, dashboards, the remote) |

* **One Elo pool per rule.** A checkpoint that moves by another rule is another player: 'visits'
  keeps `elo/` (delver1's whole history), another rule gets `elo/<rule>/` (`cq`, `cq-n4`: the
  guard; results.json + `select`, `since`). A pool takes only its rule's evaluations (each
  evaluation and Elo row records `select`, absent = 'visits'), so a run that changes its rule at a
  restart leaves `elo/` byte for byte as it was; the new pool begins at its first evaluation
  (`since`) and replays no history.
* **Checkpoints rated through Elo matches only** (the raw offsets' never-evaluated opponents; a pool
  begun mid-run's older opponents) carry `"evaluated": false` in the pool's ratings.json and in
  models/index.json and are never `best.pt` nor either dashboard's best.
* **The remote** plays the run's rule (the mirror's config.json), owns its pool (copied back) and
  ships the raw offsets' checkpoints; a result naming another rule (a Mac checkout without the
  rule) is refused before anything is recorded and retried as a failure.
* **The dashboards** (`mtgz.az.dashboard`, zerodash) read the current rule's pool; `mtgz.az.dashboard`
  draws the other pools as their own lines (one chart, never one fit).
* In this repo: nothing game-specific - the pin, `engine/tests/draft_deferred.rs` (DriverCfg's new
  `move_log` field), and `tools/select_eval.py` (57.2).

### 57.2 Measured on the production path (`tools/select_eval.py`)

`python tools/select_eval.py --run runs/delver1 --iter K --rules visits,cq,cq-n2,cq-n4 --games 200
--out E:/exp-select2` evaluates a copy of checkpoint K with `Run.evaluate` - the code a run and its
`eval_remote` run - once per rule on a scratch mirror (the run's settings, the rule, 200 games
against the heuristic, no random games, CPU, 6 search threads; the run directory only read). Every
rule plays the run's seeds (`7919 x K + 1`), so game g has the same deal under every rule (paired).
Results (`E:/exp-select2/select_eval.jsonl`, 2026-10-28):

| Checkpoint | visits | cq | cq, >= 2 visits | cq, >= 4 visits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| delver1 iter 12 | 46.0% | **61.5%** | - | - |
| iter 26 | 71.0% | 77.0% | **77.5%** | 76.5% |
| iter 27 | 71.0% | 73.0% | 73.5% | **76.5%** |

| Paired against visits (score points, +- 1 se) | iter 12 | iter 26 | iter 27 | 26 + 27 (400 games) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cq | +15.5 +- 4.9 | +6.0 +- 3.7 | +2.0 +- 3.6 | +4.0 +- 2.6 |
| cq-n2 | - | +6.5 +- 3.7 | +2.5 +- 3.6 | +4.5 +- 2.6 |
| cq-n4 | - | +5.5 +- 3.8 | +5.5 +- 3.2 | +5.5 +- 2.5 |

Between the guards (26 + 27, paired): cq -> cq-n2 +0.5 +- 1.4, cq -> cq-n4 +1.5 +- 2.0, cq-n2 ->
cq-n4 +1.0 +- 1.8. Head to head, iteration 27 against itself (`zero.h2h`-style, cq vs visits, 200
games, 32 simulations): **51.0 +- 3.5%** (+7 Elo). Games under 'cq' were a little shorter (15.4-16.4
rounds against 16.8-17.2).

**The gain shrinks as the network improves**: +15.5 points at iteration 12, +2 to +6 at 26-27, and
nothing measurable head to head at 27. The rule fixes a weak network's habit of playing its prior at
32 simulations; as the prior and the search agree more, there is less to fix. It costs nothing
(the search is the same; the moves are chosen from the same root statistics).

### 57.3 Which guard: 4 visits

None of the guards differs significantly from another (57.2). `eval_select_min_visits` 4 is the
recommendation: it has the best pooled estimate against visits (+5.5 +- 2.5, the only rule more than
2 se above it) and the most one-sided paired record (iteration 27: 26 games better, 15 worse,
against 28 / 23 for cq-n2); and it is the least noise-prone choice by construction - at 32
simulations an option's Q from one or two visits is one or two leaf values, and the rule's scale
((50 + max N) x Q, ~70 Q) lets a Q lucky by 0.03 outweigh an 8-fold prior; with 4 visits Q is an
average of four. Without a guard an unvisited option, completed at v_mix, can even be chosen. The
guard keeps the rule's intent (Q overrules the prior's favourite among the options the search
looked at) and drops its noisiest picks; its rule name, and the pool, is `cq-n4`.

### 57.4 Elo against recent iterations, and the Mac's evaluation time

With `eval_every` 8 and `elo_opponents` 2, delver1's checkpoint k played k-8 and k-16 only; at
`elo_offsets` '1,2,4,8' it plays k-1, k-2, k-4 and k-8 - the recent progress, from checkpoints that
exist anyway (k-1, k-2, k-4 rated through these games only: "evaluated": false). The random bot's
50 games go (`eval_random_games` 0); the reference games (random vs the heuristic, bots only) are
played once in the new pool.

`tools/select_eval.py --run runs/delver1 --iter 24 --elo-timing` timed the two Elo settings on the
desktop's CPU (6 threads, both at 'cq', the yardstick games left out - the same 100 in both):

| | games | random phase | Elo phase | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| today: 50 random; Elo vs 16, 8 at 20 games | 50 + 40 | 144.5 s | 222.2 s | 366.7 s |
| re-pin: no random; Elo vs 23, 22, 20, 16 at 25 games | 0 + 100 | 0 | 427.7 s | 427.7 s |

With the yardstick's 100 games (~180-280 s on that CPU, from 57.2's timings) an evaluation goes from
~550-650 s to ~610-710 s: **+10-11%** (+61 s). The Mac's evaluations took 193-384 s (evals.jsonl,
iterations 1-56; 193 s at 56): expected ~210-420 s, about the same, once every 8 iterations (~30
minutes). Once, at the switch: the 100 reference games and the uploads of the raw offsets'
checkpoints the mirror lacks (k-1, k-2, k-4 of every evaluated k so far: ~20 files of 6 MB at
iteration 64). `--elo-games 20` (80 Elo games) would keep the time equal (the Elo phase ~3.4 s a
game here past a fixed ~85 s); 25 is the user's choice.

## 58. The action layout's slot limits, and the public-state encoding gate

Branch `public-state` (from main 5c18d35), two parts: an engine fix for a panic remote self-play
found (58.1-58.5, tier "engine rules/cards", commit 78c9e89), and a standing gate that proves public
state reaches the network's input, with the gaps it found fixed in layout v4's spare floats
(58.6-58.12, tier "encoding-only", commit 835f5b3). **Layout v4 is unchanged** (33,652 floats,
`mtgz/az/layout_v4.json` as it was, the action ids as they were): checkpoints of every v4 run load
as they are (58.11). (57 is another branch's.)

### 58.1 Stack targets in reach (the panic of 56.11)

dv_local's remote worker died in iteration 4 of a `delver-smoke` run (56.8) on `search worker
panicked: stack slot 38 out of range`, game 348 of the queued setup "8883:348", driver seed
7777778, the network of iteration 3 (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/shared-queue2/mirror/dv_local/w00.log`):
`Game::stack_action` asserts that a stack item's `STACK` slot is below `STACK_N` (32), and a
decision offered a target 38 items deep. The Delver mirror builds tall stacks (Cori-Steel Cutter's
flurry triggers, the Monk tokens' prowess, Baubles' draws, counterspells answering counterspells),
and a tiny network's play reaches 39+ items; any decision that names a stack item that deep panics
(a Counterspell, Force of Will, Tishana's Tidebinder's trigger, a copy's new target), and so does
a cube storm count with a counterspell. The game was not reproduced (56.11: which games the shared
queue accepts first depends on timing, and the search's choices on the network's batches); the
same panic is reproduced deterministically by constructed states (58.5): on main 3 of the 7 engine
tests panic with `stack slot 32 out of range`.

**The rule** (class B, docs/shortcuts.md 58.1): a spell's or an ability's target may be one of
the **31 stack items below it**; the deeper (older) items of a taller stack can't be targeted.
Targets are chosen with their spell or ability already on the stack (CR 601.2a-c, 602.2a-b, 603.3d),
on top, so the 32 `STACK` slots name it and 31 items below it. Keeping the newest items in reach is
the rules-safest cut: a response is nearly always about what was just put on the stack, and the
alternative (no spell or trigger once the stack holds 32 items) would change far more games.

`Game::stack_in_reach` is the one list of stack items a target may be (spells and abilities, top
first, the top 31 not counting the item whose targets are chosen); `target_candidates` and
`has_candidates` both read it, so every decision that names a stack item (`Target` for a spell, an
activated or a triggered ability; the modes' availability, `ChooseModes`; an activated ability's X
for "X targets"; `NewTarget` for a copy) and every check before an item is put on the stack (a
cast's or an activation's `targets_available`, `distinct_choosable`, a trigger's 603.3d check)
agree. `Game::targeting` (a transient, 0 between tasks) is the item whose targets, modes or X are
chosen while it is on the stack: it is not counted; a check before the item is put on the stack
counts every item, and the item then goes on top: the same items are in reach, so "a cast is
offered only if it can be completed" holds (section 6; the fuzzer's option completion). A
copy's current target beyond reach is kept by `PASS`; a target chosen earlier that sinks deeper
stays legal on resolution (608.2b reads no slot).

### 58.2 96 permanents a player

`Game::perm_action` asserts a permanent's `MY_PERM` / `OPP_PERM` slot below `PERM_N` (96). The
token cap (`token_count`, 26.11.6, 30) kept that for tokens with room for every card the player
owns to enter too (`perm_reserve`: their cards elsewhere or controlled by another player). Three
paths went around it: gaining control of another player's permanent (`change_control`: Dack
Fayden's -2, Thieving Skydiver, Dack's emblem, giving one away), another player's card entering
under a player's control (Reanimate, Animate Dead, Necromancy on an opponent's graveyard; a stolen
spell resolving: `GainControlOfSpell`), and a copy of a permanent spell, which becomes a token
(CR 707.10, 111.1: Sage of the Skies copies itself). Each needs a player at 96 less their reserve
permanents (a full token board, then a steal): never seen, but legal.

Now (class B, docs/shortcuts.md 26.11.6 extended): `Game::perm_room(p)` = 96 less `p`'s permanents
and reserve (the token cap's accounting, which `token_count` now shares). With no room, gaining
control of a permanent `p` doesn't own does nothing (`change_control`; an exchange of control keeps
both counts and is unchecked: `set_control`), another player's card enters under its owner's
control (its owner's reserve holds the room), and a token or a copy ceases to exist instead of
entering (`put_onto_battlefield_attached`, as a token beyond the cap is never created). Below the
limit nothing changes. Left as it was: cards in no zone (a revealed companion outside the game, a
Mox Diamond set aside) are not in the token cap's reserve, so with every other card of a player on
their battlefield they could still exceed it by one each; the assert stays (loud).

### 58.3 The deck limit counts a companion

The engine plays at most 64 cards a player in the game (`constructed::MAX_DECK`: a hand, a library
list and a graveyard have 64 action slots, 54.4). `constructed::check` refused a larger
constructed deck but not a 64-card deck with a companion (103.2b, 116.2g: a 65th card can join the
game), and limited lists were not checked at all (CR 100.2a has no maximum).
`constructed::check_size` (deck + 1 with a companion in the sideboard, at most 64) now checks every
decklist an `mtg` spec gives (constructed, limited lists with or without sideboards, drafted
seats); the random, evaluation and drafted decks have 40 cards (class B, docs/shortcuts.md 58.3).

### 58.6 The public-state encoding gate

The hidden-information checks (section 10, 36.11, 55.4) prove that worlds differing only in
hidden things encode identically; nothing proved that public things get into the encoding, and
55.1's declared mulligan passed every gate while missing from it. The dual check:

1. **Classification** (`engine/src/public_state.rs`, `fields`): every field of the structs that
   hold a game's state (`Game`, `Player`, `Obj`, `Turn`, `StackItem`, `ManaPool`, `Dungeon` and the
   match's `MatchState`) is listed by a destructuring without `..` (the `classify!` macro, as
   `lower/` does for the IR): a new field is a compile error there until it is classified
   **public** (it needs a perturbation), **hidden** (the hidden-information checks cover it) or
   **derived** (internal, a cache, a transient clear at every decision, the settings, a container
   whose elements are classified on their own; exempt with a one-line reason).
2. **Perturbations** (`perturbations`): for each public field one or more small changes of a
   position's clone, made by hand on the state, never through the rules (whose events and
   triggers would change other things too: a creature put into a graveyard by hand, not
   destroyed): life + 1, a counter of each kind, tap or untap, a card from a graveyard to exile,
   another step, a continuous effect of each kind on a permanent, a stack item's X, a match's
   game won, ... 140 in all.
3. **The test** (`tests/az.rs`, `public_state_reaches_the_encoding`): 240 positions (60 each: the
   cube's random decks, the Delver mirror, best-of-three matches, a drafted 2v2 `team_draft`
   match), mid-game (turn 2 or later, about one decision in 40, sideboarding left out), mixed
   heuristic and random play. Every perturbation on a clone of each position must change the view
   (`Game::view_of` and `public_state::match_view`) for both players (the change is public) and
   the encoding (`MtgAz::encode`: `encode_features` and the match block) for both viewers (it
   reaches the network), but for the listed limits; a perturbation that never applies fails unless
   it is marked rare (positions of random games seldom have what it needs: a prepared permanent,
   divided damage, a ninjutsu attack, a splice). It prints one line per perturbation (applied,
   view unchanged, encoding unchanged per viewer, the first example) and runs in 1.1 s (release;
   `AZ_SCALE=k` for k times the positions). `public_state_classification` prints the table, and the
   module's unit test checks that every public field has a perturbation, every perturbation names a
   public field and every limit a perturbation.
4. **Limits** (`limits`): the perturbations whose change the encoding leaves out, each with its
   reason: by design (58.9), or a gap with no spare float left in layout v4 (58.10). Anything else
   that fails is a finding.

### 58.7 The classification

211 fields: **116 public, 7 hidden, 88 derived**; 140 perturbations.

| Struct | Fields | Public | Hidden | Derived | Perturbations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Game` | 95 | 23 | 3 (`rng`, `face_down_ids`, `clouds`) | 69 | 47 |
| `Player` | 35 | 33 | 0 | 2 (`pool`: a container; `last_turn`: the turn number, who is active and the extra turns give it) | 33 |
| `Obj` | 28 | 21 | 1 (`known`) | 6 (`zone`: the zone lists' mirror; `inc`; `deathtouched`, a transient; `lki_power`; `pw_extra`; `flips`) | 21 |
| `Turn` | 10 | 9 | 0 | 1 (`cleanup_again`) | 9 |
| `StackItem` | 20 | 16 | 0 | 4 (`id`, `delve_floor`, `discarded_land`, `flips`) | 16 |
| `ManaPool` | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| `Dungeon` | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| `MatchState` | 17 | 8 | 3 (`pools`: what the other player knows of a pool is the `OPP_POOL` bag; `rng`; `priors`) | 6 (`gspec`, `decks`: sizes in the match block, cards in the zones; `turns_before`, `over`, `seen`: `earlier` between games; `sb`: `encode_sideboarding`) | 8 |

`Game`'s 69 derived fields: the containers (`objs`, `players`, `stack`, `turn`, `dungeons`), the
engine's continuation (`agenda`; `pending`, computed from it: its kind and decider are the context
block's, its options the decider's), the settings (`db`, `spec`: the one that varies, the turn cap,
is the turns left `g[19]`; `known_pools`), fast paths and caches (`tokens`, `first_token`,
`any_loss`, `n_static`, `n_self_types`, `seen`, `copy_objs`), counters (`next_ts`,
`next_stack_id`, `decisions`), event bookkeeping (`ev_seq`, `batch_fired`, `group_ts`), last known
information (`leaving`, `lki_counters`, `lki_copy`, `lki_damage`, `spell_lki`), the engine loop
caps' counters (`may_copies`, `activations`: no rule reads them), the search's (`observer`, `keys`,
`forced`, `forced_at`, `no_auto`), `rules_srcs`, `log`, and 33 transients set and cleared around
one move or one decision (`entering_*`, `batching`, `answer`, `combat_dmg`, `route_choice`, ...,
`choosing_for`, `targeting`).

### 58.8 Findings fixed

The first run (on this branch's 78c9e89, `Game::view_of` and the encoding as main's) reported **65
findings**: 37 view gaps (public fields `Game::view_of` left out) and 27 encoding gaps the view
showed, and one perturbation never applied (`ManaPool::haste`, now rare); 3 were the perturbations'
own (a base 7/7 set on a 7/7 creature, a colour chosen again, an effect whose end changes nothing:
now skipped).

**The view.** `Game::view_of` (testkit: what the hidden-information checks compare across worlds;
no behaviour reads it) now has every public field: the turn's normal player, additional combats
and the extra turns; the marks (by the object's place); a player's pool tags, losses, turns begun,
revolt, this turn's draws and spells, life gained, energy, Yawgmoth's Will, graveyard exile, the
city's blessing, protection from everything and the companion's card; a permanent's control since,
what it blocks, first-strike damage, evoked, flashback; a stack item's costs (additional,
alternative), where it was cast from, delve, X, the division, splices, a ninjutsu attack, a
trigger's event and noted permanents (objects by place, stack items by position). The fuzzer's
`determinize` checks compare these too (58.11).

**The encoding**, in the spare floats of layout v4 (no width, offset, segment or identity changed;
every other feature's meaning and offset as main's):

| Float | Feature | Why (cube and Delver cards) |
|---|---|---|
| `g[127]` (`glob::MONARCH`) | the monarch: 1 the viewer, -1 the opponent, 0 none (CR 724) | Palace Jailer, Aragorn, Okoye, Forth Eorlingas! |
| match block 27-28 (`mtch::SPELLS`) | spells cast this turn / 4 (squashed), the viewer's, the opponent's | Cori-Steel Cutter's flurry ("your second spell each turn": the Delver mirror's engine), prowess, Sage of the Skies, storm |
| match block 29-30 (`mtch::ENERGY`) | energy counters / 4 (squashed), per player (CR 122.1) | Galvanic Discharge, Guide of Souls |
| permanent status 91, 92 (`perm::CANT_BLOCK`, `CANT_BE_BLOCKED`) | it can't block, it can't be blocked (`Game::flags_of`: effects and statics) | Aragorn, Headliner Scarlett, Zirda; Kappa Cannoneer, Manifold Key |
| permanent status 93 (`perm::OTHER_COUNTERS`) | its counters other than +1/+1, -1/-1, loyalty and lore / 4 (stun, keyword, named: charge, oil, ...; squashed) | Cryogen Relic's and Kaito's stun counters, charge counters |
| permanent status 94 (`perm::EXILED_WITH`) | the cards exiled with it / 4 (`Game::links`, face up: they return when it leaves, CR 610.3) | Portable Hole, Leyline Binding, Palace Jailer |
| permanent status 95 (`perm::PROTECTED`) | it has protection from something (printed or from an effect, CR 702.16; a summary) | Giver of Runes, True-Name Nemesis |
| stack status 31 (`stack::X`) | X / 8 (squashed, CR 107.3a) | 15 cube cards: Walking Ballista, Green Sun's Zenith, ... |
| a permanent's descriptor, card types and colours (code 32-37, 38-42) | as they are (layers 4 and 5, `types_of`, `colors_of`, a copy's exceptions included), not its card's | an animated land is a creature; Painter's Servant's colour; "becomes an artifact" |

Free in layout v4 now: the context block's 246-255 (the decision's, kept for decisions, 55.2) and
the match block's 31 (the match's). The match block's 27-30 hold game facts: the token network
reads the globals and the match block as one input (`TokenNet.g`, 160 inputs), so they are globals
to the network; `Game::encode_features` writes them, `encode_match` the match's floats, and
sideboarding's encoding leaves them 0. The fixes were chosen by the cards that use each fact (the
Delver mirror's first); the rest is 58.10. `the_public_state_fixes_are_encoded` (`tests/az.rs`)
reads each new float back for both viewers (Palace Jailer's monarch and exiled creature, spells cast,
Walking Ballista's X on the stack, stun counters, True-Name Nemesis's protection, Galvanic
Discharge's energy). After the fixes the gate reports **93 perturbations encoded**, 4 deliberate
limits, 42 gaps for layout v5 (4 of them rare, never applied) and one rare public field never
applied (`Game::prepared`).

### 58.9 Deliberate limits

The perturbations whose change the encoding leaves out by design (`LimitKind::Design`):

* **Bag order**: two graveyard cards swapping places (graveyards are bags of identities, 22.2; the
  order matters to a few cards). **A gap since section 65**: a `GRAVEYARD` id is a graveyard
  position, so the order is what those ids mean (`LimitKind::NextLayout`).
* **What the opponent knows of the viewer's own cards**, outside the hand (where `HAND` status 4
  shows it): a card of the viewer's exiled face down is in its exile bag by identity like a face-up
  one, and the viewer's own reveals in earlier games of a match are not encoded for it (the
  opponent's are `OPP_REVEALED`).
* **The turn a permanent entered**: `NEW` is "under its controller's control since this turn" (CR
  302.6); the turn it entered differs from that only after a control change and is read by two
  cards.

And the limits the perturbations respect by construction (they change objects in the encoded slots
only): 32 permanent slots a side (a bag and the globals' counts for the rest), 8 stack slots (the
stack's size `g[20]` for the rest), 16 hand slots (the hand bag), 4 trigger slots, 4
graveyard-ability slots; numbers exact within +-128 then squashed (46); summaries where a slot has
one float (protection's qualities, other counters' kinds).

### 58.10 Gaps for layout v5 (encoded by layout v5: section 60)

42 gaps need room layout v4 doesn't have (`LimitKind::V5`; each with its reason in
`public_state::limits`). Grouped by where a v5 would put them:

* **Per-player globals** (none left): cards drawn this turn and in the draw step (Orcish
  Bowmasters), noncreature spells cast this turn, life gained this turn, can't gain life, creatures
  that attacked this turn (raid), spells cast this game, Yawgmoth's Will this turn, graveyard exile
  this turn, the city's blessing, protection from everything (The One Ring), the pool's
  artifact-only and haste mana, delayed triggers waiting (Mana Drain's mana, Sneak Attack's
  sacrifice, Flickerwisp's return, a Bauble's draw), cards they may play from exile (impulse draw,
  Urza, Fallen Shinobi, Dauthi Voidwalker; the holder sees them as `EXILE` options when it decides).
* **Globals**: the extra-turn order (`Turn::normal`), additional combat phases.
* **Per permanent** (status 91-95 used): must attack (Mod::MustAttack), exiled if it would die,
  subtypes an effect adds, evoked, escaped, the player chosen as it entered (True-Name Nemesis,
  Dauthi Voidwalker), monstrous, exhausted, the colour chosen as it entered, exerted, abilities
  resolved this turn, once-each-turn actions done.
* **Per stack item** (status 31 holds X): which modes were chosen (their count and the targets are
  encoded), the alternative cost (evoke: an evoked Solitude, dash, Force of Will's pitch), how and
  from where it was cast (flashback, a graveyard: exiled as it leaves), cards exiled for delve
  (Murktide Regent's counters), a triggered ability's event amount, noted permanents, divided
  damage, a ninjutsu attack, splices.
* **Graveyards**: cards discarded this turn (mayhem).

(Done since: layout v5, section 60, encodes all 42 with v4 kept as it is, so a v4 network widens onto
it exactly instead of starting fresh.)

**Recommendation.** No v5 now: the Delver mirror's most relevant facts are in v4's spare floats,
and a v5 means a fresh start for every run (never resume across a layout change). When a v5 comes
for another reason, add: a second per-player block of 24 globals (the per-player items above), 2
globals, 16 more permanent status floats (the per-permanent items, the colour chosen as a one-hot),
8 more stack status floats (the chosen modes as a bitmask, the alternative cost, cast from, delved
instants and sorceries, the event amount), and an exile segment (the cards a player may play from
exile, with their permission), then fold this gate's 42 v5 limits into fixes. Until then the
context block's 246-255 could take up to 10 more game floats at the cost of the decision's room
(55.2); not done.

### 58.12 Runs

Both parts keep layout v4, the action ids and the shards' width, so a running v4 run can **re-pin
onto this branch at an iteration boundary without a fresh start** (44.5, 53.4, as 55.6): its
checkpoints, optimiser state and window load as they are. The engine part changes behaviour only in
states with a stack taller than 32 items, a player at the 96-permanent limit or a 64-card deck
(none in the digests): a re-pin removes the panic of 56.11 from the desktop's driver and the Mac's
workers. The encoding part makes the network's input more complete: the window's older samples carry
0 where this build writes the new facts (spells cast this turn, energy, the monarch, X, the flags,
counters, links, protection) and printed card types and colours for animated or painted permanents;
those inputs were constant in training (their weights untrained, 58.11), so the old samples teach
nothing that contradicts the new ones, and the window rotates them out (delver1: 6 iterations). The
re-pin: this branch merged, a pinned worktree of the merged commit built (`bash tools/build_py.sh`),
`bash tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout`, the tier "re-pin" checks (digest equal to main's recorded
317b5ba05dc569fb, one smoke configuration on the run's spec), `touch runs/<run>/STOP` during an
iteration, then the supervisor's command from the new worktree; `runs/delver1` and the A/B runs are
the user's call (not done here).

## 59. The selection scale apart from the training scale (the Delver main line)

The 'cq' evaluation rule of section 57 chooses a move by the argmax of the 'cq' training target's
logits, `ln P0 + (c_visit + max N) c_scale completedQ`, and until now it read the run's own
`cq_c_scale`, the training target's scale. So one knob set both the training target and the move
rule. The overnight A/B series (`runs/ab/results.md`, 2026-10-28/29) showed what that costs:
experiment 2, `--cq-c-scale 0.3` forked from `ab1-valueq06` at iteration 72, won its head to head at
iteration 82 with **64.2 +- 2.4%** and became the main line (`runs/ab2-cqscale03`). But the fork
also *selected* its moves at 0.3 (`select_a` 'cq-n4-v50-s0.3') while the control selected at 1.0
(`select_b` 'cq-n4'). The same checkpoints with both sides at `--select visits` (400 games):
**49.0 +- 2.5%**, no training effect. The 64% came from selecting with cq at scale 0.3 instead of
1.0. The user's decision (2026-10-29): the selection scale and the training scale become two
settings, so a training A/B never silently changes the evaluation rule.

### 59.1 What was built (zero-core `feat/select-scale` c8110c1, on main 45885aa)

zero-core docs/az.md 1.2, 5.4 (the transform, the pools, what "unset" should mean) and 12.5 (the
build and the checks); docs/search.md 3.3. Run settings:

| Setting | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `eval_select_c_scale`, `eval_select_c_visit` | unset (null) | the evaluation 'cq' rule's own completed-Q transform; unset = `cq_c_scale` / `cq_c_visit` (the training target's: one knob, today's behaviour byte for byte). Every evaluation seat (the yardstick, Elo, the `eval_remote`, co-training's evaluations), and `mtgz.az.h2h` / `mtgz.az.replays` of the run's checkpoints. The rule 'cq' only; `none` on the command line unsets a saved value |
| `selfplay_select_c_scale`, `selfplay_select_c_visit` | unset (null) | the same for `selfplay_select` 'cq' (self-play after `temp_moves`); the recorded targets keep `cq_c_scale` / `cq_c_visit` whatever these are |

* **The pool follows the effective selection transform.** The rule's name (its evaluations'
  `select`, its Elo pool `elo/<rule>/`) carries the transform it actually selects with:
  `cq-n4-v50-s0.3` whether the 0.3 comes from `cq_c_scale` or from `eval_select_c_scale`, `cq-n4` at
  50 / 1. A run whose selection scale is pinned keeps its pool when only `cq_c_scale` changes; a run
  with it unset changes pool with `cq_c_scale`, as before.
* **The training targets never read the new settings**: in the Rust driver `Select::Cq` and
  `PolicyTarget::CompletedQ` already held their own transforms; the bindings' new seat keys
  `select_c_visit` / `select_c_scale` feed the first only.
* **`mtgz.az.h2h`** (zero.h2h): a checkpoint's run's rule now comes with its effective transform;
  `--cq-c-scale` / `--cq-c-visit` for both sides and, new, per side `--a-cq-c-scale`,
  `--b-cq-c-scale`, `--a-cq-c-visit`, `--b-cq-c-visit`. One checkpoint at two selection scales:

  ```
  python -m mtgz.az.h2h runs/ab2-cqscale03/models/iter_0120.pt runs/ab2-cqscale03/models/iter_0120.pt \
    --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3 --b-cq-c-scale 1.0 --sims 32 --games 400
  ```
  (`select_a` 'cq-n4-v50-s0.3', `select_b` 'cq-n4'). Without `--select` the per-side flags apply
  over each side's run rule; a transform for a 'visits' side is an error, as are both-sides flags
  when neither side plays 'cq' (before, `--cq-c-scale` without `--select` was silently ignored).
* **`mtgz.az.replays`**: the run's rule with its transform; `--cq-c-visit` / `--cq-c-scale`.
* In this repo: nothing game-specific, only the pin (c15a22d).

### 59.2 Defaults, and what "unset" should mean long-term

Unset follows `cq_c_scale` (today's behaviour) and stays the default for now: every existing run and
config evaluates, trains and names its pools bit for bit as before (59.4). The recommendation for
later (zero-core docs/az.md 5.4): **unset = a fixed transform** (50 / 1, or the value the selection
measurement settles on) instead of following the target. The two knobs act separately (the A/B
above: training at 0.3 changed nothing measurable, selecting at 0.3 instead of 1.0 was ~+100 Elo
head to head), and following turns every training A/B of `cq_c_scale` into an A/B of the
evaluation rule. Flipping the default needs one migration first: every run config with a 'cq' rule
and a `cq_c_*` other than the new default gets its current effective value written in (e.g.
`ab2-cqscale03`: `eval_select_c_scale` 0.3), so no run changes moves or pool. Until then: pin the
selection scale on every run whose `cq_c_scale` an A/B may change, and give both arms of such an A/B
the same `--eval-select-c-scale` (or read it with both sides at one `--select` and one
`--cq-c-scale`).

### 59.3 Giving the main line (`runs/ab2-cqscale03`) its own selection scale

Its training stays exactly as it is: `cq_c_scale` 0.3 (saved in its config.json since the fork), the
'cq' targets, `selfplay_select` 'visits' (no self-play scale to set: `--selfplay-select-c-scale`
would be an error with 'visits'). Only the evaluation's selection scale gets its own value S (the
user's choice from the running h2h measurement). Procedure as 56.10 / 57.5: zero-core
`feat/select-scale` and this branch merged, a pinned worktree of the merged commit built (`bash
tools/build_py.sh`; the engine is a6bb3bc's, so the tier is "re-pin onto an already-verified
commit": digest equal to main's recorded 317b5ba05dc569fb, one smoke configuration), `bash
tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout` from that worktree (the Mac's evaluation checkout must have the
setting: an older one selects at `cq_c_scale` and, when S is not 0.3, its results name another rule
and are refused, 57.1), `touch runs/ab2-cqscale03/STOP` during an iteration, then from the new
worktree the run's current command plus one flag:

```
python tools/launch_hidden.py "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2-cqscale03/supervisor_console.txt" \
  python tools/supervise.py "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2-cqscale03" --preset delver-mirror --seed 1 \
  --eval-remote mac --selfplay-remote mac --games 800 --conc 192 --ram-budget-gb 20 --selfplay-remote-linger 1 \
  --eval-select cq --eval-select-min-visits 4 --eval-random-games 0 --elo-offsets 1,2,4,8 --elo-games 25 \
  --window-cache 1 --train-prefetch 2 --iters 400 --eval-every 8 \
  --eval-select-c-scale S
```

(`--eval-select-c-visit` stays unset: 50, the run's `cq_c_visit`.) What happens at the next
evaluated iteration K (a multiple of 8):

* **S = 0.3**: nothing changes - the same moves, the same pool `elo/cq-n4-v50-s0.3/` (since 72), the
  same files (59.4's cq-rule run: byte for byte). The scale is then pinned: a later training A/B of
  `cq_c_scale` forked from this run keeps selecting at 0.3.
* **S = 1.0**: the evaluations select at 1.0 and begin the pool `elo/cq-n4/` (since K: the reference
  games once, K's yardstick games, its raw-offset Elo matches; 57.5).
* **another S**: likewise, the pool `elo/cq-n4-v50-s<S>/` (e.g. `cq-n4-v50-s0.1`).

What to check: the log's `iter K vs heuristic (remote mac, ...): {... 'select': '<rule>'}` and `iter K
elo ... (pool <rule>) (remote mac)`; evals.jsonl's row K with `"select": "<rule>"`; the pool directory;
the next iteration's `selfplay` / `train` rows as before (the training is untouched: same targets,
same `cq_c_scale`); `watch_run`. A new pool's Elo is not comparable with the old pool's; the
yardstick's win rate is the continuous series. **The delverai publisher** (`tools/delverai_publish.py`)
reads the pool through `zero.elo` of its own checkout: on a core without this change it would compute
the old rule's name (from `cq_c_scale`) and keep reading `cq-n4-v50-s0.3` once S is not 0.3; its
checkout needs the new pin too (or its settings list `SETTINGS` the new key, for the page).

### 59.5 Limits

* **Unset still follows** `cq_c_scale` (59.2): an A/B of `cq_c_scale` on a run without a pinned
