## 60. Layout v5: the gate's 42 gaps encoded, and a v4 network widened onto it exactly

Branch `layout-v5` (from main 6c27a9b), with zero-core `feat/token-widen` (f606724 and its docs
f3f5535, on main c8110c1), pinned here at f3f5535. Tier: an encoding change plus a zero-core network
change (60.6). 58.10 left 42 public facts that layout v4 had no room for and recommended a v5 only
"for another reason", because a new layout meant a fresh start for every run. It no longer does:
**layout v5 is layout v4 with additions only**, and zero-core's `widen` now follows such a layout
change exactly, so a v4 network becomes a v5 network that computes what it computed (60.2). A run
still never resumes across a layout change: it forks into a new run directory whose iteration 0 is
its widened checkpoint (60.5). (59 is the selection scale's.)

### 60.1 The layout

Every v4 float keeps its index within its block and its meaning; blocks after a wider one move.

| Block | v4 offset | v4 floats | v5 offset | v5 floats | Added |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| globals | 0 | 128 | 0 | 128 | |
| context | 128 | 256 | 128 | 256 | |
| bags | 384 | 17 x 1024 | 384 | 19 x 1024 | rows 17-18: the exiled cards the viewer may play, those the opponent may play |
| tops | 17,792 | 6 x 54 | 19,840 | 6 x 54 | |
| my permanents | 18,116 | 32 x 148 | 20,164 | 32 x 172 | status 96-119 (16 used, 8 spare) |
| opponent permanents | 22,852 | 32 x 148 | 25,668 | 32 x 172 | the same |
| hand | 27,588 | 16 x 60 | 31,172 | 16 x 60 | |
| stack | 28,548 | 8 x 84 | 32,132 | 8 x 124 | status 32-71 (32 used, 8 spare) |
| triggers | 29,220 | 4 x 56 | 33,124 | 4 x 56 | |
| list | 29,444 | 64 x 60 | 33,348 | 64 x 60 | |
| graveyard abilities | 33,284 | 4 x 56 | 37,188 | 4 x 56 | |
| companions | 33,508 | 2 x 56 | 37,412 | 2 x 56 | |
| match | 33,620 | 32 | 37,524 | 32 | |
| globals v5 | | | 37,556 | 64 | per player 24 (16 used; 22 since section 72), the game's 16 (2 used) |
| **total** | | **33,652** | | **37,620** | +3,968 (bags 2,048, permanents 1,536, stack 320, globals 64) |

The same 11 segments in the same order with the same slot counts, present flags, identities (card
codes) and action ids: the token network has the same 170 token positions and pointer columns. A
128 x 4 network grows from 1,500,317 to 1,552,797 parameters (the input maps: permanents 2 x 24 x
128, stack 40 x 128, bags 2 x 129 x 128, globals 64 x 128). A sample is 75 KB in a shard (float16)
instead of 67 KB (+11.8%: a window budget holds 10.5% fewer samples). `mtgz/az/layout_v5.json` is
checked in (`encode::layout_json`, version 5; `layout_json_is_checked_in`), and `layout_v4.json`
stays as it was (the layout of every v4 checkpoint, and the widen's source: `mtgz/az/__init__.py`
registers v5). v5's layout declares its **global blocks** (`globals` 0-127, `match`, `globals_v5`;
zero-core's optional layout key, its docs/az.md 10.3), so a later widen can add globals inside a
block or between blocks; v4 declares none (its 160 globals map onto v5's first 160 in feature
order). Room for later facts without a v6: permanent status 112-119, stack status 64-71, 8 globals
per player and 14 of the game's (and v4's context 246-255 and match float 31).

### 60.2 The exact widen, and the proof on the main line's checkpoint

**zero-core** (`net.widen(old, features, actions, layout=)`, `net.token_feature_map`; its docs/az.md
10.3): given the game package's layout, a token network whose stored layout differs is widened
segment by segment: the segments by name and order (the same slots, present flags, identities and
actions; a slot may be wider at its end), the bags by name (rows added at the end, new bags), the
globals by declared block (else as a prefix in feature order). Every new input column gets zero
weights in its projection (the segment's input map `seg_in`, the bag map, the global map `g`);
everything else is copied. A layout that would add tokens (a new segment, more slots) or change
what a token is (present flag, identity, actions, another vocabulary) is refused. `fork_run.py
<src.pt> <new run>` and the co-training `resolver_init` pass the game's layout; without a layout, or
with the same layout, `widen` is as before. The layout description says which columns belong to
which segment (offset, slot count, width): the widen maps a v4 slot's floats to the first floats of
the v5 slot.

**The encoding side**: `encode::v4_projection()` (the v5 index of each v4 feature) is the map the
widen derives from the two checked-in JSON files (`layout_v5_widens_layout_v4_exactly` derives it
with the widen's rules), and it holds the v4 encoding exactly:

* **`DIGEST_ENCODING=v4`** (tests/digest.rs: every 10th decision's encoding hashed through the
  projection) gives **317b5ba05dc569fb**, layout v4's recorded full digest (58.11): over the 2,500
  digest games every v4 float of every hashed v5 encoding is v4's, bit for bit.
* `opening_encodings_but_the_declaration_are_unchanged` hashes the opening's encodings through the
  projection and keeps its recorded values (cube, best-of-three, Delver; `MtgAz::encode`, so the
  match block too).
* `the_v4_projection_leaves_exactly_the_v5_additions` (encode.rs): one to one, and the v5 floats it
  leaves are exactly the additions of 60.1.

**Real states, two builds**: a v4 build (main a6bb3bc, `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/v5/v4ref`) and this
build played the same seeded games (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/v5/exact_collect.py`: uniform random play,
24 games each of the cube's random decks, best-of-three matches and the Delver mirror with
`runs/ab2-cqscale03`'s spec; every legal-action list hashed: the same trajectories in both). Of
their 8,440 encodings (both viewers every 5th decision: 2,034 cube, 4,756 best-of-three, 1,650
Delver), **the v5 encodings at the widen's map equal the v4 encodings bit for bit, all 8,440**; 8,068
of them have a v5-only float set (343 of the 3,968 new floats are set somewhere).

**The real network** (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/v5/exact_compare.py`, results in `exact_result.json`): a
copy of `runs/ab2-cqscale03/models/iter_0115.pt` (layout v4, tokens 128 x 4; read only) widened
with this build's layout, through `tools/fork_run.py` into `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/v5/fork-ab2` (its
iteration 0 is the in-memory widen tensor for tensor). On the 8,440 positions (CPU, float32):

| Widened network on | vs the source on the v4 encoding: policy logits | value logits | value probabilities | margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the v5 encoding | max abs 5.7e-6 (7,984 rows bit for bit) | 1.9e-6 (8,012) | 3.0e-7 | 8.3e-7 (7,984) |
| the v5 encoding, every v5-only float uniform noise in [-4, 4] | the same | the same | the same | the same |

and the widened network on the v5 encoding with its v5-only floats zeroed equals it on the real
v5 encoding bit for bit (all 8,440 rows, all three heads): the new columns have no effect at all,
and the residual 1e-6 is float rounding of the input maps' sums over more (zero-weighted) columns.
The source's value probabilities on these positions span 1e-5 .. 0.99999. Also: zero-core's tests
(a synthetic wider layout, declared blocks, the refusals, fork_run across a layout change) and this
repo's pytest `test_a_v4_token_network_widens_onto_layout_v5_exactly` (a random v4 network on this
build's real encodings, the v5 floats randomised).

**End to end** (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/v5/smoke-v4`, `smoke-v5`): a v4 `delver-smoke` iteration with
a tiny token network (32 x 1, 2 heads) on the v4 build; its `iter_0001.pt` forked by `fork_run` into
a new run on this build; `delver-smoke` 2 iterations there: iteration 0's evaluation (the widened
network: vs the heuristic 2/8, vs random 3/4), self-play with v5 shards (75 KB a sample),
training (policy 0.942, 0.918), evaluation and Elo at 1 and 2, no failure.

### 60.3 The 42 gaps, encoded

Per-player globals (`g5::*`, at `encode::O_GLOBALS_V5` + 24 x side, viewer first; squashed counts):

| Fact (the gate's perturbation) | Float |
|---|---|
| cards drawn this turn; in the draw step | `DRAWN` / 4, `DRAW_STEP` / 2 |
| noncreature spells cast this turn; spells cast this game | `NONCREATURE` / 4, `SPELLS_GAME` / 16 |
| gained life this turn; can't gain life | `GAINED_LIFE`, `CANT_GAIN` |
| creatures that attacked this turn | `ATTACKED` / 4 |
| Yawgmoth's Will this turn; graveyard exile this turn | `GY_PLAY`, `GY_EXILE` |
| the city's blessing; protection from everything | `CITY`, `PROTECTED` |
| the pool's artifact-only and haste mana | `POOL_ART` / 4, `POOL_HASTE` / 4 |
| delayed triggers waiting | `DELAYED` / 4 (their controller's) |
| exiled cards they may play | `EXILE_PLAY` / 4 (face down included) and the bags 17-18 by identity |
| graveyard cards discarded this turn | `DISCARDED` / 4 (their owner's) |
| the last normal turn; additional combats | the game's `NORMAL` (the viewer's), `EXTRA_COMBATS` / 2 |

Permanent status 96-111 (`perm::*`): `MUST_ATTACK` and `EXILE_IF_DIES` (counts of those rules
effects / 2; goad keeps its own float), `SUBTYPES` (effects that change its subtypes / 2),
`EVOKED`, `ESCAPED`, `MONSTROUS`, `CHOSEN_PLAYER` (1 the viewer, -1 the opponent), `EXHAUSTED`
(exhaust abilities activated / 2), `CHOSEN_COLOR` (5, one-hot), `EXERTED`, `RESOLVED` (times its
abilities resolved this turn / 4), `DONE_ONCE` (once-each-turn actions / 2). Stack status 32-63
(`stack::*`): `MODES` (8: the times mode k was chosen / 2; the most modes of an ability in either
card table is 4, `every_mode_has_a_float`), `ALT` and `ALT_INDEX` (an alternative cost and which),
`FROM` (7, one-hot: flashback, flashback with the mana-cost choice, escape, a permission from exile,
another graveyard route, miracle, the library's top) and `FREE`, `ORIGIN` (4, one-hot: a graveyard,
exile, a library, another zone; from hand none), `DELVED` / 4, `AMOUNT` (a trigger's event amount
/ 8), `EXILED_AFTER` (it is exiled as it leaves), `FLASHBACK` (the card's flashback flag),
`NOTED` / 4, `DIVISION` (its first two targets' amounts / 8), `ATTACK_AS` and `ATTACK_WALKER`
(ninjutsu), `SPLICED` / 4.

Counts rather than flags wherever the same thing can apply twice (a second "attacks each combat",
a second exhaust ability, another ability resolving): one more always shows. The cards a player may
play from exile are a bag (their identities, pooled into the global token like every bag) plus a
count, not a segment: a segment's tokens would join the attention (no exact widen), and a bag goes
through zero weights until training reaches it. A face-down card is in a bag only for a viewer who
knows it; its existence is in the count for both (Headliner Scarlett).

**The gate** (`public_state_reaches_the_encoding`, 240 positions, 140 perturbations): **131
encoded, the 4 deliberate limits of 58.9, 0 gaps** (the test now asserts that only `Design` limits
are left), and 5 rare perturbations never applied by random positions: a prepared permanent (58.8),
haste mana, divided damage, a ninjutsu attack, a splice; the last four are encoded and read back by
hand (`v5_rare_stack_and_pool_facts_are_encoded`, encode.rs: every other float unchanged). The
limits' kind `V5` became `NextLayout` (none). `public_state::V5_FIXED` names the 42. One
perturbation changed: "an exiled card may be played this turn" picks a card its owner may not play
yet (another permission on a playable card changes nothing they may do).

`the_v5_facts_are_encoded` reads the Delver mirror's facts back for both viewers: Prismari Charm's
mode 2 on the stack (`MODES` 0, 0, 0.5), the caster's noncreature spell and spell this game;
Force of Will cast by exiling Counterspell (`ALT` 1, `ALT_INDEX` 0.25; the Bolt below at 0);
Murktide Regent delving five cards (`DELVED` 1.25); Brainstorm's three draws (`DRAWN` 0.75); True-Name
Nemesis's chosen player (-1 / 1 by viewer) and Painter's Servant's red.

### 60.4 Hidden information

Every new fact is public (the fields were classified public in 58.7, and `Game::view_of` already
showed them, 58.8), except a face-down card's identity, which only its knower's bag holds. Tests:
`the_v5_facts_encode_no_hidden_information` (the 42 perturbations on the gate's positions of the
four kinds: 2,667 perturbed positions; for each viewer three `determinize` worlds compared with each
other, 10,668 worlds: identical; worlds rather than the position itself, because a change made by
hand can leave the other player's pending decision stale and every world of a non-deciding viewer
recomputes it), and its Headliner Scarlett part (the face-down card in P0's `MY_EXILE_PLAY` bag, not
in P1's `OPP_EXILE_PLAY`, the count 0.25 for both; 40 worlds of P1 encode the same while the card is
resampled); the existing `determinize_keeps_features_and_legal_actions_for_both_viewers`,
`equal_keys_mean_equal_features` and `the_opening_encodes_no_hidden_information` on v5; the fuzzer's
`determinize` checks (20,000 Delver games, 60.6).

### 60.5 Moving a run to v5

**Never resume across a layout change**: a v4 run's window holds v4 shards (33,652 wide), its
optimizer state has v4's parameter shapes, and its checkpoints read v4 inputs. Note the hazard: a
v4 token checkpoint evaluated by a v5 build reads the first 33,652 floats of a v5 encoding without
any error (`TokenNet.forward` takes `x[:, :features]`, the prefix read that lets an older network
read a wider input whose new features come last): everything after the bags would be misread. So a v4 run stays on its v4 pinned build until it moves, and it moves by
**forking its newest checkpoint into a NEW run directory** (`tools/fork_run.py <iter_K.pt> <new
run>`: iteration 0 of the new run is the widened network, 60.2). In the new run the **iteration
numbering, the Elo pool, the window and the optimizer state restart**; the network's knowledge
carries over exactly. Settings tied to the iteration number restart with it: the learning rate's
step decay (`lr` x 0.5^((it - 1) // `lr_halve_every`), floor `lr_min`) and `value_q`'s warm-up, so the
fork sets the main line's current values; AdamW starts fresh with its warm-up (`lr_warmup_steps`
100, as after any fresh optimizer); the window grows from the fork's own first iteration
(`window_grow`), and training waits for `min_window_samples` (30,000: about one iteration of 800
games).

**The live Delver main line** (`runs/ab2-cqscale03`, layout v4; at iteration 131 on 10-29, `lr` at its
floor 1e-4, `value_q` 0.6), once this branch and zero-core `feat/token-widen` are merged (the
procedure of 56.10 / 57.5 / 59.3 for the worktree; `<sha7>` the merged commit, `<K>` the newest
checkpoint, `ab2v5` the new run's name):

```
# 1. the pinned worktree of the merged commit, built; the Mac's checkout of it (evaluation, self-play)
git -C "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero" worktree add "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero-wt/run-<sha7>" <sha7>
cd "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero-wt/run-<sha7>"
bash tools/build_py.sh
bash tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout
# 2. stop the main line at an iteration boundary (it exits after the iteration in progress)
touch "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2-cqscale03/STOP"
# 3. its newest checkpoint widened into a new run; the main line's settings (cq_c_scale 0.3 and the
#    rest: a flag overrides, the preset fills only what the run has not saved)
python tools/fork_run.py "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2-cqscale03/models/iter_<K>.pt" \
  "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2v5"
cp "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2-cqscale03/config.json" "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2v5/config.json"
# 4. the main line's command (59.3) on the new run, plus the iteration-tied settings at the main line's values
python tools/launch_hidden.py "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2v5/supervisor_console.txt" \
  python tools/supervise.py "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab2v5" --preset delver-mirror --seed 1 \
  --eval-remote mac --selfplay-remote mac --games 800 --conc 192 --ram-budget-gb 20 --selfplay-remote-linger 1 \
  --eval-select cq --eval-select-min-visits 4 --eval-random-games 0 --elo-offsets 1,2,4,8 --elo-games 25 \
  --window-cache 1 --train-prefetch 2 --iters 400 --eval-every 8 \
  --lr 0.0001 --value-q-warmup 0
```

(With 59.3's `--eval-select-c-scale S` if the main line has one by then. Optionally `--window-grow
0`: the window reaches 6 iterations as soon as it has them.) Then `watch_run` on the new run, and
the delverai publisher pointed at `runs/ab2v5` (`tools/delverai_publish.py`; its checkout needs this
pin). The main line's directory stays as it is (stopped, its checkpoints, Elo pool and shards kept);
`fork_run` only reads it.

**Evaluation and Elo continuity** (what to read across the move):

* **Iteration 0 of the fork is iteration K of the main line** (60.2: the same outputs to 1e-6). Its
  evaluation (100 games against the heuristic at 32 simulations, the reference games) is a fresh
  measurement of K's strength on the same yardstick: the yardstick's win rate is the continuous
  series (it should agree with K's within its standard error; the searches see the same values up
  to float rounding, so a game may still take another line at a near tie).
* **Elo restarts**: the fork's pool (`runs/ab2v5/elo/<rule>/`) holds its own iterations from 0;
  anchored on the same yardstick (the heuristic, 1000) its ratings are on the main line's scale but
  another fit (other opponents, other games), so a few dozen points between the two series mean
  nothing. On the dashboard the fork is a new run (its own line); the main line's chart ends at K.
* **Head to head across the move**: any v4 checkpoint widens exactly, so the main line's
  checkpoints can be compared with the fork's in the v5 build: `fork_run` (or `zero.net.widen` with
  the layout) gives the v5 form of `iter_K.pt` (or of an older main-line checkpoint), and `python -m
  mtgz.az.h2h` between it and the fork's iteration j measures the fork's progress against the main
  line directly (a v4 build can't play a v5 checkpoint, nor the v5 build a v4 one unwidened).
* The new floats start untrained (zero weights): the fork plays exactly as the main line did until
  training moves those weights; the first iterations' gains, if any, are learning to read the 42
  facts (Delver: spells this game, noncreature spells this turn, draws this turn, the stack's modes,
  pitch costs and delve).

**The paused v4 runs** (td1, mtg5): they stay on their v4 pinned worktrees and builds (never
re-pinned onto a v5 build: the hazard above) until migrated the same way. mtg5 (a single-game `mtg`
run): `fork_run` of its newest checkpoint into a new run, its config copied, the iteration-tied
settings set as above. td1 (co-training): its draft network's layout (`team_draft`, draft_v2) is
unchanged, its play network (the resolver, game `mtg`) is v4: a v5 td1 is a new co-training run
whose draft network is a `fork_run` of td1's (the same layout: a copy) and whose resolver starts from
td1's resolver checkpoint through `resolver_init` (widened onto v5 at the start: `init_resolver`
passes the layout since zero-core f606724); not rehearsed here. (Rehearsed in 60.7, which corrects
it: with only the forked draft checkpoint the co-training bootstrap overwrites it with a fresh
network, so both iteration-0 checkpoints come from `fork_run`.)

## 61. The checkpoint / layout mismatch guard (zero-core's encoding guard)

Branch `ckpt-guard` (main b903fa2), zero-core `feat/ckpt-guard` 7132cb8 (code) + edf4b89 (docs),
2026-10-29, CPU only, `runs/delver2` live on the GPU and the Mac; every run directory only read.

### 61.1 Why

Layout v5 (60) is 37,620 floats, v4 33,652. A v4 token network loaded by a v5 build was **misread
without an error**: `TokenNet` takes the first 33,652 floats of each row (`x[:, :features]`) and
reads its slots and globals where v4 had them - the permanents' slots start 2,048 floats later in
v5 and are 24 floats wider. The only safe move across a layout change is `tools/fork_run.py`'s widen
into a new run (60.2, 60.5). `mtgz.az.replays.check_encoding` (fce517e) refused such checkpoints in
the replay recorder alone; zero-core now refuses them at every load, for every game (its docs/az.md
10.4).

### 61.2 What zero-core checks, and where

`zero.net.check_encoding(config, game)`: a checkpoint's config against this build's game - the game,
`num_features` / `num_actions`, and for a token network the layout's segments, bags and vocabulary
(not the declared global blocks) and the layout `version` when the checkpoint and the build both
carry one. Every `zero.net.load` runs it (so every load site: the run's evaluators - self-play, the
yardstick, the Elo matches -, training's checkpoint, co-training's both networks, the remote
evaluation and remote self-play on the Mac, h2h, replay, targets, bench, this repo's human picks and
`tools/match_noise.py`), the run checks its newest checkpoint before it resumes, the evaluator
refuses leaf batches of another width, and an optimizer state that does not fit the network is not
loaded. A refused resume exits with **status 78** (`runctl.EXIT_REFUSED`; `run_state.json`
`refused`), and the supervisor does not restart it. On the Mac: a refused remote evaluation is one
line `ZERO_REMOTE_REFUSED` there and `remote eval mac iter N REFUSED by the remote's build ...` in
the run's log (retried every 5 minutes: `bash tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout` fixes the checkout); a
refusing self-play worker is `worker k REFUSED the run's checkpoint ...` in the run's log while the
desktop plays every game. The opt-outs (`allow_mismatch=True`): fork_run's widen and co-training's
`resolver_init` (both check the network they write), `selfplay_digest.py` (check_checkpoint_compat).

### 61.3 This repo

* `mtgz.az.replays.check_encoding(ckpt)` is zero-core's `check_checkpoint(ckpt)` now (the same
  refusal, the same place: before anything is played; the message names both sides).
* **The layout version is recorded**: zero-core's normalised layout keeps a layout's `name` /
  `version` (only when set), so a network made from now on (`make_net`, a fork_run widen onto
  `layout_v5.json`) carries `"version": 5` (the draft network `"version": 2`) in its checkpoint
  config, and the guard compares it with the build's when both have one. Networks from before (every
  v4 run, delver2, mtg5-v5, td1-v5) carry none and are judged by their structure, which tells v4
  from v5 already. A resumed run keeps its checkpoint's config: delver2's checkpoints stay as they
  are.
* `tests/test_mtg_az.py::test_the_encoding_guard_refuses_a_v4_network_and_takes_a_v5_one`: a
  layout_v4.json network refused by `load`, a run's evaluator and the replay recorder (the message:
  33652 -> 37620, layout v4 vs v5, fork_run); its widen accepted and recorded as v5; a new network
  v5; a v5 network recorded as another version refused; one without a version accepted; the draft
  network v2, and refused as an `mtg` network.

### 61.4 The real checkpoints (copies; sha256 equal to the originals)

| Checkpoint | Run resume (`python -m mtgz.az.run --run <scratch run> --preset mtg-smoke --iters 0`) | Evaluator (`Run.evaluator` + a real driver's leaf batches) |
|---|---|---|
| `runs/ab2-cqscale03/models/iter_0137.pt` (v4, sha256 a04543f6...) | **refused**: exit 78 in 1.8 s, `run_state` refused, nothing written | **refused** (EncodingMismatch) |
| `runs/delver2/models/iter_0000.pt` (v5, sha256 2ffd293b...) | **accepted**: "starting after iter 0", exit 0 | **accepted**: 20 leaf batches of 37,620 features answered |

The refusal, as logged: `run REFUSED (exit status 78: the supervisor does not restart it):
.../iter_0000.pt: a network of another encoding than this build's (features 33652 -> 37620; token
layout: segment tops: offset 17792 -> 19840; segment my_permanents: offset 18116 -> 20164, width 148
-> 172; segment opponent_permanents: offset 22852 -> 25668, width 148 -> 172; 8 more). The network:
'mtg': 33,652 features, 1,024 actions, token layout without a version (11 segments, 1 bag), arch
'tokens'. This build: 'mtg': 37,620 features, 1,024 actions, token layout v5 (11 segments, 1 bag).
Fed this build's inputs it would misread them without an error. Move a run across an encoding
change with python tools/fork_run.py <checkpoint> <new run> (...)`.

Every run's newest checkpoint on this build (read-only): **accepted** - delver2 (iter_0016, the
live main line), mtg5-v5, td1-v5 and its resolver, td1's draft network (draft_v2, unchanged);
**refused** - ab1-valueq06, ab2-cqscale03, ab3-pfull05, ab4-selfplaycq, delver1, mtg4, mtg5, td1's
resolver (v4), mtg3 (v3), mtg1, mtg2, mtg2a/b/c, mtg2n (13,532 features). The refused ones are the
runs 60.5 says never to resume on a v5 build; none of them is a legitimate v5 resume. delver2's
`opt_latest.pt` (iteration 16) fits its checkpoint (the new optimizer-state check: no mismatch).

### 61.5 Co-training's first start no longer overwrites a forked network

60.7's hazard is fixed in zero-core (`CoRun.first_checkpoints`): with no iteration holding both
checkpoints, an existing checkpoint 0 of either network is kept (logged `primary iteration 0 = the
checkpoint already there, kept`), the missing one created (the primary fresh, the resolver from
`resolver_init`, else fresh), both checked by the guard; refused (nothing written) when the
resolver has a checkpoint 0 and `resolver_init` is set too, or when a network has checkpoints after
0 but no iteration has both. So 60.5's route (draft network by fork_run, play network by
`resolver_init`) works as written; td1-v5 (both iteration-0 checkpoints from fork_run) resumes
through the normal path (iteration 0 has both) and is unaffected. zero-core's test: a primary forked
into iteration 0 survives bit for bit a start with `resolver_init`.

### 61.6 Checks

Tier "core behaviour, byte-identical defaults for matching checkpoints" (the tiered gates):

* zero-core (7132cb8): `cargo test --release` 50 + 3 passed; `pytest tests` 202 passed (15 new:
  `tests/test_encoding_guard.py`); toy runs and `check_checkpoint_compat` against f3f5535 identical
  (its az.md 10.4); Glass Road c1f56dc, Caverna a6fad73, Kingdom Builder 4202a4a build against it;
  every game's paused run accepted with the worktree it resumes from, every other run with its
  game's build (az.md 10.4).
* This repo (ckpt-guard, pinned to 7132cb8 for the checks; the docs commit edf4b89 changes no code):
  `bash tools/build_py.sh` (1 min 26 s), `cargo test --release -p engine --test az` **27 passed**,
  `pytest tests` **48 passed** (1 min 11 s).
* No search smoke, no digest re-record: no game plays differently (the guard only reads configs;
  the engine is unchanged).

### 61.7 Re-pinning delver2

delver2 can re-pin onto this core at an iteration boundary once it is merged (tier "re-pin onto an
already-verified commit"): its checkpoints and optimizer state pass the guard on the v5 build, and
nothing it runs behaves differently (the changed code paths are the checks, the refusals, fork_run,
co-training's first start and widen's same-layout case, which a resumed single-game run never
takes). Procedure as 59.3 / 60.5: a pinned worktree of the merged main, `bash tools/build_py.sh`,
`bash tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout` (the Mac's evaluation and self-play checkout must have the same
layout: with the guard a stale one refuses loudly instead of misreading), stop at an iteration
boundary (STOP), relaunch the supervisor from the new worktree with the same command, watch_run.

## 62. A bigger network for the Delver mirror: sizes, throughput, a distilled warm start

Branch `bignet` (main e5483aa), zero-core `feat/bignet` (code c539d8f + 907bad6, docs f1cdbd9, a device fix
437cef0; on main edf4b89; its docs/az.md 10.5, 13), 2026-10-29, **CPU only**: the round-2 A/B (`runs/ab-r2`) held
the desktop GPU, the Mac and the desktop's self-play driver; every run directory only read (copies in
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/bignet`).
Nothing here was trained or played on the GPU: 62.6 is the plan for it.

### 62.1 Why

The Delver main line has plateaued: `runs/delver2` (layout v5, the widened `ab2-cqscale03` iteration
137) is at ~86% against the heuristic (iteration 16: 86 / 100 games) and gains about one Elo point an
iteration in 400-game head-to-heads (`runs/ab/`: iteration 102 vs 62 of the main line +67, 137 vs 102
+38, delver2's 17 vs 0 +17 +- 17), its training losses flat for 20 iterations (policy 0.352, value
0.40). The user's hypothesis: the network's capacity (tokens 128 x 4, 4 heads, feed-forward 256, 1.55M
parameters) is the ceiling; round 2's cheap knobs (lr, value_q, window, sims) test the alternatives.

### 62.2 Candidate sizes and what they cost

**Measured** (desktop CPU, `python -m mtgz.az.bench infer` with zero-core's new options: real rows of
delver2's iterations 19 and 21, the Mac's shape of 3 torch threads per inference worker at batches of
192; zero-core docs/az.md 10.5 has the full table, the other shapes and the operator counts):

| network | parameters | multiply-adds / leaf | CPU leaves/s (2 workers x 3 threads, batch 192) | cost per leaf | kernels / forward, batch 96 | kernels / training step, batch 512 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 x 4 (delver2) | 1.55M | 21.9M | 4,627 | 1 | 515 | 3,357 |
| 128 x 8 | 2.08M | 39.9M | 2,918 | 1.59 | 595 | |
| **192 x 6** | **3.59M** | **65.5M** | **1,996** | **2.32** | **555** | **4,293** |
| 192 x 8 | 4.18M | 85.1M | 1,536 | 3.01 | 595 | |
| 256 x 6 | 5.93M | 112.8M | 1,114 | 4.16 | 555 | 4,293 |
| 256 x 8 | 6.98M | 147.1M | 864 | 5.36 | 595 | 5,229 |

(heads of 32 floats, feed-forward twice the width; the multiply-adds are the matrix products' and the
attention's, from zero.bench's operator count.)

**Estimated for the two producers of the shared queue**, from delver2's measured iterations 18-21
(800 games: the Mac 25.1k leaves/s, ~679 games, 8.3k leaves a game; the desktop 5.5k leaves/s on CUDA
at batches of 96, ~121 games, 7.8k leaves a game; self-play 174 s + training 37 s = 211 s an
iteration, ~13.6k games an hour):

* **The Mac** (CPU, 2 processes x 4 inference workers x 3 threads): its rate divided by the CPU cost
  per leaf above. That is the pessimistic end: 50.3 found the 128 x 4 network's self-play bound by the
  driver's Python loop with cores to spare (4-6 busy per process), so part of the growth may land on
  idle cores; a bigger network makes it arithmetic-bound soon (192 x 6 needs ~2.3x the core-seconds a
  leaf). Measure it before the A/B (62.6, one command, ~3 minutes on an idle Mac).
* **The desktop GPU**: eager CUDA inference of this network is bound by its operators, host syncs and
  per-row work, not its arithmetic (54.11: 5.0-6.5k leaves/s at batches of ~384 as at 96; zero-core
  az.md 10.5: the same 14 syncs and +8% kernels at 6 layers, +16% at 8, whatever the width; the 3x-7x
  arithmetic is a millisecond a batch on the RTX 5090). Estimated 0.9x the rate at 6 layers, 0.85x
  at 8; the training phase 1.3x (6 layers) to 1.6x (8) by its kernels, ~0.09 s a step now.
* The iteration T solves Mac x T + desktop x (T - training) = 800 games (the Mac lingers through the
  training: 211 s measured, 222 s by this model).

| network | Mac leaves/s | desktop leaves/s | games / hour | 800-game iteration | vs now |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 x 4 | 25.1k (measured) | 5.5k (measured) | 13.6k (measured) | 3.5 min | 1 |
| 128 x 8 | 15.8k | 4.7k | 8.8k | 5.5 min | 0.65 |
| **192 x 6** | **10.8k** | **5.0k** | **6.8k** | **7.1 min** | **0.50** |
| 192 x 8 | 8.3k | 4.7k | 5.6k | 8.6 min | 0.41 |
| 256 x 6 | 6.0k | 4.9k | 4.7k | 10.3 min | 0.34 |
| 256 x 8 | 4.7k | 4.6k | 4.0k | 11.9 min | 0.30 |

(The Mac's evaluations every 8 iterations, where its self-play stops, grow by the same factor.)

### 62.3 The recommendation: 192 x 6

**Tokens 192 x 6, 6 heads of 32, feed-forward 384: 3.59M parameters (2.3x), 3.0x the arithmetic a
leaf, half the self-play throughput (~6.8k games an hour, ~7 minutes an 800-game iteration against
3.5).** Both directions grow (width 1.5x, depth 1.5x); it is the largest step that keeps the Mac above
the desktop's own rate (10.8k vs 5.0k leaves/s) and an A/B arm of 10 iterations near 70-75 minutes.
256 x 6 (3.8x the parameters) is the more decisive capacity test at a third of today's throughput
(10-11 minutes an iteration); 128 x 8 (depth only) the cheap one. If 192 x 6 wins its A/B per
iteration, 256 x 6 is the next step; if it does not, capacity at this data rate is unlikely to be the
ceiling.

### 62.4 The warm start: distillation (zero-core `tools/distill.py`, `fork_run --net`)

The student is a fresh 192 x 6 network of layout v5 (version 5 recorded in its config; the encoding
guard of this build and of the A/B's pinned build run-e5483aa accept it, and every load path - the
run, the Mac's evaluation and self-play, h2h - builds it from its config: no code on the run path
changed), trained on the teacher's answers (its policy over the legal actions, its value, its margin;
since 62.9 a teacher's belief head too, which the student gets) on the run's own shards, then forked into a continuation of the run at K with `fork_run --source
<run> --dest <fork> --iter K --net <student.pt>`: the fork has the run's window, iteration numbers,
settings and Elo history, the student as checkpoint K, no optimizer state (a fresh AdamW with its
warm-up at the run's lr) and K's Elo results dropped (zero-core az.md 13.3).

**Why not the function-preserving widen** (zero-core az.md 13.2): depth grows exactly (zero-output
blocks), width does not - the LayerNorms average over the width, so only exact duplicates (x 2, never
192) keep the function, and duplicates train in lockstep until noise breaks the exactness; the
student of a distillation is a fresh network that uses all of its capacity, of any size, and the tool
serves every game. The price is a GPU phase (62.6: an estimated 40-55 minutes) and a fidelity short
of exact, which the held-out agreement and the head-to-head gate measure.

### 62.5 Evidence on CPU

* **Toy** (zero-core tests): students of another size and architecture converge to their teacher on
  held-out positions (KL 0.077 -> 0.009, top-1 0.12 -> 0.92 in 300 steps; az.md 13.4); `fork_run
  --net` continues a toy run with a distilled bigger student as checkpoint K and trains it.
* **delver2's iteration 21 into 192 x 6** (`tools/distill.py` on copies; CPU, 6 torch threads at
  below-normal priority, 23 minutes, 0.54 s a step): trained on 79,427 rows (the Mac's 33 shards of
  iterations 16-20, 232,665 rows subsampled by a 6 GB budget), held out 8,192 rows of iteration 21's
  six Mac shards (never trained on); 2,500 steps of 256 rows (8 epochs), lr 1e-3 (warm-up 150, cosine
  to 1e-5), `teacher_w` 1. Held out (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/bignet/cpu192/student_192x6.pt.log.jsonl`):

  | step | policy KL (nats; p90) | top-1 | abs. P(win) difference (sq.) | student's policy CE vs pi / value CE vs z / value acc. |
  |---:|---|---:|---|---|
  | 0 (fresh) | 0.595 (1.065) | 0.688 | 0.302 (0.1220) | 0.946 / 0.701 / 0.476 |
  | 500 | 0.126 (0.348) | 0.881 | 0.075 (0.0137) | 0.476 / 0.416 / 0.790 |
  | 1,000 | 0.097 (0.259) | 0.898 | 0.066 (0.0106) | 0.446 / 0.407 / 0.791 |
  | 1,500 | 0.077 (0.200) | 0.916 | 0.057 (0.0086) | 0.426 / 0.402 / 0.799 |
  | 2,000 | 0.067 (0.178) | 0.919 | 0.055 (0.0078) | 0.415 / 0.401 / 0.799 |
  | 2,500 | **0.067** (0.175) | **0.921** | **0.053** (0.0075) | 0.414 / 0.400 / 0.799 |
  | the teacher | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0.352 / 0.377 / 0.815 |

  Every decision of the shards has at least 2 legal actions (8,192 of 8,192). The training KL at the
  end was 0.026 against the held-out 0.067: on 79k rows the student fits its rows better than it
  generalises, so the GPU run takes the whole window (~4x the rows) and more steps (62.6 a). The
  path works end to end: the student is a layout v5 checkpoint the guard accepts on this build and on
  the A/B's (`run-e5483aa`: loaded, 3,585,117 parameters), its record in its `extra`.
* **Head to head on CPU, student vs teacher** (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/bignet/cpu_h2h.py`:
  `zero.h2h.match`, seats alternating, 32 simulations, chance_k 2, seed 7, both sides `cq-n4-v50-s0.3` as round 2's
  head-to-heads; 3 search threads, one torch thread): the distilled student **62.5% +- 7.0** against
  delver2's iteration 21 (48 games in 13.7 minutes, mean margin +4.1, none unfinished) - parity within
  1.8 se: the 23-minute CPU student is not weaker than its teacher. The head-to-head discriminates: the
  fresh 192 x 6 network (the student before its distillation) lost all 24 of its games (margin -20.7).
  A sanity check, not the gate: 48 games cannot tell 50% from 60% (62.6 b's 400 on the GPU can).

### 62.6 The GPU plan (not run; for the main line `r3-2b-beliefsearch`, rewritten 2026-10-29: 62.9)

When round 3 (`runs/ab-r3`) is done and the GPU and the Mac are free; Git Bash on the desktop. `MAIN` is
the main line then (`runs/ab-r3/state.json` "main"), stopped at an iteration boundary (STOP, its
supervisor gone), `K` its newest checkpoint: the commands read both (written when they were
`r3-2b-beliefsearch` at 91: 128 x 4 tokens with the belief head, root-view leaves with value-only samples
0.5, belief-weighted determinization in self-play and evaluation; 62.9 says what changed and why). The
distillation, the fork and the head-to-heads run from a pinned worktree of a main that has zero-core's
distillation of auxiliary heads (zero-core `feat/distill-aux`, az.md 13.6) and its build; the A/B's two
arms run on the main line's own pinned build (round 3's `worktree`), which loads the 192 x 6 student like
any checkpoint (nothing on the run path changed).

```
AB="C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/ab-r3"
MAIN="$(python -c "import json; print(json.load(open(r'$AB/state.json'))['main'].replace(chr(92), '/'))")"
K=$(python -c "import glob, os; print(max(int(os.path.basename(p)[5:9]) for p in glob.glob(r'$MAIN/models/iter_*.pt')))")
KK=$(printf %04d $K); K10=$(printf %04d $((K + 10)))
OUT=E:/mtg-zero-scratch/distill-gpu/k$K; mkdir -p $OUT
FORK="C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero/runs/r3-big192x6"
SPEC="$(python -c "import json; print(json.load(open(r'$MAIN/config.json'))['spec'])")"
VIEW="$(python -c "import json; print(json.load(open(r'$MAIN/config.json')).get('selfplay_leaf_value_view') or 'mover')")"
H2H=(--sims 32 --spec "$SPEC" --device cuda --threads 8 --seed 7 --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3
     --b-cq-c-scale 0.3 --a-leaf-value-view $VIEW --b-leaf-value-view $VIEW)
cd "C:/Users/Gregg Keithley/mtg-zero-wt/run-<sha of that main>"     # bash tools/build_py.sh done there
```

**0. The Mac's real cost** (optional, ~3 minutes, the Mac idle; this checkout pushed): the Mac's
inference shape (8 workers x 3 threads at batches of 192) on real rows of the main line, the three sizes:

```
scp "$(ls "$MAIN/data/iter_$KK"/m00-*_000.npz | head -1)" greggkeithley@100.95.248.116:/tmp/delver_rows.npz
bash tools/mac.sh 'bash tools/build_py.sh && for n in "128 4 4 256" "192 6 6 384" "256 6 8 512"; do set -- $n; python -m mtgz.az.bench infer --game mtg --arch tokens --hidden $1 --blocks $2 --heads $3 --ff $4 --shard /tmp/delver_rows.npz --batches 192 --workers 8 --torch-threads 3 --seconds 10; done'
```

**(a) Distil the student on the desktop GPU.** The window: the main line's 6 iterations, ~460k rows (77k
an iteration, a third of them value-only), of which a 30 GB budget keeps ~367k (80%); held out: the
newest iteration's desktop shard (~13k rows). 16,000 steps of 512 rows (~22 epochs) at lr 1e-3, the
student at its best held-out KL kept as well. The teacher's belief head comes with it - copied into the
student and distilled at the defaults (`--aux-w 1`, `--aux-teacher-w 1`: zero-core az.md 13.6, 62.9) -
and the value-only rows train the value, not the policy (the run's own mask):

```
python tools/distill.py "$MAIN/models/iter_$KK.pt" $OUT/student_192x6.pt --data "$MAIN/data" \
    --heldout "$MAIN/data/iter_$KK/r00_000.npz" --hidden 192 --blocks 6 --heads 6 --ff 384 \
    --steps 16000 --batch 512 --lr 1e-3 --lr-min 1e-5 --warmup 500 --ram-budget-gb 30 --heldout-rows 16384 \
    --eval-every 1000 --save-every 2000 --keep-best --device cuda --torch-threads 4 --seed 1 \
    > $OUT/distill_console.txt 2>&1
```

The first line (`start`) must show `"aux": [["belief", 1024, "multinomial"]]`, `train_view_rows` (~a
third of `train_rows`) and `train_aux_rows` = `train_rows`; every `train` line `aux_belief_kl`, every
`heldout` line `decision`, `view` and `aux`.

* **Time, estimated 40-55 minutes**: the window's load ~1-2 min (54 shards read whole and subsampled;
  the CPU run read 18 in 11 s), the teacher's answers once with its belief (~367k rows, ~1-3 min),
  ~0.12-0.15 s a step = 32-40 min (the run's own GPU training step on this line: 0.097 s at 512 rows for
  128 x 4 with the head - r3-2-belief025's iterations 89-91, ~46 s for ~300 steps of which 17-20 s the
  load -; a 192 x 6 step has 1.28x its kernels, its arithmetic is milliseconds; the head and the
  teacher's predictions add 2 MB a batch), 16 held-out evaluations (~1 min). The first `train` line's
  `s_per_step` gives the real figure; `--resume` continues after a crash from `student_192x6.pt.partial`
  (every 2,000 steps).
* **Why 16,000 steps** (the old plan 12,000): a third of each batch is value-only rows, which teach the
  value and the head but not the policy; 16,000 x 512 x 2/3 = 5.5M decision rows seen, ~0.9x the old
  plan's 6.1M (12,000 x 512, all of them decisions).
* **RAM**: 81.7 KB a row (75.5 KB of features and targets, 6.1 KB for the head: the shards' belief
  targets and the teacher's predictions, zero-core az.md 13.6), so 30 GB = 367,264 rows (24 GB: 293,811,
  of which ~98k value-only, against the old plan's 318k decisions). Peak ~40 GB: the window 30 + the
  held-out rows ~1.3 + the shards being loaded (8 at a time, up to ~6) + CUDA and torch ~3. The main line
  is stopped (its 20 GB window cache freed) and nothing else large may run; on a busier machine
  `--ram-budget-gb 24` (peak ~34 GB). More distinct games help (the CPU run of 62.5 overfit 79k rows):
  other v5 Delver data directories of the same line can be added with more `--data`.

**(b) Fork, then verify** (~35-45 minutes). The student goes into the fork first, so that its side of
the head-to-head searches as the run does: `mtgz.az.h2h` reads each side's search from its checkpoint's
run (`config.json` next to `models/`: eval_belief_tilt 1 and belief_mix 0.25 whatever `--select` says,
and eval_root_search when the line has the Gumbel root - then both sides search with it, whatever
`--select` says), while a student file outside a run would search with the defaults (uniform worlds,
PUCT); `$VIEW` gives both sides the leaf view the line trains with (round 3's driver does the same).
`fork_run --net` checks the encoding and the belief head before it copies anything (net.HeadMissing for
a student without the head, the refusal the run would give at its start):

```
python tools/distill.py --compare $OUT/student_192x6.pt "$MAIN/models/iter_$KK.pt" --data "$MAIN/data/iter_$KK/r00_000.npz" --device cuda
python tools/fork_run.py --source "$MAIN" --dest "$FORK" --iter $K --net $OUT/student_192x6.pt
python -m mtgz.az.h2h "$FORK/models/iter_$KK.pt" "$MAIN/models/iter_$KK.pt" --games 400 "${H2H[@]}" | tee $OUT/h2h_student_vs_teacher.json
```

**Gate: `a_score` >= 0.45** (2 se below parity at 400 games) **with `select_a` = `select_b`** (both sides
the same search: `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv-b1m0.25` on this line, `gumbel-m16-...-rv-b1m0.25` on a Gumbel one);
expected near 0.5 with held-out top-1 >= 0.95 and a belief KL well under the 64 x 2 CPU student's 0.026
(62.9). Below it: `rm -rf "$FORK"`,
distil further from the student (`--init $OUT/student_192x6.pt --steps 8000 --lr 3e-4 --warmup 200`, or
`student_192x6.best.pt` if the held-out KL rose late), fork and verify again. Time: `--compare` and the
fork ~1 min each (the fork hard-links the window); 400 games ~30-40 min (round 3's 600-game
head-to-heads of two 128 x 4 networks took 30-48 min with the belief or root-view leaves on one side,
`runs/ab-r3/state.json`; here both on both sides, one side 2.3x the arithmetic).

**(c) The A/B** (round 3's method: the fork arm K -> K + 10 with the student - the fork of (b) -, then
the control K -> K + 10, on the same build with round 3's `base_flags`, then a 600-game head-to-head of
the two K + 10 checkpoints, each side with its run's search; the fork wins at a score >= 0.5 + 2 se):

```
WT="$(python -c "import json; print(json.load(open(r'$AB/ab_config.json'))['worktree'])")"; cd "$WT"
BASE=(--preset delver-mirror --seed 1 --eval-remote mac --selfplay-remote mac --games 800 --conc 192 --selfplay-remote-linger 1
      --eval-select cq --eval-select-min-visits 4 --eval-select-c-scale 0.3 --eval-random-games 0 --elo-offsets 1,2,4,8
      --elo-games 25 --window-cache 1 --train-prefetch 2 --iters $((K + 10)) --eval-every 1000)
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py "$FORK/supervisor_console.txt" python tools/supervise.py "$FORK" "${BASE[@]}"
# ... checkpoint K + 10 in $FORK and its supervisor gone (watch_run / the dashboard), then the control:
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py "$MAIN/supervisor_console.txt" python tools/supervise.py "$MAIN" "${BASE[@]}"
# ... checkpoint K + 10 in $MAIN, then (from the distillation's worktree or the pinned one):
python -m mtgz.az.h2h "$FORK/models/iter_$K10.pt" "$MAIN/models/iter_$K10.pt" --games 600 "${H2H[@]}" | tee $OUT/h2h_ab.json
```

The fork's config.json is the main line's (its leaf view, value-only samples, belief weight, tilt and
mix, the Gumbel root if the line has it) with the student's size (arch, hidden, blocks, heads, ff);
`BASE` repeats round 3's flags only. The Mac self-plays a share of every iteration with the 192 x 6
network from the pinned build's checkout (it exists for the main line).

* **The A/B entry** for round 3's driver (an `ab_config.json` experiment), once its fork step passes an
  experiment's network to `fork_run.py` - not made here (`runs/` is the user's): a few lines in
  `runs/ab-r3/ab_driver.py`, `+ (['--net', exp['net']] if exp.get('net') else [])` on its `fork_run.py`
  command, and a blocker when the K it stopped the main line at is not the experiment's `net_iter` (a
  student distilled from another checkpoint):

  ```json
  {"name": "big192x6", "iters": 10, "needs_belief_head": true, "net_iter": 91,
   "net": "E:/mtg-zero-scratch/distill-gpu/k91/student_192x6.pt", "flags": [], "set": []}
  ```

  (`net` and `net_iter` for K = 91: the student must be the K at which the driver forks; its h2h then
  follows each arm's leaf view as round 3's do. The driver makes its own fork, `r3-<n>-big192x6`: delete
  the gate's `$FORK` after (b) when the driver runs the A/B.)
* **Time, estimated**: the fork arm **~70-80 minutes** (10 iterations at ~6.8-7.5 min: 62.2's model with
  this line's measured rates - the Mac 3.39 games/s and the desktop 0.66 at 128 x 4, r3-2-belief025's
  iterations 89-91 at 250 s an iteration - divided by 2.32 and 0.9 for 192 x 6, the training 1.3x; the
  first iteration ~1 min more: a fresh AdamW warms up, the window cache fills), the control **~42
  minutes** (4.2 min an iteration), the head-to-head **~45-60 minutes** (600 games) - with (a) and (b)
  **about 4-4.5 hours**. The first fork iterations measure what 62.2 estimated: `selfplay.remote.leaves_per_s`
  (the Mac), `selfplay.leaves_per_s` (the desktop), `train.seconds`. If the fork wins per iteration, the
  per-hour question is the fork's K + 10 against the control's K + 20 (the same wall-clock: run the
  control 10 more iterations, ~42 minutes, then the same head-to-head).

### 62.8 Limits

* The Mac's and the GPU's costs are estimates from the desktop CPU (62.2); the A/B's first
  iterations measure them (`metrics.jsonl` `selfplay.remote.leaves_per_s`, `selfplay.leaves_per_s`).
* A distilled student is close to its teacher, not equal: the gate is the head-to-head (62.6 b).
* The A/B compares equal iterations (800 games each), so it tests capacity per game of data; the
  bigger network's iterations take ~2x as long, so a per-hour comparison is the fork's K + N against
  the control's K + 2N.
* `fork_run --net` drops K's Elo results; the fork's Elo pool rates the student from its own games on.

### 62.9 The plan for the current main line: what changed and why (2026-10-29)

Branch `distill-aux` (main 014b85a), zero-core `feat/distill-aux` (on main 2f0a2e8; its az.md 13.6),
user-approved 2026-10-29 as a plan held in reserve for a plateau of the main line, **CPU only**: round 3's
Gumbel test held the desktop GPU and the Mac; `runs/` only read (copies in `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/distill2`).

**Why.** 62.4-62.6 were written for delver2 at 21. The main line is now `r3-2b-beliefsearch` (round 3:
root-view leaves adopted at 71, the belief head trained from 72, belief-weighted determinization
adopted at 91), and the distillation tool predated three of its features:

* **The belief head** (66, `aux_belief_w` 0.25) and **the belief search** (69, `selfplay_belief_tilt` /
  `eval_belief_tilt` 1, `belief_mix` 0.25), which refuses a checkpoint without the head (exit 78): a
  student distilled before had no head, so the main line could not continue from it.
* **Value-only rows** (67, `selfplay_view_samples` 0.5: a third of the window's rows, no policy target):
  the tool averaged its policy terms over every row, the value-only rows' zeros included, so the policy
  weighed two thirds of what the value did.
* **The head-to-head reads each side's search from its run** (eval_belief_tilt, belief_mix,
  eval_root_search): the old plan's `h2h $OUT/student.pt $MAIN/...` would have played the student with
  uniform worlds against a teacher with the belief (checked on CPU: `select_a` `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv`
  against `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv-b1m0.25`).

**What changed.** zero-core (az.md 13.6): the student gets the teacher's head and distils it (KL to the

## 63. The self-play league: past checkpoints in the Delver mirror

Branch `league` (main 0b476e0), zero-core `feat/league` 5099f00 (code) + d507df8, f57ee57 (docs: its
docs/az.md 14) on zero-core main 437cef0, 2026-10-29, CPU only (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=`, below-normal
priority, at most 8 threads), the A/B round 2 (`runs/ab-r2`, `runs/delver2`, `runs/r2-*`) live on the GPU and the Mac;
every run directory only read.

### 63.1 Why

The Delver main line `runs/delver2` (59, 60) gains about +1 Elo per iteration in head-to-heads
(`runs/ab/results.md`, round 2 under way), and against a different opponent it slips: its
evaluations on the Mac rate iterations 0 / 8 / 16 at 1477 / 1409 / 1312 (pool cq-n4-v50-s0.3), 94% /
91% / 86% against the heuristic. In a mirror, pure self-play trains the network against its own
current habits only - what beats them is learned, the habits it exploited fade, and nothing holds the
policy to what it already knew. Fictitious self-play and AlphaStar's league play part of the games
against past versions instead. zero-core's run setting `selfplay_league` is that, opt-in.

### 63.2 What zero-core built (its docs/az.md 14)

* `--selfplay-league F` (0 = off, the default): a share F of the self-play games - exactly over each
  driver's started games, spread evenly, seats alternating - puts a past checkpoint in one seat.
  `--selfplay-league-pool` (default `2,4,8,16,32`: raw offsets back from the self-playing checkpoint
  i-1, i.e. i-3, i-5, i-9, i-17, i-33, those that exist; or `all`), `--selfplay-league-slots` (1: one
  past checkpoint per iteration, its own evaluator key `L0`), `--selfplay-league-pick` (`uniform`, or
  `pfsp`: weighted by (1 - x)^2, x = the current networks' recent score against it).
* **Samples: the current network's decisions only.** The past network's seat searches with the
  self-play settings (noise, temperature, playout cap: it plays as in its own self-play) but records
  nothing (the Rust seat's new `record` flag); `z` is the game's result from the current network's
  seat, `q` its own search's root value. The past network's targets would pull the policy back to the
  habits the league is meant to keep it from settling into, and its values are an older head's.
* The past checkpoints load through the encoding guard (61): a past network of another layout is
  refused. Delver2's own checkpoints are all layout v5 (its iteration 0 is the widen of
  ab2-cqscale03's 137, 60.5), so the whole run is the pool; the v4 runs before it never are.
* Remote self-play on the Mac (52, 56): the phase line names the slot's checkpoint, the run ships it
  into the mirror with checkpoint i-1, the workers keep it through their clean-up, play the run's
  league table and report their accepted league games. A Mac checkout without the league would be
  refused (it would record both seats); the `mac` remote runs exactly the run's commit anyway
  (RunCommitRemote, 44).
* Metrics (`selfplay.league` per iteration): the share, the current network's score against the
  league and per checkpoint, the slots, the candidates, this machine's / the remote's league games;
  a log line `iter N league: ...`. `tools/fork_run.py --set selfplay_league=...` links every
  checkpoint the fork's league may play.
* Co-training (td1) refuses the setting; a run without it plays exactly as before (zero-core's
  az.md 14.5: byte for byte against edf4b89 and 437cef0).

### 63.3 This repo

Only the pin moves (zero-core f57ee57): no engine, encoding or package change. Digests and layout v5
unchanged (the engine is not touched).

### 63.4 Evidence on MTG (CPU)

* `delver-smoke` with the league on (`--iters 4 --selfplay-league 0.25 --selfplay-league-pool 1,2`,
  E:/mtg-zero-scratch/league/ds1 and, on the rebased branch, ds1b: 37-42 s): 4 of 16 games every
  iteration were league games (exactly 25%); iteration 1 played its own checkpoint 0 (`self`: no past
  checkpoint yet), iteration 2 checkpoint 0 (the one candidate), 3 checkpoint 0 of {1, 0}, 4 checkpoint
  1; 743 / 709 / 636 / 768 samples - the same on both builds (a classic driver is deterministic); Elo
  matches and evaluation as before.
* The same with the remote 'local' (`--rolling 1 --games 48 --conc 24 --selfplay-remote local
  --selfplay-remote-linger 1`; ds2 before the rebase and ds2b on this branch: a worker process on the desktop
  running the committed checkout, `MTGZ_REMOTE_COMMIT` and the engine stamp set as tools/mac.sh does):
  the quota 48 exact every iteration (ds2b: here 38 / 5 / 0 / 0, the worker 10 / 43 / 48 / 48 - the
  worker starts its phases early and lingers, so it took the toy-sized quota), league games 11 / 12 /
  13 / 8 (17-27% of the accepted games; the started games' share is exact), of them the worker's 2 /
  11 / 13 / 8; the mirror held checkpoints 1-3 after the last phase; iteration 4's league games split
  between checkpoint 0 (5: lingering games of phase 3, played against phase 3's slot) and checkpoint 1
  (3), as attributed; ds2: staleness mean 0-0.57, every row within one checkpoint.
* Throughput (zero-core az.md 14.3; the desktop's CPU, 96 games in flight, 4 search + 2 torch
  threads, delver2's iterations 23 and 11 as the current / past network, phases of 60-90 s next to the
  A/B arms): leaves/s off 1,824 / 2,034 / 1,757 / 1,330 (mean 1,736), F 0.25 one slot 1,642 / 1,344 /
  1,770 / 1,296 (mean 1,513, -13%), two slots 1,395 / 1,233 (-24%). A slot's call of ~6 leaves costs
  ~12 ms against ~46 ms for the current network's ~42 leaves.

### 63.5 Costs on the Delver line (estimates from 63.4 and delver2's iterations 18-23)

* **Self-play time**: the Mac plays ~85% of the 800 games (two CPU workers, ~25k leaves/s), the
  desktop's GPU the rest (~5k leaves/s, batches of 96). One slot at F 0.25: about -13% of the Mac's
  leaves per second (its workers infer on the CPU; measured on the desktop's CPU, 63.4), the desktop one more small CUDA graph replay per group
  dispatch (not measured: the GPU is the A/B's). The self-play phase (~175 s) grows by ~15% (~25 s);
  an iteration (~210 s) by ~10%.
* **Samples**: a league game records one side: ~12.5% fewer samples per iteration at F 0.25 (~48k
  instead of ~55k), training's steps with them (-5 s).
* **Mac traffic**: one more checkpoint per iteration into the mirror, 6.2 MB (the iteration's own
  checkpoint is 6.2 MB, the shards coming back ~50 MB compressed).
* **Memory**: one more 6.2 MB network per self-playing process (the desktop's driver, each Mac
  worker), inference only; nothing per game.

### 63.6 The A/B (flags)

As round 2 (`runs/ab-r2/ab_driver.py`): fork the main line at its newest checkpoint K with the league
on, run the fork then the control K -> K + 10 on the same build, h2h of the two K + 10 checkpoints (600
games, both sides `--select cq --select-min-visits 4` at scale 0.3); the fork wins at >= 0.5 + 2 se.
The build: a pinned run worktree of the merged main (`git worktree add --detach
~/mtg-zero-wt/run-<sha> <sha>`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=E:/cargo-target/mtg-zero/run-<sha> bash
tools/build_py.sh`, then `bash tools/mac.sh --eval-checkout` there: the Mac's `run-<sha12>` serves the
evaluations and the self-play). With the league off that build plays as the main line's (zero-core
az.md 14.5), so the control continues delver2 unchanged. The experiment entry for an `ab_config.json`
(the driver's `requires` waits for a build that has the flag; `set` goes to fork_run, so the fork
links the pool's checkpoints, `flags` to the fork's supervisor):

```json
{"name": "league25", "requires": "--selfplay-league",
 "flags": ["--selfplay-league", "0.25", "--selfplay-league-pool", "2,4,8,16,32",
           "--selfplay-league-slots", "1", "--selfplay-league-pick", "uniform"],
 "set": ["selfplay_league=0.25", "selfplay_league_pool=2,4,8,16,32",
         "selfplay_league_slots=1", "selfplay_league_pick=uniform"]}
```

By hand (K = delver2's newest checkpoint after a STOP; `$BASE` = round 2's `base_flags`):

```
BASE="--preset delver-mirror --seed 1 --eval-remote mac --selfplay-remote mac --games 800 --conc 192 \
  --selfplay-remote-linger 1 --eval-select cq --eval-select-min-visits 4 --eval-select-c-scale 0.3 \
  --eval-random-games 0 --elo-offsets 1,2,4,8 --elo-games 25 --window-cache 1 --train-prefetch 2"
python tools/fork_run.py --source runs/delver2 --dest runs/r3-1-league25 --iter K \
  --set selfplay_league=0.25 --set selfplay_league_pool=2,4,8,16,32 --set selfplay_league_slots=1 \
  --set selfplay_league_pick=uniform
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/r3-1-league25/supervisor_console.txt \
  python tools/supervise.py runs/r3-1-league25 $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000 \
  --selfplay-league 0.25 --selfplay-league-pool 2,4,8,16,32 --selfplay-league-slots 1 --selfplay-league-pick uniform
# when it has iteration K+10: the control, the same flags without the league
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/delver2/supervisor_console.txt \
  python tools/supervise.py runs/delver2 $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000
N=$(printf %04d $((K+10)))
python -m mtgz.az.h2h runs/r3-1-league25/models/iter_$N.pt runs/delver2/models/iter_$N.pt \
  --games 600 --sims 32 --spec "$(python -c "import json; print(json.load(open('runs/delver2/config.json'))['spec'])")" \
  --device cuda --threads 8 --seed 7 --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3 --b-cq-c-scale 0.3
```

Read alongside the verdict: the fork's `selfplay.league.win` per
iteration (its score against its own past; a run that forgets shows it falling against some
checkpoints), both arms against the heuristic (their next evaluations: 63.1's slide), and the arms'
K + 10 against an older main-line checkpoint (e.g. K - 16, the same h2h flags) - the league's aim is
robustness, which a head-to-head of the two arms alone may not show in 10 iterations. Expect the fork
to be ~10% slower per iteration (63.5). Follow-ups if it helps: `--selfplay-league-pick pfsp`, share
0.5, `--selfplay-league-pool all`.

## 64. Root minimum visits at the Delver mirror's small decisions (zero-core `root_min_visits`)

Branch `root-min-visits` (from main 3b2e6f4): zero-core pinned at **b486d36** (feat/root-min-visits:
5ce50d4 + docs abb0bbc, b486d36, on main f57ee57 = the league), `tools/mull_floor.py`, this section. Nothing of this repo's engine
changed; with the new settings off a run is the run of before, byte for byte.

### 64.1 Why

Fable's gameplay review of the Delver line (2026-10-29): at the mulligan (Keep / Mulligan) the
network's prior is >= 0.98 in 433 of 444 seven-card decisions, so at 64 simulations the option it
does not favour gets no visit, its Q is never estimated, and with completed-Q targets (section 22,
zero-core docs/search.md 3.1) an unvisited option is completed at v_mix - about the visited option's
Q - so its target stays at its prior: it cannot recover. The run keeps 0-land hands 58% of the time
and 1-land hands 87%, while the value head rates those hands 0.38 / 0.49 against 0.52 for normal
ones. The same starvation can hit any small decision under a saturated prior (attack or not, pay
for Daze, yes / no).

### 64.2 What zero-core does (its docs/search.md 3.5, az.md 1.2 and 9.2)

* **The floor.** A full search whose root has 2 .. `root_min_visits_max_actions` (default 4) options
  gives each at least k visits, when its budget allows (2 x options x k <= its simulations): a walk
  keeps PUCT's root option unless that option already has k visits and another has fewer, then it
  takes the least-visited one - a *forced walk*. Full searches only: the self-play seat's recorded
  ones (`sims`, the `p_full` share) and every search of an evaluation seat, never a fast
  (`sims_fast`) or minor (`sims_minor`, the mana payments) search. With this line's 64 / 16 / 4, k 4
  or 8 reaches every root of 2-4 options of the full searches.
* **What reads what.** Q, the 'cq' target and the 'cq' rule (and its guard) use every visit: a forced
  walk is a Q measurement; every option of a forced root is visited, so the target is softmax(ln P0 +
  sigma Q) over measured Q's. The visit counts - the 'visits' target, temperature sampling (this
  line's first 60 searched decisions, the mulligan among them), the 'visits' rule - and the root value
  target q leave the forced walks out exactly (`root_visits_pruned`, `root_win_pruned`): a move is
  sampled or wins the count only through PUCT's own visits, including those PUCT gives it once the
  forced walks have shown a good Q.
* **Settings.** `selfplay_root_min_visits` (self-play), `eval_root_min_visits` (every evaluation
  seat; its Elo pool is named after it: `cq-n4-v50-s0.3-f4`), `root_min_visits_max_actions`; 0 / 0 /
  4 by default. Seat keys `root_min_visits`, `root_min_visits_max_actions` (the Mac's checkout must
  have this core for remote self-play or evaluation with the floor on: an older one refuses the
  unknown seat key).
* **Tests and parity** (zero-core): the Rust tree (a 2-option root at 0.999 / 0.001 gets >= k visits
  on both, the cq target, the pruned counts and root value), the driver (a keep-or-mulligan test
  game: targets, sampled moves, the move rules, fast searches untouched; the golden records and match
  unchanged with the floor off), Rust vs Python trees and drivers at the noise floor, toy runs byte
  for byte with the settings at their defaults.

### 64.3 The demonstration: delver2's iteration 21 at the mulligan (CPU)

`python tools/mull_floor.py --model <copy of runs/delver2/models/iter_0021.pt> --zero 50 --one 100
--control 50 --reps 2 --small 300` (a copy, sha256 fcdf2116...; CPU, 4 torch threads, below normal;
45 s): seven-card hands at the mulligan declaration from games of the mirror's spec (the PlayDraw
choice at random; the starting player's declaration and, after it keeps, the other player's), 50
with no land, 100 with one, 50 with 2-4 as a control; each searched twice (two seeds) by the Rust
tree at 64 simulations without root noise (an evaluation's search), with the floor k = 0 (today), 4
and 8. Means over the searches:

| hands | k | prior on Mulligan | value of the hand | Mulligan's visits (forced + PUCT's) | Q Keep | Q Mulligan | cq target on Mulligan (s 0.3 / 1.0) | keep: 'visits' rule | keep: sampled | keep: cq4 s0.3 (this line's rule) | keep: cq4 s1.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 lands | 0 | 0.418 | 0.383 | 25.5 (0 + 25.5) | 0.439 | 0.356 | 0.376 / 0.230 | 58% | 59.5% | 58% | 69% |
| 0 lands | 4 | | | 27.2 (2.3 + 24.9) | 0.432 | 0.375 | 0.376 / 0.242 | 58% | 57.8% | 58% | 75% |
| 0 lands | 8 | | | 28.0 (4.5 + 23.4) | 0.429 | 0.375 | 0.382 / 0.279 | 58% | 57.8% | 59% | 73% |
| 1 land | 0 | 0.078 | 0.488 | 4.8 (0 + 4.8) | 0.501 | 0.338 | 0.072 / 0.053 | 91% | 92.4% | 91.5% | 94.5% |
| 1 land | 4 | | | 8.4 (3.6 + 4.8) | 0.501 | 0.375 | 0.071 / 0.048 | 91% | 92.0% | 91.5% | 95% |
| 1 land | 8 | | | 11.9 (7.3 + 4.7) | 0.500 | 0.368 | 0.075 / 0.064 | 91% | 91.8% | 91.5% | 93% |
| 2-4 lands | 0 | 0.009 | 0.513 | 0.4 (0 + 0.4) | 0.522 | 0.323 (2 searches) | 0.002 / 0.000 | 100% | 99.4% | 100% | 100% |
| 2-4 lands | 4 | | | 4.3 (3.9 + 0.4) | 0.521 | 0.378 | 0.002 / 0.000 | 100% | 99.4% | 100% | 100% |
| 2-4 lands | 8 | | | 8.3 (7.9 + 0.3) | 0.521 | 0.370 | 0.003 / 0.000 | 100% | 99.4% | 100% | 100% |

(Q Mulligan at k 0: the mean over the searches that visited it. "Sampled": 1 - Mulligan's share of
the visit counts without the forced walks, the temperature move's keep rate.)

* **The starvation is real.** The prior on Keep is >= 0.98 for 89 of the 100 one-land hands (42% of
  the 0-land ones, 98% of the controls), and at k 0 Mulligan got no visit in either search for 89 of
  the 100 one-land hands, 21 of the 50 zero-land ones and 49 of the 50 controls. The value of the
  hands is the review's: 0.38 / 0.49 / 0.51.
* **The floor measures what was missing**: with k 4 every starved hand's Mulligan gets its 4 visits
  (8 with k 8), PUCT's own visits stay as they were.
* **But the network's Q says keep.** Measured, Mulligan's Q is below Keep's in **every** starved
  low-land hand: by 0.087 on average for the 21 zero-land ones, by 0.137 for the 89 one-land ones
  (k 4; k 8 the same). A mulligan to six is worth ~0.37-0.40 to this network, below its estimate of
  keeping (0.43 with no land, 0.50 with one). So the cq target barely moves (1 land 0.072 -> 0.071 at
  scale 0.3) and **the keep rates do not move**: 0 lands 58% at k 0, 4 and 8 ('visits' rule; this
  line's cq4 s0.3 rule 58 / 58 / 59%), 1 land 91% (cq4 s0.3 91.5%). The review's 58% and 87% are the
  network's judgement, not the search's starvation.
* **Where Q favours Mulligan the search follows it**: the 5 (k 4) to 7 (k 8) zero-land hands whose
  measured Q favours Mulligan are mulliganed by every rule and their cq target (s 1.0) goes 0.71 ->
  0.95 - but those hands' priors already favoured Mulligan (none was starved at k 0).
* **Iteration 29** (a copy; the same command): the same picture - 0 lands keep 58% at k 0 and 4, 1 land
  91%; 23 of 50 zero-land and 91 of 100 one-land hands starved at k 0; Mulligan's measured Q below
  Keep's in all of them but one (one-land; gaps -0.097 / -0.128).

### 64.4 Where the keeps come from: on the draw, and the opponent's view

Split by the declaration (the same rows, k 4):

| hands | declares | hands | value of the hand | Q Keep | Q Mulligan | keep ('visits' rule) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 lands | first (on the play) | 21 | 0.351 | 0.362 | 0.340 | **0%** |
| 0 lands | second (on the draw) | 29 | 0.406 | 0.483 | 0.400 | **100%** |
| 1 land | first | 51 | 0.484 | 0.509 | 0.352 | 82% |
| 1 land | second | 49 | 0.492 | 0.492 | 0.399 | 100% |

The 58% is not a coin: the starting player mulligans every 0-land hand, the player on the draw keeps
every one (and every 1-land hand). Two things show in the network's values after Keep (the value
head on the state after the keep, from the keeper's own view and from the view of the player to move
next, who cannot see the keeper's hand):

| hands | declares | keeper's P(win): before | after Keep, own view | after Keep, the next decider's view |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 lands | first | 0.351 | 0.356 | 0.509 |
| 0 lands | second | 0.406 | 0.469 | 0.475 |
| 1 land | first | 0.484 | 0.491 | 0.522 |
| 1 land | second | 0.492 | 0.604 | 0.480 |
| 2-4 lands | first | 0.529 | 0.539 | 0.521 |
| 2-4 lands | second | 0.493 | 0.611 | 0.478 |

* **The opponent's view is blind to the hand.** The search evaluates a leaf from its decider's view
  (zero-core's `encode(decider)`): after the starting player keeps a 0-lander, the next leaf is the
  other player's declaration, valued 0.509 for the keeper - a normal hand's value - against 0.356 from
  the keeper's own view. For the first declarer the search soon reaches its own turn (it plays first),
  so its Q Keep is right (0.36). For the second declarer the keep is followed by the opponent's whole
  first turn, all of it valued from the opponent's view, so at 64 simulations Q Keep is mostly what
  the opponent's view says.
* **The value head itself over-rates a landless keep on the draw**: from the keeper's own view 0.469
  after the keep (0.611 for a normal hand, 0.604 for one land), above its 0.40 for a mulligan to six.
  If kept 0-landers mostly lose, the outcomes should correct it, but this line's value target is 60%
  the search's own root value (`value_q` 0.6), which the opponent's-view leaves may keep up (not
  measured here: the outcomes of kept 0-landers in delver2's games would tell).

So the root minimum visits are not the fix for the mulligan: the floor gives Mulligan its Q and the
Q is low. The levers are the value of the post-keep positions (the outcomes' weight, `value_q`) and
the search's leaf view of the root player's private information (a zero-core design question: a
leaf valued from the root decider's view needs an encoding of a position from a non-deciding seat's
view, which the network was never trained on).

### 64.5 The floor on the other small decisions

`--small 300`: 300 decisions of 2-4 options (mana payments left out), one in six of those met in 48
games played by the network's sampled prior (219 priority decisions, 22 library searches, 18
mulligans, 13 targets, 8 play / draw, 5 yes / no, 5 attacks ...), each searched once per k:

| | iteration 21, k 4 | k 8 | iteration 29, k 4 | k 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| an option without a visit at k 0 | 62% | | 63% | |
| the cq target (s 0.3) moved by > 0.1 total variation | 10.7% | 10.0% | 13.3% | 12.0% |
| the cq4 s0.3 move changed | 2.7% | 3.0% | 3.7% | 4.0% |
| a forced option's measured Q above the most visited option's | 28% | 29% | 30% | 29% |
| forced walks per search (of 63) | 5.7 | 11.4 | 5.5 | 10.9 |

Of the decisions with more than one option met in those games (1,968, the games' early turns: the
sampling stopped at 300), 93% had 2-4 options and were not mana payments (4 were) - small roots are
most of this deck's decisions.

So in self-play the floor would change the training target materially at about one small decision in
nine or eight - the decisions where a starved option's Q is high enough to beat the log-prior gap -
and an evaluation's move at about one in thirty.

### 64.6 The A/B (flags; not run)

As round 2 and 63.6 (`runs/ab-r2/ab_driver.py`): fork the main line at its newest checkpoint K with
the floor on in self-play, run the fork then the control K -> K + 10 on the same build, h2h of the two
K + 10 checkpoints (600 games, both sides `--select cq --select-min-visits 4` at scale 0.3, no floor);
the fork wins at >= 0.5 + 2 se. The experiment entry for an `ab_config.json` (`requires`: the driver
waits for a build that has the flag):

```json
{"name": "rootmin4", "requires": "--selfplay-root-min-visits",
 "flags": ["--selfplay-root-min-visits", "4"],
 "set": ["selfplay_root_min_visits=4"]}
```

By hand (`$BASE` = round 2's `base_flags`, as in 63.6):

```
python tools/fork_run.py --source runs/delver2 --dest runs/r3-2-rootmin4 --iter K --set selfplay_root_min_visits=4
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/r3-2-rootmin4/supervisor_console.txt   python tools/supervise.py runs/r3-2-rootmin4 $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000 --selfplay-root-min-visits 4
# then the control: the same flags without the floor (as 63.6), and the h2h of the two K + 10 checkpoints
```

* **Only self-play changes.** `eval_root_min_visits` stays 0 on both arms: the same evaluation rule
  in the same pool (`cq-n4-v50-s0.3`), and `mtgz.az.h2h` follows a run's `eval_root_min_visits` only
  (0 here), so the head to head has no floor either. `root_min_visits_max_actions` 4 (the default):
  roots of 2-4 options. A league opponent's unrecorded seat (63) is the self-play seat and would take
  the floor too, if both experiments were ever combined.
* **The build**: a pinned run worktree of the merged main and its Mac checkout (`bash tools/mac.sh
  --eval-checkout`): remote self-play ships the fork's seat with the new keys, which an older checkout
  refuses. With the floor off the build searches as the main line's, byte for byte (64.7), so the
  control continues delver2 unchanged.
* **Throughput cost**: none in leaves per second or games per hour - no extra simulation, no extra
  network call. The cost is the budget the forced walks take from PUCT inside the full searches it
  applies to. Measured (64.5, fresh trees): 5.7 of a forced search's 63 walks with k 4 (11.4 with k
  8); 93% of the multi-option decisions are forceable (2-4 options); the full searches are the `p_full`
  0.25 share at 64 simulations against 16 for the fast ones, i.e. 16 of the 28 simulations a searched
  decision gets on average. So the floor takes ~8% (k 4; ~17% with k 8) of the full searches' walks
  from PUCT, **~4.7% of all self-play simulations with k 4, ~9.5% with k 8** - an upper bound: a
  reused root already holds visits, and a root where PUCT gives every option k visits pays nothing.
  The fast searches, which play three quarters of the moves, are untouched.
* **What to read**: the verdict; the mulligan keep rates of both arms' K + 10 (`tools/mull_floor.py
  --ks 0`, 64.3: expected unchanged, the value head drives them); `train.entropy` and the policy loss
  (the floor gives the cq target Q for starved options: its entropy should not fall faster than the
  control's); both arms against the heuristic. If k 4 shows nothing, k 8 is the variant (2 x 4 x 8 =
  64: still inside every 2-4 option root's budget). The expectation from 64.3-64.5: nothing for the
  mulligan, a target change at ~1 in 9 of the other small decisions - a small effect; the mulligan's
  levers are 64.4's.
