## 65. Murktide Regent's delve choices: a graveyard id is a position the network cannot see

Branch `delve-encoding` (main 0b476e0), 2026-10-29, CPU only, `runs/delver2` and an A/B round live
on the GPU and the Mac; every run directory only read. Tier "encoding-only" (the layout is
unchanged). 65.1-65.9: the finding and the encoding of a delve's picks (the branch's first part);
65.10-65.15: option A of 65.7, the user's choice (2026-10-29): graveyard choices and targets on the
list's ids (rebased on main 87ea619; tier "engine + decision-id change").

### 65.1 The finding

A gameplay review of the Delver mirror (2026-10-29): over 301 Murktide Regent casts in recorded
games, 150 exiled fewer instants and sorceries than the graveyard offered (0.84 counters lost per
resolved cast; 20 Regents came down as 3/3-4/4 with 5/5+ available). Example: replay
`runs/delver2/replays/20261029-080154_002.json.gz`, turn 8: P0's graveyard is Ponder, Daze, Mishra's
Bauble, Misty Rainforest, Lightning Bolt, Volcanic Island, Brainstorm, Polluted Delta (bottom first),
two Islands untapped, so five cards must be delved; the first pick offers ids 404-407 (positions
0-3) and the network takes 405 (Daze, prior 0.445; Ponder at 404 had 0.229): Ponder is passed for
good and the Regent gets 3 counters, not 4.

The network's priors at the Regent's delve decisions with two or more graveyard options, in the 96
recorded replays (`runs/delver2/replays`, six games each of iterations 0, 2, .., 30; `acts` / `p0`
of each frame, the option's text for its card), for iterations 16-30 (160 decisions, 961 options;
all 96 replays: 347 decisions, the same picture):

| | mean prior |
|---|---|
| an instant or sorcery card (39% of the options) | 0.154 |
| any other card (lands, the Baubles, creatures) | 0.174 |
| the lowest offered position | 0.396 |
| the second | 0.276 |
| the third, fourth, fifth, sixth | 0.140, 0.099, 0.087, 0.060 |

The prior's argmax is an instant or sorcery in 49 of the 133 decisions offering both kinds (37%,
against 39% of the options): the prior does not tell the cards apart and follows the position. The
13 Target decisions of Tamiyo, Seasoned Scholar's -3 (return an instant or sorcery card from the
graveyard, `GRAVEYARD` ids too) show the same: in the first, 0.57 on the lowest position (Ponder)
against 0.07 for Force of Will.

### 65.2 Hypothesis 1, the action mapping: right in the engine, invisible to the network

**The engine side is right.** A graveyard choice's id is `GRAVEYARD` + the card's position in its
owner's graveyard, bottom first, the decider's 0..63 and the other player's 64..127
(`Game::graveyard_action`, section 11). During a delve the positions are **stable**: the chosen
cards stay in the graveyard until the payment ends (`Mark::DelveExile`, 51.6), so nothing is
renumbered between picks; the picks go up the graveyard (each set once: the options are the
positions above the last pick that leave enough cards for the picks still needed). The option's
text ("Choose Ponder", the replay viewer's) and its identity come from the same `Choice::Card`.
Test `murktide_delve_maps_each_graveyard_id_to_its_card_and_encodes_the_picks` (`tests/az.rs`)
builds the replay's graveyard and asserts all of it at each of the five picks, for both players'
ids.

**The network side is the cause.** No segment of layout v5 scores a `GRAVEYARD` id: the token
network (zero-core `TokenNet`) gives a slot's actions pointer logits from that slot's token, and
every other action a **generic logit** of the pooled state (`gen(z)`, one weight row per action id;
22.2). The graveyard is in the input only as two bags of identities (counts, no order). So the
logit of id 404 + k is a learned per-position weight on a summary of the board: it can learn "the
lowest position" (the table above), never "the card at position k". Every graveyard choice is
made this way: delve, flashback and escape casts at priority, a graveyard card as a target (Tamiyo's
-3), Exhume-like choices, a graveyard cost. The public-state gate listed the graveyard's order as a
deliberate limit ("the order matters to a few cards only", 58.9); it is a gap: the order is what the
`GRAVEYARD` ids mean. `public_state::limits` now classifies "two graveyard cards swap places" as
`NextLayout`, and the gate asserts that it is the only gap (65.6; since 65.10 the gap is
Priority's `GRAVEYARD` ids only). The search sees the difference
only through its values (Q differences of 0.01-0.03 at 64 simulations), which is why it sometimes
finds the right card anyway.

### 65.3 Hypothesis 2, the picks so far: fixed in layout v5's floats

Before this branch a delve decision showed the count of cards chosen (the stack slot's v5 status
`stack::DELVED`, updated at every pick) but not which: the chosen cards were still in the graveyard
bag, and the context block had no card (`Task::Delve` was not among the tasks naming a stack item)
and no cost (its cost floats were a mana payment's only). Now, in floats that were zero there:

* **The committed picks by identity**: a graveyard card chosen for a delve in progress (a live
  `Mark::DelveExile`) is counted in its owner's exile bag, not the graveyard bag (both viewers;
  `encode_bags`). They are exiled when the payment ends (CR 601.2h, after the mana abilities of
  601.2g), so the bags show where they are going; the zone sizes in the globals stay the true ones.
* **The context's card**: the spell being cast (`frame_card` names `Task::Delve`'s stack item) - so
  the context token's identity is the Regent (the layout's context segment reads its identity there).
* **The cost left**: the context's nine cost floats (`ctx::COST`: generic / 8, pips / 4, as a mana
  payment's) hold the spell's total mana cost less one generic per card chosen
  (`total_mana(card, item).less_generic(item.delved)`, what `Game::delve` offers from); {5}{U}{U}
  with two picks is 3/8 and 2/4 blue.

The delve's floor (the positions already passed) is not in the input: no float per graveyard
position exists in layout v5 (65.7 adds one with the options; 65.10: the list holds the graveyard
in order, the passed cards present and not options). Gate: the new perturbation "a graveyard
card is chosen for delve" (`Game.marks`, a `DelveExile` mark on a random graveyard card) changes
both views and both encodings in all 233 positions it applies to.

### 65.4 Hypothesis 3, the option's text and the card's identity: consistent

The option text names `Game::name` of the option's card and the encoding's identity is that card's
definition (`objs[c].def`) - the same object (`Choice::Card(c)`), in every zone; a double-faced card
(Tamiyo) is named by its full name and encoded by its card's identity. Nothing to fix.

### 65.5 Hypothesis 4, the delve flow: no rules or flow bug

* **Order of picks**: one decision per card in increasing graveyard position (each set of cards
  once, 23.4); passing a card is final within the delve. Correct, but with blind priors it is what
  turns the position bias into lost counters (the first pick passes everything below it).
* **"Stop delving"** (`PASS`) is offered exactly when the rest of the cost can be paid with mana (the
  fewest more cards needed is 0) or nothing else is offered; never while more cards are needed.
* **Mana and delve**: delve's cards are chosen first and exiled after the mana abilities (51.6);
  delving more than needed to keep mana open is offered. Lotus Petal-style sources are `MY_PERM` ids
  (none in the mirror).
* The review's metric counts every Regent that exiled a land or an artifact while an instant was
  left; some of those keep delirium for Dragon's Rage Channeler (four card types) or an instant for
  Tamiyo's -3, so not all 150 are mistakes.
* `DIGEST_ENCODING=0` is unchanged (65.8): no game plays differently.

### 65.6 Tests

* `murktide_delve_maps_each_graveyard_id_to_its_card_and_encodes_the_picks` (`tests/az.rs`, new): the
  replay's graveyard, five picks (Ponder, Daze, Bolt, Brainstorm, Delta); at each pick, for both
  viewers: each option is `GRAVEYARD` + its card's position (the other player's id 64 higher), its
  text names the card, the graveyard unchanged while picking, exactly the positions above the last
  pick that leave enough cards; the context's card is the Regent and its cost floats the cost left;
  `stack::DELVED` = picks / 4; each chosen card in the owner's exile bag and out of the graveyard
  bag; the Regent enters with 4 counters. It also asserts the gap (no segment's actions reach
  404..531; it fails when 65.7 lands, to be updated then). Fails on main (no context card).
* `public_state_reaches_the_encoding`: the perturbation "a graveyard card is chosen for delve"
  (141 perturbations: 132 encoded, 3 deliberate limits, 1 gap - "two graveyard cards swap places",
  179 of 179 applications encode the same); the test asserts that this is the only gap.
* The encoding reads `total_mana` for a `Task::Delve` context only when the spell's alternative
  cost index exists (a state the gate perturbed by hand can have `alt` beyond the card's costs; the
  engine never makes one).

### 65.7 The options for the gap (an action-id or layout change: the user's decision)

(The user chose A on 2026-10-29: 65.10.)

None fits layout v5 with its action ids: a `GRAVEYARD` id needs a token to point from, and v5's
spare floats (8 per permanent and stack slot, some globals, the context's last 10) have no room
for a float per graveyard position, let alone a card code.

* **A. Graveyard choices on the list's ids (no layout change).** A `ChooseGraveyardCard` decision and
  a target in a graveyard offer `LIBRARY` + k, the list block holding the offered graveyard cards
  (graveyard order, or by definition with equal cards offered once, as a searched library: delve's
  sets by definition), with the list's floats for offered and chosen. The list's pointer column
  scores each card from its token. Layout v5 and every checkpoint stay valid (the guard passes); a
  running network re-pins directly (no widen, no fork); its list column (trained on searches, piles,
  seen hands, sideboarding) starts the scoring. Costs: section 11's table changes (`LIBRARY` gains a
  meaning, `GRAVEYARD` keeps priority's casts: flashback and escape stay blind, none in the mirror,
  since the list holds Bolas's Citadel's card there); the encoding-free digest changes (it hashes the
  ids); a target over both graveyards needs at most 64 offered cards (an assert, as 58.3's limits);
  engine tests that name `GRAVEYARD` ids change. The smallest and fastest fix.
* **B. Layout v6: `GRAVEYARD` pointer columns on the list segment.** The ids stay; the list segment
  gets the action pair `[404, 1]` and the list holds the decider's graveyard during graveyard
  choices. zero-core's widen refuses new action pairs (its az.md 10.3: a segment's actions must be
  the same), so a zero-core change (new pointer columns at zero), then 60.5's fork and widen of each
  run (iteration numbers, Elo pool and window restart). The opponent's graveyard (ids 468..531)
  needs a second pair or stays blind.
* **C. Layout v6: two graveyard segments.** 64 slots a side (card code + offered, chosen for delve,
  castable from there), always filled (public), actions `[404, 1]` / `[468, 1]`: every graveyard
  choice by card (priority's casts, both graveyards), and the order itself in the input. +7,168
  floats and up to +128 tokens (the network packs present tokens only: a Delver graveyard holds
  ~5-15 cards a side, against ~21 tokens a position now, so a large share more attention and
  feed-forward work); zero-core's widen must accept new segments (refused today) and new pointer
  columns; 60.5's fork. The most complete; it could ride along a network change already planned
  (section 62's distilled student is a new network: distilled on re-encoded rows it could be v6).

### 65.9 Runs

(The first part; with option A see 65.15.)

* **Re-pinning onto this branch**: the layout is v5 and every float keeps its offset, so a running
  network loads and resumes (the encoding guard passes; no widen, no fork). Its inputs differ at

  trained with zeros there, it starts from what it learned and adapts. The gain is small on its
  own: the choice itself stays blind until 65.7.
* **What remains a learning gap** after a 65.7 fix: the increasing-position enumeration makes the
  first pick decide the whole set (A's by-definition list softens it); delve decisions are few
  (~4 a game in the replays) and their value differences small (a +1/+1 counter); and the trade-offs
  (delirium's card types, Tamiyo's -3 targets, Regent counters later from instants leaving the
  graveyard) have to be learned from the value head.

### 65.10 Option A: graveyard choices and targets on the list's ids

Layout v5 is unchanged (37,620 floats, `mtgz/az/layout_v5.json` the same, the encoding guard passes):
what changes is the action ids of graveyard choices and the list block's contents while one is
pending.

* **Which decisions.** `ChooseGraveyardCard` (an effect's or a cost's choice of a graveyard card:
  delve; a graveyard exile cost, escape's or an ability's; Exhume's "each player"; "return a card
  from your graveyard" without targeting; an Aura entering attached to a graveyard card; "enter as a
  copy of a card in a graveyard"; "cast a card from your graveyard now"; a milled card taken), and
  `Target` and `NewTarget` (a target in a graveyard: Tamiyo, Seasoned Scholar's -3, Reanimate,
  Animate Dead, Lion Sash; a copy's new target). A graveyard
  card's option in them is `LIBRARY` + its slot in the decision's **graveyard list**
  (`Game::graveyard_list`). The other options keep their ids: `PASS`, `PLAYER`, permanents (delve's
  Lotus Petal), stack items, all below `LIBRARY`, so the renaming keeps the order of every
  decision's options.
* **The list.** Offered cards in one graveyard: that graveyard whole, in order (bottom first), so
  the cards passed, chosen and still to come of a set picked in increasing position are all in it
  (delve's floor: the passed cards present, not options). A player's graveyard holds at most 64
  cards (the deck limit, 58.3): it always fits. Offered cards in both graveyards (Reanimate, Lion
  Sash): the offered cards only, the decider's graveyard's first, each graveyard in order. The
  list is public and deterministic (the same in every world `determinize` makes; a refreshed
  decision of the other player gets the same ids). The list block holds it for the decider only,
  as every list (the viewer's own decision): slot k is `LIBRARY` + k, the list segment's pointer
  action (`[340, 1]`), so the network scores each graveyard option from its card's token.
* **The list's floats.** The card code (identity and descriptor, as in the bags), `list::PRESENT`,
  `list::OPTION` (its id is an option now), `list::COPIES` (copies of its definition in the list /
  4), and two in the floats a sideboarding pool list uses for `IN_DECK` and `AT_START` (a list is
  one or the other): `list::THEIRS` (in the opponent's graveyard) and `list::CHOSEN` (chosen for
  the delve in progress, `Mark::DelveExile`; also counted in its owner's exile bag, 65.3).
* **Naming a card.** The choice is the card itself (`Choice::Card`, `Choice::Target`), as before:
  graveyards are public, and section 10's rule (a choice of a hidden card names its definition) is
  for hidden zones. Equal cards are not merged: each keeps its own option and slot, so the
  decisions offer exactly what they offered.
* **The limit** (class B, docs/shortcuts.md 65.10). At most 64 graveyard cards offered at once
  from both graveyards; more is a loud failure (an assert in `Game::ask` naming the counts), never
  an id beyond the list or a card left out. Only an "any card in a graveyard" target reaches it,
  with more than 64 cards in the two graveyards together (two 40-card decks hold 80): the default
  fuzz's most is 57 cards offered (Lion Sash, 5,000 games; the same in 20,000 games and 52,013
  graveyard-list decisions, the Mac). The Delver mirror has no choice over both graveyards (its
  longest list: 46 cards of one graveyard, 20,000 games and 58,446 decisions). Whole graveyards for
  both (this branch's first try) gave the same 57 for Lion Sash and longer lists for every other
  choice over both: the offered cards are the shortest list with one id per option.
* **What stays on `GRAVEYARD` ids.** Priority's casts and plays from the graveyard (flashback,
  escape, retrace, mayhem, Yawgmoth's Will, Lurrus, Serra Paragon, lands with Crucible
  of Worlds): `GRAVEYARD` + the card's position in the decider's graveyard (the opponent's range
  468..531 is now unused), still a generic logit of the pooled state, blind as before (65.2). None
  is in the Delver mirror. `GY_ABILITY` (a graveyard card's ability: its own segment) is
  unchanged. `Game::name_graveyard_options` asserts that no other decision offers a `GRAVEYARD`
  id, and that a graveyard card's option arrives with its `GRAVEYARD` id (every asker builds it so).
* **The gate.** "Two graveyard cards swap places" stays the one `NextLayout` gap, now for
  Priority's ids: 178 of its 179 applications encode the same for each viewer (the others: a
  graveyard choice pending for the viewer, whose list shows the order). Option C (65.7, a layout
  change) closes it.
* **Code.** `Game::graveyard_list` and `Game::name_graveyard_options` (`decision.rs`), called by
  `Game::ask` before it sorts the options; the list block (`encode.rs`); `list::THEIRS`,
  `list::CHOSEN`.

### 65.11 The proof: the same games, only the ids renamed

The encoding-free digest hashes the ids, so it changes: 5f0579aa50453818 -> **c62a5ce5f290814e**.
A new digest mode, `DIGEST_IDS=choices` (`tests/digest.rs`), hashes the same 2,500 games id-free: every
action id (the legal ones and the one taken, in the game and in the determinized clones) as the
choice it names (`Game::describe_choice`: the card by name and index, the target, the number), a
`KEY_AUTO` chance key without its action (its decision kind and player kept), no encodings. The
default mode is unchanged (main's engine with this branch's digest test: 5f0579aa50453818). On
this branch's head (main 87ea619), the desktop:

| engine | `DIGEST_ENCODING=0` | `DIGEST_IDS=choices` |
|---|---|---|
| main 87ea619's (this branch's `tests/digest.rs`) | 5f0579aa50453818 (main's) | 4c1b03a561402745 |

With the renaming off, every id, chance key and decision of the 2,500 games is main's bit for bit:
nothing else in the branch plays differently. With it on, the games take the same choices among the

The fuzzer now checks, at every decision, that every `LIBRARY` option points at a list token of the

* `ChooseDiscard` with a permanent among its options ("exile a nonland card from their hand or the
  chosen creature", Cloak and Dagger, `ExileHandCardOrTargetUntil`): the list's hand was the owner's

* Bolas's Citadel's top card with two faces to cast or play (`Choice::Faces`, `CastFace`,
  `PlayFace` at `LIBRARY` + 0) had no list token. Now it has.

### 65.15 Runs: re-pinning, and what the policy head must relearn

* **Re-pinning is direct.** The layout is v5 and every float keeps its offset: a running network
  (delver2, the A/B round's arms) loads (the encoding guard passes) and resumes; no widen, no fork,
  no new iteration numbering. The change is an engine and decision-id change (its gates are 65.14),
  so a run moves to it once it is on main.
* **What the policy must relearn.** Only the graveyard choices' logits move. Their old ids
  (404..531) were generic logits of the pooled state (one weight row per id: the per-position bias
  of 65.1); in the Delver mirror those decisions are delve's picks (~4 a game) and Tamiyo's -3
  targets. Now they are the list segment's pointer logits from the cards' tokens. That column was
  trained on the other lists (the Delver networks: their fetch lands' searches and Ponder's pile;
  the cube's: searches, piles, seen hands), so at first it scores graveyard cards with what it
  learned there, not with the old position bias, and the visit targets of these decisions then
  train it on graveyard choices. The generic rows of 404..531 are no longer read by them (Priority's
  casts still read 404..467). The value head is untouched, so the search's Q values still find the
  better card where they see a difference (65.2). `list::THEIRS` and `list::CHOSEN` are new inputs
  of the list's token map (for the Delver networks those weights never met a non-zero input: a small
  random term until trained).
* **Still a learning problem** (65.9): the first pick of a delve decides the set; the value
  differences are small (a +1/+1 counter); delirium and Tamiyo's -3 trade-offs come from the value
  head. A gameplay review after some iterations should compare the counters lost per Regent (0.84
  before) and the share of instants delved.
* **Cube runs** (mtg5, td1, paused): the same re-pin; their games have choices over both
  graveyards (Reanimate, Lion Sash), whose lists are the offered cards. The 64 limit is a loud
  failure: a Lion Sash with more than 64 cards in the two graveyards stops the worker (watch_run
  sees it). The fuzz's most is 57 in 20,000 random games (65.10), so it is reachable in a long
  milling game; if it happens, the class-B alternative is 58.4's (offer the first 64), a rules
  departure the user would have to accept.

## 66. A belief head: the opponent's hand from public information (stage 1; zero-core auxiliary targets)

Branch `belief` (on main 590e7fe): zero-core pinned at **a560448** (feat/belief-head on main b486d36: 1549668 the
feature, 5dbe2ba + 2cb150d two small fixes, the rest docs;
auxiliary training targets, its docs/az.md 15 and search.md 1.2), the engine's target (`MtgAz::AUX`,
`aux_target`), `mtgz/az/belief.py` (names, the replay field, the baselines' public facts), the package's
declaration (`aux`, `replay_aux`), `tools/belief_eval.py`, tests, this section. With the new setting at
its default (0) a run is the run of before, byte for byte (66.9).

### 66.1 Why

Players never see hidden information (section 10: observer masking; `determinize(viewer)` deals the
viewer's unknown cards uniformly over the consistent assignments). But a strong player infers: "they
left blue open and passed: likely Daze or Force of Will". The question is whether the Delver network's
trunk already carries that inference, and whether training it explicitly helps. Stage 1 (this section)
builds an auxiliary head that predicts the opponent's hand from public information, trained against the
true hand (which the simulator knows: a label, never an input), measures it on CPU against the
uniform prior the search uses today, and gives the A/B flags (66.7). Stage 2 (66.8, designed here,
built in section 69) deals the search's worlds from the head's prediction instead of uniformly.

### 66.2 The target: the opponent's true hand, by identity

`MtgAz::aux_target(viewer, out)` (the zero-core auxiliary target `belief`): for every card in the hand
of the decider's opponent, +1 at its identity (`identity::D` = 1,024 columns: the encoding's identity
space, 22.2 - the cube's 546 cards, the legacy registry's from 546, the tokens' from 768). The TRUE hand
(`self.g.player(1 - viewer).hand`), so it differs between the worlds `determinize` deals for the
decider while the decider's encoding does not (tested: 66.9). Empty while sideboarding (no hand
between a match's games) and before the deal. Why the identity space and not a compact per-game set
(the Delver list's 21 distinct cards):

* **A fixed width.** zero-core's targets have one width per game (`SearchGame::AUX`), and `mtg` plays
  the cube's random decks, best-of-three pools, drafted decks and constructed lists with one encoding: a
  per-deck column set would change with the spec. The identities are the same in every spec and every
  layout since v2 (stable by construction, 22.2).
* **The encoding's own vocabulary.** The bags count cards by these identities (`OPP_HIDDEN`, the
  opponent's unseen cards; `OPP_HAND_KNOWN`; `OPP_HAND_CLOUD`), so column k of the head and identity k
  of the input are the same card, and the baselines (66.6) read the hidden pool by the same index.
* **Cheap.** 1,024 float16 a sample (+2.7% of a Delver row; mostly zeros: the Mac's compressed shards
  barely grow), a 128 x 1,024 last layer. The head learns to put ~0 on identities that never occur (a
  deck's 21 cards dominate after a few hundred steps).

### 66.3 The loss: a multinomial over identities

The head's 1,024 outputs are a softmax p over identities and the loss is the cross-entropy against the
hand's composition, -sum_k (t_k / n) log p_k (n = the hand size, t the counts): zero-core's
'multinomial' loss (az.md 15.2). Why this and not a per-identity expected count with Poisson or MSE:

* **The hand size is public** (the globals encode it), so the only unknown is the composition: the
  multinomial spends no capacity on n and its prediction is consistent by construction - n x p sums to
  the hand size exactly. A Poisson or MSE head must also learn n per position and its counts need not add
  up.
* **A proper scoring rule over "a card of their hand"**: the cross-entropy is minimised by the true
  conditional distribution of a random card of the hand given the public state, which is exactly the
  "what do they hold" a reader wants, and the per-card log-loss is comparable across positions and with
  the baselines (each is a distribution too).
* **Stage 2 needs urn weights.** The weighted deal (66.8) draws the hand's unknown cards one at a time
  from the pool with per-identity weights: a distribution over identities is that, directly.
* What it does not model: correlations between the hand's cards (two Force of Will vs one) beyond the
  marginal - the expected count n p_k is right, the joint is the urn's. Fine for a prior.

### 66.4 The head and the carry-over (zero-core az.md 15.2, 15.4)

zero-core's auxiliary head: one MLP from the token network's pooled state z (the global token's output
and the tokens' mean, 2 x 128 floats - where the value head reads) to 128 to 1,024, built after every
other parameter, its last layer zero (the first prediction is uniform over the 1,024 identities). The
search never computes it (only `forward(..., aux=True)`: training, `NetEvaluator.aux`). Run setting
`aux_belief_w` (default 0 = off: nothing recorded, built or trained). With it on, self-play records the
target with every sample (shard key `aux`, on the Mac too), a new run's first network has the head, and
a checkpoint without one - delver2's - gets a fresh head at the run's first training with every other
weight exactly its own (its policy, value and margin outputs unchanged; the AdamW moments of the trunk
kept): `tools/fork_run.py --source runs/delver2 --dest <fork> --iter K --set aux_belief_w=0.25` is the
whole carry-over. The encoding guard (61) accepts the checkpoints with the head (the head reads no
input). `net.add_aux` does the same by hand (66.6's head-only checkpoint).

### 66.5 Recording and replays: the `belief` field

`python -m mtgz.az.replays <checkpoint with the head>` (and zero-core's `zero.replay`) adds to every
network decision's frame the head's belief for the decider - one forward pass of the root's features
after its search (the search's evaluations never compute the head; a reused tree's root was evaluated in
an earlier search, so the root's own pass is the one every decision has; `mtgz.az.belief.render`):

```json
"belief": {"for": 1, "n": 5, "cards": [["Force of Will", 1.482], ["Daze", 0.913], ["Island", 0.402], ...]}
```

`for` = the seat whose hand is predicted (the decider's opponent), `n` = that seat's hand size in the
frame's state, `cards` = the 12 largest expected counts (the head's distribution x n), largest first,
rounded to 3 places, card names as the spectator view writes them in a hand (tested against
`export_state`); they sum to about n (the 1,012 others hold the rest). The seat lists `aux: ["belief"]`.
A checkpoint without the head: no field (the frames of before). The delverai site renders it as "what I
think they hold".

### 66.6 Evidence on CPU: what delver2's trunk already reads

All on the desktop's CPU (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`, below normal; round 2 of the A/B live on the GPU and
the Mac), from a copy of **delver2's iteration 41** (the newest when copied; sha256 ab0827e4...) in
scratch run directories under `E:\mtg-zero-scratch\belief` (`runs/` only read). The shards were made
for this (delver2's have no target): this branch's self-play with `aux_belief_w` on, the Delver spec,
iteration 41's network, **32 simulations at every decision, every decision recorded** (`--sims 32
--p-full 1`: four times delver2's samples per game for a similar budget per game; the run's `temp_moves`
60, cq targets at scale 0.3), CPU inference, 1,270-2,100 leaves/s.

* **Train**: 600 games (seeds 11, 13, 14; three runs of 200), 147,762 decisions, 139,071 with a
  non-empty opponent hand (mean 3.7 cards). The head fits on the first 80% of the shards (~480 games)
  and stops early on the other 20% (another ~120 games: a shard holds whole games but at its edges).
* **Held out**: 80 other games (seed 12), 21,063 decisions, 19,994 with a hand; 13.7% of them have a
  card of that hand known to the decider (a Daze returned an Island, a revealed card), 0.7% a cloud.
* **The models** (`tools/belief_eval.py`, its docstring): *uniform* = today's determinize from the
  features (the known hand cards + the rest uniform over the hidden-pool bag); *count-matching* = the
  uniform prior with one weight per identity fitted on the train rows so the mean counts match (what a
  static per-card bias explains: Force of Will 1.74, Unholy Heat 1.47, Murktide 1.36, Daze 1.27 ...
  Brainstorm 0.60, Urza's Bauble 0.33, Mishra's Bauble 0.28 - cantrips and Baubles leave the hand,
  counterspells and finishers wait); *head-only* = zero-core's head (z -> 128 -> 1,024) on iteration
  41's FROZEN trunk, AdamW 1e-3, wd 0.01, early-stopped (epoch 2); *residual* = count-matching's logits
  + a fresh head on the frozen trunk (it starts at count-matching: what z adds to the static bias);
  *joint (run loop)* = scratch run `sp`'s iteration 1: the run loop's own training, the head added to
  iteration 41 at its first step (the carry-over), 199 steps at the run's lr 1e-4 on 200 of the games;
  *joint (fine-tune)* = the head-only network trained further by zero-core's training step (the trunk
  too, policy + value + margin + belief, weight 1) for 400 steps at lr 1e-4 on all 600 train games.

Held-out, per decision with a hand (cross-entropy per card in nats, lower is better; count error = 0.5
sum_k |n p_k - t_k|, the cards misplaced; top-1 = the most likely card is in the hand):

| model | cross-entropy | count error | top-1 | AUC holds Force of Will | AUC Daze | AUC Bolt | AUC Murktide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform (today's deal) | 2.807 +- 0.003 | 2.843 | 0.400 | 0.661 | 0.751 | 0.754 | 0.724 |
| count-matching | 2.705 +- 0.003 | 2.750 | 0.552 | 0.661 | 0.752 | 0.753 | 0.725 |
| head-only, frozen trunk | **2.599** +- 0.004 | 2.665 | 0.500 | 0.695 | 0.770 | 0.788 | 0.792 |
| residual, frozen trunk | 2.441 +- 0.005 | 2.454 | 0.605 | 0.745 | 0.808 | 0.808 | 0.816 |
| joint, the run loop's first iteration | 2.865 +- 0.003 | 2.968 | 0.428 | 0.597 | 0.684 | 0.739 | 0.707 |
| joint fine-tune, its own head (400 steps, weight 1) | 2.375 +- 0.005 | 2.437 | 0.638 | 0.802 | 0.823 | 0.832 | 0.822 |
| head-only refit on that fine-tuned trunk | 2.283 +- 0.005 | 2.317 | 0.678 | 0.822 | 0.834 | 0.849 | 0.836 |
| residual on that fine-tuned trunk | **2.200** +- 0.006 | **2.188** | **0.722** | **0.837** | **0.849** | **0.853** | **0.860** |
| control fine-tune (the same 400 steps, weight 0): head-only refit | 2.542 +- 0.004 | 2.597 | 0.526 | 0.716 | 0.785 | 0.793 | 0.805 |
| control fine-tune: residual | 2.402 +- 0.005 | 2.404 | 0.622 | 0.757 | 0.811 | 0.805 | 0.835 |

(+- = the standard error over rows; rows of one game are correlated, so the honest error is larger:
the 80 held-out games' spread. With only the first 200 train games the head-only fit stopped at 2.787
and the residual at 2.624: both gain with data, the head-only more.)

**Read**: the frozen trunk carries real information about the opponent's hand beyond what a static
per-card bias explains - the residual head takes 0.26 nats per card off count-matching's 2.71 (0.37 off
today's uniform deal), misplaces 0.30 fewer cards of a 3.7-card hand, and ranks the hands that hold a
Force of Will at AUC 0.75 against 0.66. The plain head (zero-core's shape, trained from zero) gets
there more slowly - with 480 games it beats count-matching by 0.11 nats and overfits after two epochs (a
game's ~250 decisions share one hand: the trunk's z identifies the game) - so in a run, with thousands
of games in a window, it should close on the residual; and a joint fine-tune shows the auxiliary loss itself shaping the trunk: 400 steps of zero-core's
training step with the belief loss (weight 1) on the 600 games leave a trunk from which a fresh head
reads 2.283 nats (from 2.599 frozen), against 2.542 after the same 400 steps without the loss (the
control: same rows, seed and steps) - 0.26 nats per card of representation the loss bought, the
jointly trained head itself at 2.375. Its price on the same held-out positions (the run loop's losses,
value_q 0.6): policy 0.3739 against the control's 0.3656, value 0.3553 against 0.3516 (iteration 41
before either: 0.3663 / 0.3913) - small at weight 1, hence 66.7's 0.25. The run loop's own first

### 66.7 The A/B of stage 1 (flags; not run)

Stage 1 changes the search in nothing: the head is trained, never read by self-play or the evaluations.
Whatever it brings comes through **representation learning** - its gradient shapes the trunk the policy
and value heads share (as KataGo's ownership target did for Go). So the A/B asks whether the main line
trains better with the auxiliary loss, at equal iterations, as round 2 asks it of its settings
(`runs/ab-r2/ab_driver.py`): fork delver2 at its newest checkpoint K with the target on, run the fork
then the control K -> K + 10 on the same build, h2h of the two K + 10 checkpoints (600 games, both
sides `--select cq --select-min-visits 4` at scale 0.3); the fork wins at >= 0.5 + 2 se.

* **The weight**: 0.25. The multinomial loss starts at the zero head's ln 1024 = 6.93 and reaches
  ~2.2-2.6 nats per card on held-out positions (66.6; lower on the window) against the policy loss's
  ~0.37 and the value loss's ~0.39 (delver2's iteration 41): 0.25 keeps the auxiliary term at ~0.6, of
  the order of the other two. At weight 1, 400 steps cost +0.008 nats of held-out policy loss and +0.004
  of value loss against the same fine-tune without it while the trunk gained 0.26 nats of belief
  (66.6): small, but the A/B's question is the policy, so a quarter of that. 0.1 and 1.0 are the
  follow-ups if 0.25 shows something (a dose response).
* **The carry-over**: `fork_run --set aux_belief_w=0.25` makes the fork's config ask for the target;
  its first self-play records it (from checkpoint K: the head is not needed to record), its first
  training adds a fresh head to K (zero-core az.md 15.4: every other weight exactly K's, the AdamW
  moments of the trunk kept) and trains on a window whose delver2 shards have no target (masked: they
  still train the policy and value as before). The window turns over in 6 iterations, so the share of
  rows with a target grows 1/6 -> 1 over the first half of the arm (`train.aux.share`).
* **The build**: a pinned run worktree of the merged main and its Mac checkout (`bash tools/mac.sh
  --eval-checkout`): the Mac self-plays a share of every iteration, and its workers must record the
  target (an older checkout's shards come back without it: accepted, logged, masked - zero-core az.md
  15.2). With the target off the build plays and trains as the main line's, byte for byte (66.9), so
  the control continues delver2 unchanged.
* **Costs**: no extra simulation or network call in self-play (the target is read from the game when a
  decision is recorded: one pass over the opponent's hand); training: the head's forward and backward
  (256 x 128 + 128 x 1024 multiply-adds a row against the trunk's ~5 M: < 1%); shards +2 KB a row
  uncompressed (+2.7% of a Delver row; the Mac's compressed shards: sparse, nearly nothing); the
  window +2 KB a row in RAM (delver2's 265k rows: +0.54 GB of 20 GB).
* **What to read**: the verdict; `train.aux_belief` and `train.aux_belief_hit` per iteration (the
  head learning; compare with 66.6's head-only numbers on the same positions); the policy and value
  losses and `train.entropy` against the control's (the auxiliary gradient must not degrade them);
  both arms against the heuristic. A null result is informative too: 66.6 says how much of the hand
  the trunk already reads without the loss.

The experiment entry for an `ab_config.json` (round 2's driver: `requires` waits for a build that has
the flag, `set` goes to fork_run, `flags` to the fork's supervisor):

```json
{"name": "belief025", "requires": "--aux-belief-w", "flags": ["--aux-belief-w", "0.25"],
 "set": ["aux_belief_w=0.25"]}
```

By hand (K = delver2's newest checkpoint after a STOP; `$BASE` = round 2's `base_flags`, 63.6):

```
python tools/fork_run.py --source runs/delver2 --dest runs/r3-1-belief025 --iter K --set aux_belief_w=0.25
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/r3-1-belief025/supervisor_console.txt \
  python tools/supervise.py runs/r3-1-belief025 $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000 --aux-belief-w 0.25
# when it has iteration K+10: the control, the same flags without the target
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/delver2/supervisor_console.txt \
  python tools/supervise.py runs/delver2 $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000
N=$(printf %04d $((K+10)))
python -m mtgz.az.h2h runs/r3-1-belief025/models/iter_$N.pt runs/delver2/models/iter_$N.pt \
  --games 600 --sims 32 --spec "$(python -c "import json; print(json.load(open('runs/delver2/config.json'))['spec'])")" \
  --device cuda --threads 8 --seed 7 --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3 --b-cq-c-scale 0.3
```

The fork's K + 10 has the head (its h2h and evaluations never compute it: the same search as a
network without one); its replays show the belief (66.5).

### 66.8 Stage 2: belief-weighted determinization (the design; built: section 69)

(Built as designed, with the departures 69.1 lists: one dedicated `ROW_BELIEF` row per search instead of an
`aux_rows` mask, a checkpoint without the head refused rather than dealt uniformly, a payment's pinned cards
counted among the unknown hand slots, no fixed-point refinement. The CPU evidence and the A/B: 69.5-69.9.)

**The idea.** Today every simulation of a search deals the opponent's unseen cards uniformly
(`Game::determinize`, section 10): every consistent assignment equally likely, Force of Will as likely
in a hand that passed with UU open as in one that tapped out for a threat. Stage 2 deals them from the
belief: at the root of each decision, one forward pass gives the head's distribution over the
opponent's hand, and every simulation of that search samples a world from it instead - so the tree's
statistics are averaged over the worlds the network finds likely.

**From the head to weights.** The head gives p_k (a random card of the hand is identity k), so
e_k = n p_k is the expected count (n = the hand size, public). Today's deal has expected count
u_k = known_k + m h_k / H (known_k: the hand cards the decider knows; m = n - sum known: the hand's
unknown cards; h_k: the identities of the opponent's cards it has not seen, the hidden pool, H their
total). The weighted deal tilts the unknown part by one weight per identity,
w_k = clip(((e_k - known_k)^+ / max(u_k - known_k, eps))^alpha, 1/R, R): alpha the tilt (0 = today's
deal; a seat setting), R the clip (e.g. 20: no card is ever ruled out or forced). A world's
probability becomes the uniform one times the product of w over the unknown cards dealt into the hand
(Fisher's multivariate noncentral hypergeometric, restricted to the consistent assignments).

**The deal, exactly as `Game::determinize` but weighted.** Everything that pins a card stays:
* the cards the decider knows exactly stay where they are (hand, library positions); the pinned mana
  sources of a payment in progress stay; public zones are untouched;
* each cloud (section 10: a Brainstorm put-back, mulligan bottoms, a look at the top, a search, a
  shuffle) first places its identities inside its domain - uniformly as today, or with the same
  weights for the cloud's hand-or-library choice (its hand slots weighted by w, its library slots not);
* the hand's remaining unknown slots (m minus the cloud cards dealt into the hand) are filled by
  **sequential weighted sampling without replacement** from the remaining pool: each draw takes
  identity k with probability proportional to w_k x (copies of k left); the hand size is exact by
  construction, and an identity the pool lacks is never drawn;
* the pool's rest goes to the library's unknown slots and the face-down cards the decider doesn't
  know, uniformly ordered (`rng.shuffle`, as today; the library order has no belief);
* best-of-three's hidden pool (36.11: `sample_hidden_pool`) is sampled first as today, the weights then
  apply to the hand of the deck it sampled (identities outside it simply have no copies).
Sequential sampling gives Wallenius' distribution, not Fisher's: the two agree to first order in the
weights' spread and the sampler is exact in hand size, cheap (n draws over <= 25 identities: well under
a microsecond against ~15 us for today's deal) and needs no rejection. If the difference ever matters,
a short Metropolis chain (swap an unknown hand card with an unknown library card, accept with
min(1, w_new / w_old)) after the uniform deal samples Fisher's exactly with every constraint kept (the
swaps never touch a pinned, known or cloud-bound card). The weights are fitted to the head by moment
matching only approximately (the ratio above); a few fixed-point steps on the Wallenius means would
make the deal's expected counts equal e_k exactly - measure first whether it matters.

**Where the root's belief comes from.** One forward pass at the root per decision: the root's features
are the decider's view, the same in every world (the encoding is blind to hidden cards), so one belief
serves the whole search. Mechanics in the Rust driver: when a decision starts (`start`), a slot whose
seat has the tilt on asks the evaluator for the root's auxiliary output - the root's own expansion row
when the root is fresh (its pass computes the head for that row), else one extra row in the next batch
of that key (a reused root was expanded during the previous search, as an inner node, and nodes keep no
head output); the slot's simulations wait for it (one batch round trip; its other games go on). Minor
decisions (mana payments) and fast searches may skip it (a seat option; default: full searches only).
Cost: <= 1 extra row per searched decision - +1.6% of the leaves at 64 simulations, +6% at 16 - and
the head (< 1% of the pass).

**The zero-core hook.** Additive, default off:
* `SearchGame::determinize_with(&mut self, viewer, rng, belief: &[f32])` - default `determinize(viewer,
  rng)` (a game without it ignores the belief): the tree calls it instead of `determinize` in
  `simulate_with` (and `set_base` without redet) when it holds a belief.
* `Tree::set_belief(Option<Vec<f32>>)` (the search keeps the root's prediction for its decision; `None`
  = today's search bit for bit).
* The leaf-batch protocol: a network batch may flag rows whose auxiliary output is wanted (`aux_rows`),
  `submit(id, priors, value, margin, aux=None)` returns it for those rows (`NetEvaluator.evaluate(...,
  aux_rows)`: the head on those rows only). Seat keys `belief_tilt` (alpha; 0 = off), `belief_clip`
  (R), `belief_mix` (the share of simulations dealt uniformly, a safety net), `belief_fast` (fast and
  minor searches too). The game's package maps the head's output to the weights (MTG Zero: the formula
  above in the engine, `MtgAz::determinize_with`, reading the decider's known cards and hidden pool from
  the game, never from the network).
* The other agent's root-view values (ENGINE.md 67, zero-core `feat/root-view-values`) touch the same
  batching interface (a second, value-only pass from the non-mover's view): both are flagged extra rows
  in the leaf batch, so they should share one mechanism - whichever lands second adds its flag to the
  other's.

**Risks.**
* **Overconfidence.** The search can only explore worlds it deals: a hand the belief puts at 0.01 is
  nearly never searched, so a sharp but wrong head makes the search blind to the punish (the opponent
  who does have Force of Will). Mitigations: the clip R (no world rarer than 1/R of today's odds per
  card), the tilt alpha < 1, the uniform share `belief_mix` (e.g. 0.25 of the simulations dealt as
  today), and the head's calibration measured per card (66.6's AUCs and predicted-vs-actual counts; a
  reliability table per iteration).
* **A feedback loop in self-play.** The head learns how this policy plays its hands; a search that
  believes it exploits this policy's tells; the policy, trained on those searches, learns to hide them;
  the head lags a window behind. That can cycle or drift into a mirror-specific equilibrium that a real
  opponent breaks. Mitigations: the league (63) and the heuristic in evaluation (fixed opponents the
  belief was not trained on), the head's loss per iteration (a sudden rise = the policy moved), alpha
  kept moderate, and turning the tilt on in evaluation first (no feedback) before self-play.
* **Cost.** The extra row and the head (above); the weighted deal is cheaper than the shuffle it
  replaces. Training is unchanged from stage 1.
* **Correctness.** The deal must keep every invariant the fuzz checks (section 10's checks: the
  decider's legal actions and observable view, known cards in place, clouds held, every card of the
  owner's pool exactly once), with a belief or without; `None` must be today's deal bit for bit (the
  digests and zero-core's golden records unchanged with the tilt at 0).

**Tests.** The deal: invariants on the fuzz positions with random beliefs (legal actions, `view_of`,
known cards, clouds, the pool's multiset, hand size); weights all 1 -> the uniform deal's distribution
(a chi-square over 100k deals of a fixed position, against `determinize`'s); a tilt -> the
Wallenius expectation on small analytic cases (a pool of 3 identities, a hand of 2); a clip honoured
(the share of worlds with a down-weighted card >= its uniform share / R); best-of-three's hidden pool
first. The driver: tilt 0 = the golden records; the belief row's cost counted; the root belief equal to
`NetEvaluator.aux` of the root's features. The fuzz: `determinize_with` at every check point with a
random belief.

**The A/B.** Two questions, cheapest first.
1. **Does the belief help the search at all?** No training: the same checkpoint (one with a trained
   head: the stage 1 fork's, or 66.6's head-only fit) against itself, one side dealing by the belief,
   600 games of the Delver h2h; then alpha 0.5 / 1 and the mix 0 / 0.25. A positive score here is
   worth a self-play run; a null one says the search's averaging washes the belief out (or the head is
   too flat: 66.6's gains over count-matching bound what it can do).
2. **Does self-play with it learn faster?** A fork of the main line with the tilt in self-play (and
   in evaluation), against the control, 10 iterations, h2h at the same move rule with each side's own
   dealing - and both against the heuristic and older checkpoints (the feedback loop's tell is a fork
   that beats its control but loses ground against fixed opponents).

### 66.10 Limits, open questions, conflict points

* **The head's input is the pooled state only.** A belief per card would read better from the tokens
  (attention from a query per identity, or the identity embeddings as the output layer); the MLP on z
  is zero-core's generic head. The residual over count-matching (66.6) suggests the cheapest gain: give
  the head the uniform prior (the hidden-pool bag is in the features) as a base. Not built: measure the
  plain head in a run first.
* **Self-play data at 32 simulations, every decision recorded** (66.6): the evidence's positions are
  denser than a run's (p_full 0.25 at 64 / 16); the head-only fits overfit by game in two epochs, so
  the numbers are a lower bound on what a run's window (thousands of games) gives.
* **The joint fine-tune trained on the train games' hands**; the held-out games are clean, the refits'
  early stopping is not (the trunk saw those games): their epoch choice, not their held-out score.
* **Conflict points.** zero-core: the other session's `feat/root-view-values` (MTG Zero's ENGINE.md
  67) extends the evaluator / leaf-batch interface; this branch only ADDS `NetEvaluator.aux` and the
  tolerant `set_weights` (no change to `evaluate`, `launch`, `result`, the protocol), `DriverCfg::aux`
  (a new field: every struct literal of `DriverCfg` gains it - this repo's `draft_deferred.rs`),
  `Record::aux`, `DynGame::aux_target`, `GameInfo::aux`, the `SearchDriver(aux=)` keyword, `Run.driver`'s
  kwargs, `train_model`'s optimizer and loss block, `Window(aux_width=)`, and az.md section 15 (the root
  view agent may number its section 15 too). Stage 2's protocol change (`aux_rows` in a batch) is
  where the two meet: one flagged-rows mechanism for both (66.8). This repo: `engine/src/az/mod.rs`'s
  `SearchGame` impl (two items appended), `mtgz/az/__init__.py`'s `GamePackage(...)` call (two keys),
  tests appended at the end of `engine/tests/az.rs`; ENGINE.md 66 between 65 and the root-view agent's 67.

## 67. Root-view leaf values (zero-core `leaf_value_view`, value-only samples)

Branch `root-view-values` (from main 87ea619, rebased onto 0f98448): zero-core pinned at
**2c04cd9** (feat/root-view-values on zero-core main a560448: the root-view values 450d267, the
recording driver 1078e02, zero.h2h's per-side view 052ea00, the flagged extra rows e5873bb, docs
2c04cd9: zero-core docs/search.md 3.6, az.md 16); this repo: the non-deciding viewer's leak
checks, two `#[doc(hidden)]` engine helpers for them, `tools/root_view.py` (the CPU evidence), this
section. With the settings off a run is the run of before, byte for byte (67.9).

### 67.1 Why

The search determinizes hidden cards from the root player's view (section 10) and, before this,
valued every leaf with the network on `encode(decider)` of the leaf: at a leaf where the opponent
decides, that view **cannot see the root player's hand** and **reads the opponent's sampled hand as
known**. 64.4 measured it at the mulligan: after a kept landless hand the next decider's view gives
the keeper 0.51, the keeper's own view 0.36. Every other leaf of the mirror's searches is the
opponent's. A replay the user flagged (Delver AI 1193650d66c0, delver2 iteration 38, frame 20: seat
1's own upkeep, Brainstorm x2 and Ponder in hand, priority with an empty stack): Pass got 1 visit at Q
0.464 against Brainstorm's 0.655 (root v 0.683) - Pass's one leaf is seat 0's priority, valued from
seat 0's view, blind to seat 1's hand.

### 67.2 The design (zero-core docs/search.md 3.6)

* **Views.** Seat key / run setting `leaf_value_view` (`selfplay_leaf_value_view`,
  `eval_leaf_value_view`): 'mover' (default) or 'root'. With 'root', a leaf of the opponent sends two
  rows in the same batch: its own, `encode(opponent)`, for the **priors** (the opponent's model of the
  game: it cannot see our hand either), and a value-only row `encode(root player)` of the same sampled
  state for the **value and margin** (relative to the root player; backed up as any). The value-only
  row has no options and is flagged `ROW_VALUE` in the batch's `extra` (zero-core's generic flagged
  extra rows: the belief head's stage 2, 66.8, adds its own kind). The evaluator interface is
  unchanged. A leaf of the root player is one row as before.
* **The encoding for a non-decider** already writes the pending decision's options, the list block
  (since 65.10 the graveyard list too) and the decision's option count only for the decider
  (`mine_to_decide`, `encode_context`): a non-deciding viewer sees the decision's kind, its decider and
  its public context (the asking task, the card, the cost being paid), nothing derived from the
  decider's hand. 67.3 checks it.
* **Value-only samples** (`selfplay_view_samples`, `view_sample_target`): a share of the recorded
  decisions also records the real state from the other player's view - `encode(other)`, its
  perspective, no options (no policy loss), z its result. **Target**: q = the other player's **own
  next search's** root value (`next_q`, the default; z when it never searches again), blended with z
  by the run's `value_q` as every sample. Why: between the sample and its next search the other
  player only learns more, so that search's value is an unbiased estimate (up to the search's error)
  of the outcome given what it knows at the sample - the tower property - with less variance than z.
  Its *previous* search's q is stale (it predates the decider's move); the decider's q negated
  (zero-sum) is computed from the decider's information set, the other player's hand sampled and the
  decider's known, so it would teach the other view to ignore its own hand and to know the decider's:
  the bias reversed. `z` alone is offered (`view_sample_target z`).

### 67.3 Leaks: the non-deciding viewer's encoding

`determinize(viewer)` keeps the cards a payment in progress pins (section 10: the payer's mana
sources in hand, the cards a cost may exile from it - Force of Will's blue card), so the existing
check (`determinize_keeps_features_and_legal_actions_for_both_viewers`) cannot see a leak through
them. Two engine helpers for tests (`#[doc(hidden)]`): `Game::resample_unpinned(viewer, rng)`
(determinize's deal of **every** card hidden from the viewer, pins included, nothing else: no reseed,
no observer, the pending decision as it is) and `Game::pinned_for(viewer)`; `determinize`'s deal is
factored out (`deal_hidden`) unchanged (the digests, 67.9).

* `tests/hidden.rs`: `a_non_deciding_viewers_features_ignore_the_deciders_hidden_cards` (60 random cube
  games, 232 worlds, the decider's hand dealt again in 215: the other viewer's features identical);
  `a_non_deciding_viewers_features_ignore_pinned_cards_of_a_payment` (P1 pays for a spell with Simian
  Spirit Guide in hand, then casts Force of Will by its alternative cost: at every decision of both,
  P0's features identical in 24 worlds each with the pinned cards dealt again; 6 decisions with pins).
* `tests/az.rs`: `a_non_deciding_viewers_encoding_ignores_the_deciders_hidden_cards` (the public-state
  gate's positions - cube, Delver mirror, best-of-three, a drafted match, 40 each: 480 worlds, all
  with cards dealt again; with `AZ_SCALE=5` 2,400) and `root_view_leaves_encode_alike_whatever_the_
  deciders_options` - the search's own case: two worlds sampled for the root player at its decision
  (cube positions and the Delver mirror), played on with the same actions while the keys agree; at
  every decision of the other player the root player's encoding is the same in both worlds, **also
  where the other player's options differ** (they follow its sampled hand: different tree nodes, one
  information state of the root player). 314 positions compared, 63 with different options (`AZ_SCALE=5`:
  1,785 and 378). `equal_keys_mean_equal_features` stops where the options differ.
* **The public-state gate** (58.6) already requires every public perturbation to reach the encoding of
  **both** viewers, the non-deciding one included: 131 encoded, 3 deliberate limits, 1 gap for the
  next layout (main's). Found on the way, not caused here: at `AZ_SCALE=5` the gate reports 3 findings
  (can't block 4 of 1,047, can't be blocked 6 of 1,047, can't be countered 2 of 249 perturbations
  without an encoding change, both viewers alike) - main 0f98448 reports the same 3 at that scale.

### 67.4 Distribution shift: calibration on CPU self-play

`python tools/root_view.py selfplay --model <copy of delver2 iteration 41> --games 192 --conc 96
--config <delver2's config>`: the line's self-play seat (64 / 16 simulations, p_full 0.25, minor 4,
cq 0.3, mover-view leaves as the line plays), every decision's value-only sample recorded (26,884
samples: 13,442 decisions and 13,442 other views; 1,006 s, 1,476 leaves/s on 4 + 4 threads). `calib`:
the network's P(win) for each row's player against the outcome.

| rows | n | log loss (constant 0.681) | Brier | ECE (5 bins) | mean prediction / won |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decisions (the decider's view: trained) | 13,442 | 0.358 | 0.117 | 0.025 | 0.568 / 0.578 |
| value-only (the other view: never trained) | 13,442 | 0.367 | 0.120 | 0.014 | 0.431 / 0.422 |

* **The shift is small**: the value head, never shown a non-decider's encoding, is about as calibrated
  on it as on the decider's.
* **The views disagree, without a bias**: the decider's own P(win) minus 1 - the other view's at the
  same state: -0.002 on average (13,442 pairs), 0.077 mean absolute, 0.21 at the 90th percentile.
  Neither view is systematically optimistic in real positions.

`finetune` (the 192 games split by game, 48 held out; 300 steps of 256, lr 1e-4, value_q 0.6; 90 s on
CPU), the held-out games' log loss / Brier / ECE:

| | decision rows | value-only rows |
|---|---|---|
| iteration 41 | 0.335 / 0.107 / 0.065 | 0.349 / 0.112 / 0.041 |
| fine-tuned with value-only samples | 0.320 / 0.101 / 0.055 | **0.330** / 0.105 / 0.036 |
| control: decision rows only | 0.319 / 0.101 / 0.059 | 0.334 / 0.107 / 0.033 |

Training on the other view helps it a little beyond fresh data (0.330 vs 0.334 nats) and costs the
decision rows nothing: value-only samples are cheap insurance, not a necessity.

### 67.5 Search: leaf values and the mulligan

`python tools/root_view.py mull --model M --reps 2` (64.3's hands: 50 with no land, 100 with one, 50
with 2-4; 64 simulations, two seeds each, no noise; both views; CPU 4 threads). At the opponent's
leaves of these searches the root player's value from its own view minus from the opponent's:
**+0.054** on average (iteration 31; +0.044 iteration 41), 0.11 mean absolute, 0.23 at p90, more than
0.05 at 73% of 16,216 leaves - far more than at real positions (67.4): in a sampled world the
opponent's hand is a uniform deal of the unseen cards, which its own view then reads as known.

Per declaration (mover view / root view; Q Mulligan where visited; keep = the line's rule cq4 s0.3):

| network | hands | searches | prior Mulligan | Q Keep | Q Mulligan | Mulligan's visits | keep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | 0 lands, first | 42 | 0.954 | 0.387 / 0.355 | 0.401 / 0.401 | 60.4 / 61.2 | 0% / 0% |
| 31 | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.028 | 0.460 / 0.417 | 0.417 / 0.404 | 1.0 / 1.6 | 100% / 100% |
| 31 | 1 land, first | 102 | 0.159 | 0.517 / 0.526 | 0.393 / 0.393 | 10.2 / 10.3 | 82% / 82% |
| 31 | 1 land, second | 98 | 0.001 | 0.470 / 0.557 | - | 0 / 0 | 100% / 100% |
| 41 | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.035 | 0.471 / 0.421 | 0.414 / 0.415 | 1.2 / 2.0 | 100% / 98% |
| 41 | 1 land, second | 98 | 0.001 | 0.482 / 0.565 | 0.349 / - | 0 / 0 | 100% / 100% |
| 41 fine-tuned (67.4) | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.049 | 0.485 / **0.378** | 0.368 / 0.371 | 1.4 / 2.7 | 100% / 97% |
| 41 fine-tuned, floor k 4 (64) | 0 lands, second | 58 | 0.049 | 0.485 / 0.378 | 0.370 / 0.369 | 4.9 / 5.9 | 100% / 97% |
| 41 fine-tuned | 1 land, second | 98 | 0.003 | 0.499 / 0.524 | 0.405 / 0.415 | 0.1 / 0.2 | 100% / 100% |

* **Root-view values move the keep's Q as predicted** where the hand is bad and the opponent acts
  next: a landless keep on the draw drops by 0.04-0.05 (0.11 after the fine-tune) to the mulligan's Q.
* **They do not move the keep rates**: overall 0 lands 58% (mover) / 58-56% (root), 1 land 91% / 91%.
  The prior (0.95-0.97 on Keep on the draw) gives Mulligan 1-6 visits, and the cq rule at scale 0.3
  needs a Q gap of ~0.09 to beat that prior; with the floor (64) Mulligan is measured and still level.
* **One-land and normal hands on the draw look better from the keeper's own view** (Q Keep 0.47 ->
  0.56): 64.4's own-view optimism of the value head for a keep on the draw, now the search's leaf
  value. The mulligan's remaining lever is that value head (the outcomes' weight), as 64.4 said.

### 67.6 The replay's upkeep Brainstorm, instants by step, and the cost

`python tools/root_view.py position --model <copy of iteration 38> --replay rep_1193650d66c0_full.json
--frame 20 --reps 16 --sims 64,256` (the game rebuilt from the replay's seed and actions - the legal
actions match at every network frame; 16 seeds per run):

| | Pass: visits, Q | Brainstorm: visits, Q | the rule's move |
|---|---|---|---|
| replay (mover view, 64) | 1, 0.464 | 62, 0.655 | Brainstorm |
| mover view, 64 | 2.0, 0.512 | 61.0, 0.643 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |
| **root view, 64** | 3.5, **0.638** | 59.5, 0.652 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |
| mover view, 256 | 11.7, 0.619 | 243.3, 0.653 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |
| root view, 256 | 11.6, 0.634 | 243.4, 0.664 | Brainstorm 16 / 16 |

After Pass the next decider is seat 0, whose view gives seat 1 **0.503**; seat 1's own view of the
same state **0.610** (after the cast: 0.535 / 0.610). So the suspicion holds - Pass's 22-point deficit
is the opponent's-view leaf - and root-view values close most of it (Q Pass 0.51 -> 0.64, the gap to
Brainstorm 0.13 -> 0.014), but **the decision does not change**: the prior (0.934) keeps the visits
and the network still rates Brainstorm now slightly higher.

**Instants by step** (`play --model <iteration 38> --games 24`: the network against itself, the line's
rule cq4 s0.3, 64 simulations, minor 4; instants = Brainstorm, Lightning Bolt, Daze, Force of Will,
Unholy Heat, Prismari Charm), cast by the player whose turn it is, by step, mover view / root view:

| step | mover view | root view | of which Brainstorm |
|---|---|---|---|
| own upkeep | 27 | 40 | 6 / 12 |
| own draw step | 47 | 49 | 19 / 18 |
| own main phase 1 | 81 | 80 | 22 / 19 |
| own main 2, combat | 14 | 14 | 3 / 4 |
| in the opponent's turn (any step; upkeep) | 72 (6) | 74 (17) | 2 / 3 |

Root-view leaves do not make the network wait for its main phase: own-upkeep instants are as common
or more (24 games each: noisy; seat 0 scored 0.33 / 0.46). The upkeep habit is the policy's, not a
leaf-view artefact; a network trained with root-view targets would be the test (67.8).

**Cost** (`speed`, iteration 41, 64 self-play games of the line's seat, 4 torch + 4 search threads, 90
s each): mover view **1,313 leaves/s**, root view **887 leaves/s** with 0.51 value-only rows per leaf -
1,313 / 1,342 network rows/s: the CPU is inference-bound, so the extra rows cost their full share
(-32% leaves/s). On the GPU (batches of ~96 rows at the line's conc 192) the extra rows ride in the
same batch and should cost less; not measured (A/B round 2 holds the GPU). Value-only samples at
share s add s samples per recorded decision: the window holds (1 + s) x the rows and training runs (1 +
s) x the steps per iteration (zero-core az.md 16.4).

### 67.7 What it means

Root-view leaf values are correct and leak-free here, cost a third of CPU leaves/s, and the value head
can serve them today (67.4). On today's networks they change Q where 64.4 said they would but rarely
the moves: the priors were trained on mover-view searches and dominate the visits at 64 simulations.
Whether a network trained on root-view searches plays better is the A/B's question.

### 67.8 The A/B (flags; not run)

As 64.6 / 63.6 (`runs/ab-r2/ab_driver.py`): fork the main line at K with root-view self-play and
value-only samples at 0.5, run fork and control K -> K + 10 on the same build, h2h of the two K + 10
checkpoints (600 games, both sides the line's rule cq4 s0.3 **and the same leaf view**: `mtgz.az.h2h`
follows each run's `eval_leaf_value_view`, mover on both arms); the fork wins at >= 0.5 + 2 se. The
experiment entry for an `ab_config.json`:

```json
{"name": "rootview", "requires": "--selfplay-leaf-value-view",
 "flags": ["--selfplay-leaf-value-view", "root", "--selfplay-view-samples", "0.5"],
 "set": ["selfplay_leaf_value_view=root", "selfplay_view_samples=0.5"]}
```

A variant isolating the data: `{"name": "viewsamples", "requires": "--selfplay-view-samples", "flags":
["--selfplay-view-samples", "0.5"], "set": ["selfplay_view_samples=0.5"]}` (the search unchanged). A
cheaper first look, no training: the same checkpoint with both views head to head, `python -m
mtgz.az.h2h M M --games 600 --a-leaf-value-view root --b-leaf-value-view mover` (the line's rule from
its run's config). By hand (`$BASE` = round 2's `base_flags`):

```
python tools/fork_run.py --source runs/delver2 --dest runs/r3-rootview --iter K --set selfplay_leaf_value_view=root --set selfplay_view_samples=0.5
MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py runs/r3-rootview/supervisor_console.txt   python tools/supervise.py runs/r3-rootview $BASE --iters $((K+10)) --eval-every 1000 --selfplay-leaf-value-view root --selfplay-view-samples 0.5
```

* **The build and the Mac**: a pinned run worktree of the merged main, and `bash tools/mac.sh
  --eval-checkout` for the Mac's checkout: remote self-play ships the fork's seat with the keys
  `leaf_value_view`, `view_samples`, `view_sample_target`, which an older checkout **refuses** (an
  error, never a silent off); remote evaluation only if `eval_leaf_value_view` is set (not in this
  A/B). With the settings off the build plays as main, byte for byte (67.9), so the control continues
  delver2 unchanged.
* **Budget**: the fork's self-play is ~1.5x the network rows per leaf (GPU and Mac), its training 1.5x
  the steps (share 0.5); equal *iterations* is the comparison, as round 2.
* **What to read**: the verdict; the mulligan rates (`tools/root_view.py mull` on both K + 10:
  0-land keeps on the draw); `train.value_view` against `value_decision` (the other view's value loss
  should fall to the decider's); `train.entropy` and the policy loss; both arms against the
  heuristic; `selfplay.view.rows_per_leaf` (~0.5).

### 67.10 Risks, limits, conflict points

* **The opponent's search in the tree plays against our hand.** With root-view values the opponent's
  nodes back up the root player's assessment (as before they backed up the mover's): the opponent is
  modelled by its priors (its own view) and by values that know our hand. That is the root player's
  best estimate of each line, and the standard choice for determinized search; an opponent whose real
  play depends on what it believes we hold is modelled only through its priors.
* **Priors trained on mover-view searches.** Today's policies were distilled from searches with
  mover-view leaves; a root-view run's targets drift from them for a while (the A/B reads entropy and
  policy loss).
* **Training cost** of value-only samples (1 + s rows and steps) and the window's RAM: lower the share
  (0.25) if the window must keep its iterations.
* **The encoding contract** now matters for non-deciders: a new decision kind or encoded field must
  keep the decider's options, list and anything derived from its hidden cards out of a non-decider's
  view (67.3's tests catch it on random and Delver positions; rare decisions only if they occur).
* **Distill** (`zero.distill`) averages its policy losses over every row: a window with value-only rows
  dilutes them (its agreement metrics already skip empty segments); not on the run path.
* **Conflict points**: zero-core `Batch` / `LeafBuf` / `Dest` (`extra`), `Pending::Leaf` (`vrow`),
  `worker::decide` (the value-only records: aux targets per record, after the belief head), `NnSeat`'s
  three fields and the seat keys, `run.train_model`'s loss block (merged with the belief head's),
  `play.PyDriver._leaf_batches` (also the recording driver's). The belief head's stage 2 (66.8) adds a
  row kind to `extra` rather than a second mechanism. This repo: `engine/src/hidden.rs`
  (`deal_hidden`), tests appended at the ends of `tests/az.rs` and `tests/hidden.rs`.

## 68. The Gumbel root search (zero-core `root_search`)

Branch `gumbel-root` (from main b818054, rebased after 69's belief search): zero-core pinned at **2f0a2e8**
(feat/gumbel-root on zero-core main 353335c: the feature 7357762, its docs 2f0a2e8: zero-core docs/search.md
3.7, az.md 1.2 and 19);
this repo: the pin, `mtgz.az.replays` (recorded games search with the Gumbel root whenever the run trains
with it - `replays.root_search`, the rule of 67's `leaf_view` - and a Gumbel seat's payments get the
minor budget's schedule), `tools/gumbel_eval.py` (the CPU evidence), this section. With the settings off a run is
the run of before, byte for byte (68.8). Approved by the user 2026-10-29.

### 68.1 Why

At 64 simulations PUCT is locked in by the prior. 64.3: Keep's prior >= 0.98 in 89 of 100 one-land
hands of delver2's iteration 21, Mulligan unvisited in most; 67.6: the replay's upkeep Brainstorm
(prior 0.934) got 62 of 63 visits, Pass 1, also after root-view leaf values raised Q(Pass) to 0.638
against Brainstorm's ~0.65 - the moves barely change because the prior holds the visits. Gumbel
AlphaZero's root (Danihelka et al. 2022) samples m candidates by Gumbel-top-k, spreads the budget by
sequential halving and plays argmax(g + logits + sigma(completedQ)): a policy improvement whatever the
budget, and with <= m legal actions every option is considered. The line already had its other two
pieces: the completed-Q target (`policy_target cq`, `cq_c_scale` 0.3) and the 'cq' move rule.

### 68.2 The design (zero-core docs/search.md 3.7, az.md 19)

* **The root** (`Tree::set_gumbel`; mctx's arithmetic, its schedule checked against mctx's source):
  noise g per root option; the score g + ln P0 + sigma(completedQ), sigma(q) = (c_visit + max N)
  c_scale q - the 'cq' target's logits; sequential halving (root walk j takes an option whose walks of
  this search equal the schedule's entry, the best score among them); the move the best score among the
  most walked options; PUCT below the root. The schedule is that of the search's simulations (a fresh
  root's own evaluation takes the first).
* **Settings and seat keys**: `selfplay_root_search` / `eval_root_search` ('puct' default | 'gumbel'),
  `gumbel_m` 16, `selfplay_gumbel_scale` 1, `eval_gumbel_scale` 0; seat keys `root_search`, `gumbel_m`,
  `gumbel_scale`, `gumbel_c_visit`, `gumbel_c_scale`.
* **Interactions** (each decided and tested in zero-core):

| with | decision |
|---|---|
| sigma | one sigma for the search and its target: self-play's is the 'cq' target's (50, 0.3); an evaluation's the rule's transform (`eval_select_c_scale` 0.3) |
| Dirichlet noise, temperature | replaced by the Gumbel noise: self-play's first `temp_moves` (60) searched decisions are searched with noise 1 (the move a sample of the improved policy), later ones without; evaluation: noise `eval_gumbel_scale` (0: deterministic) |
| the move rule (`*_select`, guard 4) | not used: the Gumbel move replaces it; `eval_select_c_scale` still gives the evaluation's sigma |
| fast and minor searches (`sims_fast` 16, `sims_minor` 4, `p_full` 0.25) | Gumbel searches too (every search of the seat): at 16 simulations a root of up to 15 options gets one walk each and the best score plays; a minor payment at 4 the top 3 by g + ln P0 once each |
| the recorded target | 'cq' (required: a recording Gumbel seat with 'visits' is refused), from every root visit as the paper's |
| the root value target q | the improved policy's value (`gumbel_q`), not the root's mean backup: the halving walks every considered option, so the mean is biased low (68.3: kept hands 0.435 against Keep's 0.518) |
| tree reuse | kept: a reused root's visits count in Q and sigma, the schedule only counts this search's walks |
| root minimum visits (64) | exclusive (an error): sequential halving gives a 2-4 option root 8-31 walks per option at 64 |
| root-view leaf values (67) | orthogonal (tested together) |
| chance, determinization | unchanged; the noise is per search |
| the league seat (63) | the self-play seat: Gumbel with self-play's noise |
| the root's belief (69) | orthogonal: the belief deals the Gumbel search's worlds; a reused root's belief row (its search waits for it) costs no simulation, so the schedule is the same (zero-core's `gumbel_with_a_root_belief` tests, both drivers) |
| evaluation's Elo pool | `gumbel-m16-v50-s0.3` (a new pool: a Gumbel-evaluated run's ratings start there; with a belief `-b1` after it) |
| `mtgz.az.h2h` (zero.h2h) | each side its run's `eval_root_search` whatever `--select` says; `--a-root-search` / `--b-root-search`, `--gumbel-m`, `--a-gumbel-scale` / `--b-gumbel-scale` |

* **Not done**: the paper's deterministic interior selection (PUCT stays below the root: the starvation
  measured is at the root; it would be a separate flag with its own A/B).

### 68.3 The mulligan: keep rates (CPU)

`python tools/gumbel_eval.py mull --model <copy of iteration 51> --reps 2 --noise-reps 8` (64.3's
hands: 50 without a land, 100 with one, 50 with 2-4; 64 simulations; no noise but `gumbel-noise`; each
mode with the line's mover-view leaves and with root-view leaves; CPU 4 threads, ~10 s per mode).
Modes: `puct` (today's: the rule cq4 s0.3), `gumbel` (sigma 0.3, no noise), `gumbel-s1` (sigma 1.0,
the paper's scale), `gumbel-noise` (self-play's: noise 1, 8 draws per hand: the rate self-play keeps).

| hands | searches | prior Mulligan | Mulligan's visits PUCT / Gumbel | Q Keep / Q Mulligan, Gumbel (mover; root view) | keep, mover view: PUCT / Gumbel / sigma 1.0 / noise | keep, root view: PUCT / Gumbel / sigma 1.0 / noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 lands first | 42 | 0.974 | 60.6 / 32.0 | 0.327 / 0.334; 0.298 / 0.331 | 0% / 0% / 0% / 1% | 0% / 0% / 0% / 1% |
| 0 lands second | 58 | 0.030 | 0.7 / 31.0 | 0.495 / 0.357; 0.440 / 0.356 | 100% / 100% / 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% / 98% / 100% |
| 0 lands | 100 | 0.427 | 25.9 / 31.4 | 0.425 / 0.347; 0.380 / 0.346 | 58% / 58% / 58% / 58% | 58% / 58% / 57% / 58% |
| 1 land first | 102 | 0.163 | 10.2 / 31.2 | 0.501 / 0.335; 0.499 / 0.335 | 82% / 82% / 84% / 84% | 82% / 82% / 86% / 84% |
| 1 land second | 98 | 0.001 | 0.0 / 31.0 | 0.503 / 0.359; 0.546 / 0.359 | 100% / 100% / 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% / 100% / 100% |
| 1 land | 200 | 0.084 | 5.2 / 31.1 | 0.502 / 0.347; 0.522 / 0.347 | 91% / 91% / 92% / 92% | 91% / 91% / 93% / 92% |
| 2-4 lands | 100 | 0.018 | 1.0 / 31.0 | 0.528 / 0.346; 0.569 / 0.347 | 98% / 98% / 100% / 99% | 98% / 98% / 100% / 98% |

* **Gumbel measures the mulligan**: Mulligan gets 31-32 of 63 walks in every search (PUCT: 0 with one
  land on the draw, 0.7 with none on the draw, 5 with one land overall).
* **The keep rates do not move**: 0 lands 58% (PUCT) / 58% (Gumbel) / 57-58% (sigma 1.0) / 58% (with
  noise), 1 land 91% / 91% / 92-93% / 92%. Measured, Mulligan's Q is well below Keep's where the line
  keeps (1 land on the draw: 0.36 against 0.50, root view 0.55): the keeps are the value head's, not the
  starvation's - 64.4's conclusion, now with Mulligan measured 31 times per search instead of never.
* **The root value**: a Gumbel search's plain root mean of a kept hand is 0.435 against Keep's Q 0.518
  (mover view; root view 0.443 / 0.533) - the halving gives Mulligan half the walks; `gumbel_q` is 0.518,
  the same as PUCT's root value 0.519 (the reason q is the improved policy's value, 68.2).
