## 72. Who knows a library's top cards, in the encoding

Branch `top-known` (from main e08bade), 2026-10-30, CPU only; the user's decision after a question
about top-of-library knowledge in the Delver mirror ("a correctness issue": fix the input before any
belief over the opponent's top cards). Layout v5 is unchanged: six spare per-player floats, as
section 55 filled v4's. The rules engine is untouched (the encoding-free digest is equal).

### 72.1 The gap

`Obj.known` (section 10) says which players know a hidden card. What the card is stays hidden;
**who knows it is public**: every event that sets or clears a bit is seen by both players (a look
at the top N, a surveil kept on top, Brainstorm's put-back, a Mishra's Bauble at one's own library,
a shuffle, a draw). The encoding showed the viewer's own knowledge (the tops block's "known to the
viewer" and the card; the `*_KNOWN` bags) and, for the hand, which of the viewer's cards the
opponent knows (hand st[4]), but not who else knows a library card:

* **The opponent's library known to its owner.** The opponent Ponders and keeps, surveils and keeps
  (Dragon's Rage Channeler, Thundering Falls), Brainstorms, or looks at its own top with a Bauble:
  everyone knows the opponent knows its next draws, and the keep or the put-back says something
  about them. The viewer's input was identical to an untouched library, so neither the trunk nor a
  belief head could learn anything from it.
* **The viewer's library known to the opponent.** A Mishra's Bauble at a top card its owner knows
  is remembered by the looker (23.7); the owner's input did not show that the opponent knows its
  next draw.

The public-state gate (58.6) could not see it: it classified `Obj.known` as hidden as a whole.

### 72.2 The fix: six spare floats per player

`g5::TOP_OWNER` (per-player floats 16-18) and `g5::TOP_OTHER` (19-21): per position k of the top
three (`TOPS`, top first) of that player's library (per-player blocks viewer first), 1 if the
library's owner knows the card there, and 1 if the other player does. Two per-player floats stay
spare. For a viewer the floats about its own knowledge repeat the tops block's "known to the
viewer"; the new information is the other player's knowledge of both libraries.

Layout v5 is unchanged (37,620 floats; `layout_v5.json` declares `globals_v5` as a block), so the
encoding guard (61) accepts every v5 checkpoint and the shards' width is the same. As in 55.2, the
inputs were always 0 in training: their `TokenNet` weight columns are their initialisation (less
weight decay) until training gives them a meaning.

### 72.3 Hidden information

Who knows stays with a card's slot: `determinize` deals identities (`set_ident`) and
`force_library_card` swaps identities between cards nobody knows, so the floats are the same in
every world either viewer's `determinize` deals, and a viewer's input says nothing about what the
cards are. `Game::view_of` now lists, per library, the positions the other player knows (whose
changes the gate needs to see); the fuzz and the hidden-information checks compare it across
worlds.

### 72.4 The gate

`Obj.known` is classified public ("who knows is public, what it is is not: leak-tested") with four
perturbations, each through `Game::learn` (which keeps the clouds right): the owner learns its top
card; the other player learns a library's top card (its owner too: a library card the other player
knows its owner knows, 23.7); the owner learns a card below the top three (a **deliberate limit**:
below the top three the encoding has the viewer's own knowledge only, in the bags; that the other
player knows a deeper card is a mulligan's bottom cards, whose number the mulligans' count gives,
or a card put under others, never the next draws); the other player learns a hand card (hand st[4]
and `OPP_HAND_KNOWN`, already encoded).

`public_state_reaches_the_encoding` (240 positions: the cube, the Delver mirror, best-of-three, a
drafted match; 211 fields, 117 public, 6 hidden, 88 derived; 145 perturbations): the owner learns its
top card, 223 applied; the other player learns a library's top card, 240; a hand card, 218 - both
views and both encodings changed every time. Below the top three: 240 applied, both views changed,
the non-owner's encoding unchanged every time (the limit, as declared). In all: 135 encoded, 4
deliberate limits, 1 gap for the next layout (the graveyard's order, as before).

### 72.5 Tests

`tests/az.rs` `who_knows_a_librarys_top_cards_is_encoded` (the constructed card pool, both viewers,
20 worlds each per step): P0 Brainstorms, putting a Mountain and a Bolt back (P0's library
`[(1,0), (1,0), (0,0)]`, (owner, other), top first); P1's Mishra's Bauble at P0's top card, which P0
knows (`[(1,1), (1,0), (0,0)]`, P1 remembers it); P0 Ponders and keeps (P1 loses track of its card:
`[(1,0), (1,0), (0,0)]` after the draw); Polluted Delta's search shuffles (all 0). P1's library stays
all 0 throughout. The gate's tests (`public_state_reaches_the_encoding`, the classification table)
and `the_v5_facts_encode_no_hidden_information` run the new perturbations.

### 72.6 Encoding, digests, networks

Encoding-free behaviour digest **a634df1919e3c337, unchanged**; the full digest 11e873a3d2e4530a ->
**6b4bc88c864c4dd4** (`DIGEST_WRITE=1`: 1,825 of the 2,500 games encode differently at some
position).

The encoding gate (`tools/gate.py encoding`, `gates/45535f0adf75.json`): the build, both digests as
above, `--test az` 39 passed, the main line's checkpoint `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch/models/iter_0196.pt`
(read only) loads and plays 8 Delver games (h2h, CPU, 16 simulations, none unfinished), pytest 59
passed. Fuzz: 300 games of the default pool and 1,000 of the Delver pool (`FUZZ_POOL=delver`), clean.

**What a v5 checkpoint sees.** Unlike 55.2's v4 networks, the main line's descend from 60's exact
widen, which gave every v5 global a zero weight column, and a column whose input is always 0 never
moves: the columns of these twelve floats are exactly 0 in `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch` iterations 100
and 196 and in delver2's iteration 0 (`TokenNet.g`, inputs 160 + 24 side + 16..21). On 4,000 Delver
positions where they are set (a third of the decisions of mixed heuristic / random games, 1.7 set
floats a row), iteration 196's and 100's values and policies are those with the floats masked, bit for
bit (P(win) shift 0, policy KL 0, no argmax changed). So a re-pin changes nothing for the network until
training grows the columns, as it grew the used v5 globals' from 0 (cards drawn 0.3-0.95, attacked 0.5-0.6,
delayed triggers - a Bauble's draw - 1.9-2.1; the ones the mirror never sets are still 0). A network
built fresh has random columns there instead, which distilling from older shards (all 0 there) never
trains: a distilled student (62.9) moved onto this build should have them zeroed first, or it plays
with an untrained input (55.6's size of effect).

### 72.7 What this does not change

* A Mishra's Bauble at a card its owner does not know is still not remembered (23.7), and a
  shuffle followed by a draw still drops the cloud it made (10): the bot's own knowledge.
* The belief head (66) predicts the opponent's hand only and the weighted deal (69) tilts the hand;
  the opponent's known top cards are dealt uniformly. A belief over them is a later step, and now
  has an input to learn from.
* A run picks this up at a re-pin (an iteration boundary; checkpoints, the optimiser state and the
  window's shards load as they are); which run and when is the user's call.

## 73. Strength measurement for the Delver line (zero-core `feat/measure`: fixed Elo anchors, held-out losses, paired + sequential h2h; behaviour fingerprints)

User-approved 2026-10-30 after a Fable review found that the main line's yardsticks could not see its
progress (zero-core docs/az.md 20 has the framework's side: settings, formulas, tests). This branch
pins zero-core `feat/measure` and adds `tools/delver_fingerprints.py`, `mtgz.az.heldout` (the shim)
and `tests/test_measure.py`. Every new setting is off by default: the engine, the encoding, the
digests and every run of before are unchanged (73.9).

### 73.1 Why

The review's evidence on `runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch` (paused at iteration 196):

* **The Elo pool** (`elo/cq-n4-v50-s0.3-rv-b1m0.25/`): every 8 iterations each checkpoint plays k-1,
  k-2, k-4, k-8 for 25 games each at 32 simulations: +-50-115 Elo per rating, no fixed reference.
  The ratings of the evaluated checkpoints 128-192 wander 1448-1613 with se 47-70; the pooled pairs
  give 0.481 +- 0.015 = -1.9 +- 2.3 Elo per iteration - a plateau and +1 Elo a generation look alike.
* **The yardstick** is saturated: 92-98% against the heuristic since iteration ~100 (the user: stop
  testing against it).
* **h2h verdicts** (600 games, se 0.020) are too noisy for the effects the A/B program adopts: two
  features went in at 0.538 and 0.534 (the bar 0.541). The games alternate seats but are not paired:
  each game's deal is its own, so a mirror's opening-hand variance stays in the score.
* **A cheap learning signal** was missing: the held-out value loss against the true outcome z on a
  fixed set of fresh rows moved 0.4066 (iteration 111) -> 0.4012 (188) in the review's check.

### 73.2 What the pin adds (zero-core docs/az.md 20)

* **Fixed anchors** (`--elo-anchors label=path,...`, `--elo-anchor-games`, `--elo-anchor-elo`,
  `--elo-anchor-calib-games`, `--elo-anchor-from`): frozen checkpoints every evaluated checkpoint plays;
  the first anchor's rating set, later ones calibrated once against it and frozen (sha256 kept); the
  fit of the pool's whole results with them fixed -> `elo_anchored` (metrics, evals.jsonl, log),
  `anchored.json`. Shipped to the Mac's mirror for `--eval-remote mac`. `--eval-games 0` drops the
  heuristic's games; every Elo match is still played (tested).
* **`--elo-paired 1`**: the run's Elo matches as paired games (even game counts).
* **Held-out losses** (`--heldout-shards`, `python -m mtgz.az.heldout make | eval`): value CE /
  accuracy / Brier against z and policy CE / top-1 against the recorded targets on a frozen row set,
  decision and value-only rows apart, every evaluated iteration (`heldout` in the metrics, a log line).
* **zero.h2h** (`python -m mtgz.az.h2h`, the same module): `--paired`, `--sprt E0,E1` (+ `--alpha`,
  `--beta`, `--batch-games`, `--max-games`), `--target-se`, `--a-sims` / `--b-sims`.

### 73.3 Paired h2h on the Delver mirror: the variance it removes

**Method.** Checkpoint 196 (A) against 188 (B) of the line, 32 simulations, each side its run's
evaluation search (config.json next to models/: the 'cq' rule n4 at 0.3, root-view leaves, the belief
tilt 1 mix 0.25 on every search), `chance_k` 0 (the run's evaluation; h2h's default 2 hit the engine
panics of 73.8), the Delver spec (**correction, section 74**: the jobs passed no `--spec`, so `zero.h2h`
played the package's `mtg` spec, random cube decks; the numbers below are of cube games played by the
Delver line's checkpoints, not of the mirror); batches of 200 games on the Mac (`nice -n 19`, beside the fuzz
farm: 6.5 min each) and one on the desktop CPU (22 min), each batch its own seed (11-14, 21); paired,
and one unpaired batch for the check.
(`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/pool_batches.py` pools them: the pentanomial counts add up.)

| batch | games | A's score | se (paired) | se_games (unpaired formula) | variance_ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| paired seed 11 | 200 | 0.490 | 0.0246 | 0.0353 | 0.48 |
| paired seed 12 | 200 | 0.500 | 0.0293 | 0.0354 | 0.68 |
| paired seed 13 | 200 | 0.470 | 0.0264 | 0.0353 | 0.56 |
| paired seed 14 | 200 | 0.460 | 0.0232 | 0.0352 | 0.43 |
| paired seed 21 (desktop) | 200 | 0.545 | 0.0247 | 0.0352 | 0.49 |
| **paired, pooled** | **1,000** | **0.493** | **0.0115** | 0.0158 | **0.53** (95% bootstrap 0.46-0.61) |
| unpaired seed 11 | 200 | 0.470 | - | 0.0353 | - |

The 500 pairs: 63 both won, **367 split (73%)**, 70 both lost, no draw (pentanomial [70, 0, 367, 0,
63]); the unpaired batch agrees (0.470 +- 0.035). In three pairs of four each side won with the same seat's deal - the deal (who is on the play,
the two hands, the library) decides most mirror games, and pairing takes that variance out:
**var(pair score) = 0.53 x var(game) / 2**, so a paired h2h of N games is as precise as an unpaired
one of 1.9 N. At 600 games the se falls from 0.020 to 0.015 and the 2-se bar from 0.541 to 0.530. (By
the way: 196 scored 0.493 +- 0.012 against 188 - -5 +- 8 Elo: eight iterations without a measurable
gain.)

**What it does to the A/B verdicts** (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/sprt_sim.py`: 8,000 simulated tests
per row; pair scores from the 3-point law with the ratio 0.54 of the first four batches, games from a
Bernoulli; zero.h2h's LLR
and bounds): the share of forks adopted and the mean games played, for a fork that is truly E Elo
better -

| true E | score | 600-game 2-se bar, unpaired (today) | ... paired | SPRT(0, 20), <= 2,400 games, unpaired: H1 / undecided / games | ... paired |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -10 | 0.486 | 0% | 0% | 0% / 3% / 1,282 | 0% / 0% / 836 |
| 0 | 0.500 | 2% | 2% | 2% / 29% / 1,804 | 2% / 9% / 1,354 |
| +10 | 0.514 | 10% | 15% | 20% / 60% / 2,107 | 30% / 39% / 1,831 |
| +20 | 0.529 | 28% | 46% | 69% / 30% / 1,791 | **90% / 8% / 1,343** |
| +30 | 0.543 | 54% | 80% | 96% / 3% / 1,266 | 100% / 0% / 841 |
| +40 | 0.557 | 79% | 97% | 100% / 0% / 926 | 100% / 0% / 655 |

Today's readout adopts a real +20 Elo fork 28% of the time; paired + SPRT(0, 20) adopts it 90% of the
time in 1,343 games on average (2.2 batches of 600), with the same 2% false adoptions of a null; a
+30 fork is decided in 841 games. SPRT(0, 15) with up to 3,000 games: +20 adopted 97% (1,448
games), +10 43%, a null 2% (1,935 games, 18% undecided). The choice (73.6) is SPRT(0, 20), alpha =
beta = 0.05, batches of 600, at most 2,400: the effects the program has adopted (0.534-0.538, +24-26
Elo) are inside its power, its false positives are the old bar's, a lopsided result still costs one
batch of 600 and a close one up to four (~76 min on the GPU).

### 73.4 Held-out losses of the main line

The set: `python -m mtgz.az.heldout make --from runs/r3-2b-beliefsearch/data/iter_0191 --rows 8192
--seed 0` -> `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/heldout/r3-2b_iter0191_8192.npz` (8.8 MB; set
`463ad8eefa5c`: 5,407 decision rows, 2,785 value-only rows of iteration 191's 800 games, generated by
checkpoint 190). Iteration 191's rows trained checkpoints 191-196 only (window 6): held out for every
checkpoint up to 190 and for all the line's next ones (197 on). All 110 checkpoints of the line's
models/ (83-196), CPU, 2.4 s each:

| checkpoint | decision value_ce | acc | policy_ce | top-1 | view value_ce | acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 83 | 0.3933 | 0.796 | 0.522 | 0.843 | 0.4103 | 0.785 |
| 96 | 0.3876 | 0.801 | 0.490 | 0.859 | 0.3995 | 0.792 |
| 112 | 0.3872 | 0.800 | 0.467 | 0.872 | 0.3908 | 0.805 |
| 128 | 0.3865 | 0.800 | 0.444 | 0.882 | 0.3938 | 0.794 |
| 144 | 0.3839 | 0.804 | 0.425 | 0.890 | 0.3916 | 0.797 |
| 160 | 0.3852 | 0.801 | 0.402 | 0.906 | 0.3950 | 0.797 |
| 176 | 0.3842 | 0.798 | 0.383 | 0.926 | 0.3974 | 0.788 |
| 188 | 0.3839 | 0.808 | 0.363 | 0.947 | 0.4053 | 0.787 |
| 190 | 0.3878 | 0.801 | 0.360 | 0.951 | 0.4099 | 0.782 |
| 191 (trained on it) | 0.3593 | 0.823 | 0.361 | 0.948 | 0.3746 | 0.805 |
| 196 (trained on it 6 x) | 0.3192 | 0.857 | 0.357 | 0.948 | 0.3309 | 0.841 |

* **The value head learns slowly**: decision rows' value CE 0.393 (83) -> 0.384 (188), a linear fit
  over the clean checkpoints (83-190) -0.009 per 100 iterations, with a checkpoint-to-checkpoint
  scatter of ~0.003 (120: 0.394). The view rows' value CE does not improve at all (-0.0015 per 100
  iterations).
* **Contamination is large**: the checkpoints that trained on the set's rows fall to 0.319 (196, six
  windows) - the value head memorizes the outcomes of games it trained on, 0.065 nats in six
  iterations against 0.009 of real progress in a hundred. A set must be fresh for the checkpoints it
  measures: iteration 191's is for 197 on.
* **The encoding moved under it**: the set's rows were encoded before section 72's top-card floats (six
  per-player globals, set at about a third of Delver decisions; 0 in the set). The line's checkpoints
  have zero weights on those columns (72: their outputs bit for bit unchanged), so they read the set
  as before; once training moves those weights, a set built from a relaunched iteration (held out from
  six iterations after it) measures the new inputs too - keep iteration 191's for the history.
* **policy_ce is agreement, not strength**: it falls steadily (0.522 -> 0.360) towards checkpoint 190,
  the search that recorded the targets, and stays there after; the line's next checkpoints will move
  away from 190's search whether they improve or not. Read it as drift (a collapse or a jump shows),
  `value_ce` as the learning signal.

### 73.5 Behaviour fingerprints (`tools/delver_fingerprints.py`)

`python tools/delver_fingerprints.py r3-2b-beliefsearch` (bands of 20 generations; `--band`,
`--min-gen`, `--max-gen`, several runs, `--json`). The replays are the Delver AI publisher's
(runs/<run>/replays: 6 games of every even generation against itself, 64 simulations), both seats
counted; a cell is rate (n). The metrics' exact definitions are in the tool's docstring; in short:

* **fetch cracked now**: of the fetches played and cracked, the share cracked with nothing between.
* **brainstorm w/ shuffle**: of the Brainstorms cast, the share with a shuffle to follow (its own
  fetch ability on the stack - `bs in resp. to fetch` -, an uncracked fetch of its own, or a fetch
  in hand with the land drop unused in its own turn before the end step).
* **murktide delve best**: of the Murktides cast, the share that exiled as many instants and
  sorceries as it could (min(5, those in its graveyard)).
* **fow pitched fow**: of the Force of Will pitch payments that offered a second Force of Will AND
  another blue card, the share that pitched the Force of Will.
* **tap-out into Daze**: of the spells cast in the caster's own main phase (empty stack, turn >= 3,
  free spells excluded) while the opponent - at its first decision after the cast - held Daze and an
  Island, the share with no untapped land left (Wasteland and uncracked fetches count as mana);
  `tapped out: dazed` = of those, the share actually Dazed.
* **T1-2 Volcanic, U only**: of the fetch searches in the fetcher's own turns 1-2 with the basic Island
  still in its library, whose turn then cast only non-red spells, the share that took Volcanic Island
  (`... nothing cast`: the turn cast nothing more).
* **mulligans**: opening sevens, keep rate by lands and play / draw, the network's mean prior on
  Mulligan and how often the search visited it.

Fixed against the review's scripts: their turn 1-2 was global turns 1-2 and read the Island's zone
after the fetch had found it (a found Island never counted as "in the library": the Volcanic share was
100% by construction); the tap-out count ignored Wasteland and uncracked fetches and read the state
one step after the cast (mana payment not always finished); Murktide's delve skipped countered casts;
the Brainstorm shuffle needed the main phase (most Brainstorms are cast in the upkeep or draw step).

What it says: the line cracks fetches at once ~90% of the time and so almost never has a shuffle for its
Brainstorm (11-16%, never in response to a fetch); it pitches a second Force of Will over another blue
card 56-91% of the time; it taps out into a live Daze about half the time and is Dazed about half of
those; it takes Volcanic Island over the basic on its first two turns when only blue was needed 60-83%;
it keeps nearly every seven with 2+ lands (85-100%) and 54-92% of one-landers; Murktide's delve leaves
an instant or sorcery behind in about a third of the casts. None of these moves across the 106
generations beyond the noise of a few dozen games a band (n in each cell): the review's reading of a
behavioural plateau holds. The fingerprints are descriptive (a Volcanic Island fetch can be right);
their use is to see a change after a fix or a new training setting.

### 73.6 The A/B driver (`runs/ab-r3/ab_driver.py`, not edited here)

The driver (read-only here) builds `python -m mtgz.az.h2h FORK CONTROL --games 600 --sims 32 --spec S
--device cuda --threads 8 --seed 7 --select cq --select-min-visits 4 --a-cq-c-scale 0.3 --b-cq-c-scale
0.3` (+ the leaf views) and adopts the fork at `a_score >= 0.5 + 2 se`. To use paired + sequential
games, change two places:

1. `h2h()`, the command (lines 157-158):

   ```python
   cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'mtgz.az.h2h', a, b, '--games', str(games), '--sims', '32',
          '--spec', spec, '--device', 'cuda', '--threads', '8', '--seed', '7',
          '--chance-k', '0', '--paired', '--sprt', '0,20', '--max-games', str(4 * games)] + H2H_SELECT
   ```

   (`games` = ab_config's `h2h_games` 600: batches of 600, at most 2,400; `--chance-k 0` is the run's
   own evaluation setting - h2h's default 2 is what hit both engine panics, 73.8; drop it to keep
   round 3's searches.)
2. `main()`, the verdict (lines 264-268):

   ```python
   score = r.get('score', r.get('a_score'))
   se = r.get('se', r.get('a_se', 0.0))
   sprt = r.get('sprt') or {}
   win = sprt.get('decision') == 'H1' if sprt else (score is not None and score >= 0.5 + 2 * se)
   new_main = fork if win else main_run
   verdict = ('FORK WINS' if win else 'control kept' + (' (undecided)' if sprt.get('decision') == 'undecided' else '')) \
       + (f' (score {score:.3f} ± {se:.3f}, {r.get("games")} games, llr {sprt.get("llr")})' if score is not None else '')
   ```

   and `write_results`' method line (line 179, 'The fork wins at score >= 0.5 + 2 se.') to 'Paired
   games (each deal from both seats); the fork wins when the SPRT of +20 Elo against 0 (alpha = beta =
   0.05) accepts +20 within 2,400 games; undecided = control kept.'

The minimal change is `'--paired'` alone in the command: the old rule then reads the paired se (`se`)
unchanged - the same bar with the variance of 73.3. The subprocess timeout (4 h) covers 2,400 games on
the GPU (600 games took 19 min in round 3). An undecided SPRT means |effect| below ~15 Elo after
2,400 games: the user's "principled fix" adoptions remain a judgement call on `a_score` +- `se`.

## 74. The two engine panics of h2h's `chance_k` 2 (73.8): a Citadel look after its options, a mill that was not one action

Branch `chance-panics` (from main f52c0bb). Section 73.8's two panics, both in a search's simulation of
`python -m mtgz.az.h2h` at its default `chance_k` 2, both reproduced, both caused by the same mechanism
meeting an older engine flaw: zero-core's `chance_k` replays (`force_chance`) an outcome recorded in
another world of the same node, and the engine's forced draw / look / reveal swaps the recorded
identity into the card about to be seen (section 10's `force_chance`). That is sound only when nothing
already depends on the card's identity, and in two places something did. Each is fixed at that place,
with tests that fail on main (and identically at d0b62b1 and 6f871ac: 74.4).

**The games were cube games, not the Delver mirror.** `zero.h2h` plays the game package's spec unless
`--spec` is given (its module docs), and `mtgz`'s `mtg` spec is the cube's
(`{"max_turns": 60, "eval_decks": 16, "eval_seed": 1}`: random cube decks every game). The measurement's
jobs (73.3's batches, `E:/mtg-zero-scratch/measure/mac_jobs*.sh`, the Mac's `~/mtgz-measure/jobs*.sh`)
passed no `--spec`: checkpoints of the Delver line played random cube decks - the paired seed-7 game's
log holds Barrowgoyf, Griselbrand, Blightsteel Colossus, Formidable Speaker, Emperor of Bones, none in
the Delver 60, and the faces panics need Bolas's Citadel (74.1), not in it either. 73.3's numbers
(the variance ratio, the scores) are therefore of cube games, not of the mirror the text names; the
A/B driver's h2h passes the Delver spec (`runs/ab-r3/ab_driver.py`, `--spec`), so round 3's
adoptions are of the mirror. This is also why round 3's h2hs at `chance_k` 2 on 6f871ac and d0b62b1
never died: the two cards involved (Citadel; Blightsteel with a mill that names its cards) are not in
the Delver deck.

### 74.1 "a card with another face": Bolas's Citadel's look came after the options it shapes

**The panic.** `faces.rs:510` (`choose_face`, "the other face" answered: paired seed 8, game 138) and
`flow.rs:689` (Priority's `CastFace`: unpaired seed 7, game 510), both an `other_face(..).expect`.

**Cause.** With Bolas's Citadel its controller may cast or play the top card of their library, so
Priority's options name that card by what it is (`top_options`: cast it, play it, its faces -
`Faces(card, mask)` when both of an MDFC's or an Adventure's faces can be cast). Its controller "looks at
it any time": `Game::look_tops`, run at the end of `advance` - **after** the pending decision was
computed. Without a forced outcome that order is harmless (the look learns the card, it changes
nothing). With one, the look's `force_library_card` swaps the recorded identity in **after** the
options were computed from the old one. In the test's two worlds (below): the replaying world's top
card was a Brazen Borrower, the options offered its face choice (`LIBRARY` + 0), the forced look made it
a Lightning Bolt - the recorded world's card -, the legal actions were the same ids (the same node), the
search walked `LIBRARY` + 0, the face choice asked for "the other face" of a Bolt: the panic, with the
h2h's message at the h2h's line; a `CastFace` option (only the other face castable) panics at
`flow.rs:689` the same way. The same stale option
as a cast gives the other failures the chance fuzz found (74.3): "no legal target for a required
target" (a Force of Negation's cast offered for what had been a castable card), "cast Forest".

**Introduced** by a2fa790 (2026-10-24, M7d: the Citadel, "keyed and forced like any look"), the first
commit with the look; neither of 73.8's builds' window.

**Fix** (`flow.rs`). `priority_ask` looks (`look_tops`) before computing its options: the forced
identity is in place when the options are made, and the replaying world's decision is the recorded
one's (the same options for the same card). `advance`'s look stays for every other decision; no other
decision's options read a top card its controller has not looked at (`top_options` is Priority's
alone), and debug builds now check it: when `advance`'s look swaps an identity, the decision refreshed
in a clone must equal the pending one (`look_tops` reports a swap). Real play (no queued outcome) is
unchanged but for the keys: the Citadel controller's `KEY_LOOK` is now emitted before a Priority the
engine answers (`KEY_AUTO`, one option) instead of at the next decision, and a top card that changes
before that decision is looked at too (74.6).

**Tests** (`engine/tests/rules_chance.rs`, the search's two worlds - the recorded one and the replaying
one, its keys forced - on real cards): `a_forced_look_at_the_citadels_top_card_comes_before_the_options`
(the Borrower made a Bolt: the same actions, `LIBRARY` + 0 casts the Bolt, which resolves; on main the
walk panics `faces.rs:510` "a card with another face", the h2h's message),
`a_forced_look_at_the_citadels_top_card_leaves_no_stale_cast` (a Bolt made a Forest: no option for the
top card, as in the recorded world; on main "340=cast Forest#3").

### 74.2 "ChooseGraveyardCard: duplicate action ids": a mill shuffled its library between its cards

**The game** (paired seed 7, game 37, reproduced with the game log - the spec's `"log": true`):
Barrowgoyf deals 7 combat damage, "you may mill that many cards. If you do, you may put a creature
card from among them into your hand" (`Ext::MayMillThenTakeCreature`). The second card milled is
Blightsteel Colossus: "if it would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, reveal it and shuffle it into
its owner's library instead".

**Cause.** The mill moved its cards one at a time from the top, and the Colossus's replacement
shuffled the library **at once** (`shuffle_in_instead`): the cards milled after it came from the
shuffled library, and the mill's pile (the cards "among them") kept the Colossus's card although it
went back. In the search's replaying world each forced reveal makes the top card the one the recorded
world milled there; after the shuffle the Colossus's card came to the top again, unknown to everyone
(the shuffle's cloud), and the queued reveal made it a Griselbrand - a legitimate swap with a
Griselbrand elsewhere in the library, unknown too, in the same cloud - which was milled: the pile held
card 14 twice, and "a creature card from among them" offered it twice. Two flaws: the mill was not one action (CR 701.13a:
the top N cards are put into the graveyard together; a replacement that shuffles one of them into the
library does so as part of that event, not between its cards), and the pile counted a card that never
reached the graveyard.

**Not only the search's.** At `chance_k` 0 the duplicate cannot happen (no forced reveal, the
Colossus's card stays a Colossus and goes back each time), but the rules bug does, in real games: any
mill that reaches a Blightsteel Colossus before its last card milled the rest from a shuffled library
(cards that were not among the top N, possibly the Colossus again). Cube pools only (the Colossus is not
in the Delver deck, which mills nothing).

**Introduced** by 302a05f (2026-10-24, Blightsteel Colossus's shuffle-instead) on b7fc16d's mill
(2026-10-22, Barrowgoyf, its milled cards forced and revealed); neither of 73.8's builds' window.

**Fix** (`game.rs`). `Game::mill(p, n, forced)`: the top `n` cards together - each (with `forced`) given
its queued outcome and revealed, then moved with `pile_moving` set, so a shuffle-instead replacement
leaves its card where it is and the library is shuffled once all `n` have moved (`flush_pile_shuffles`,
the mechanism a looked-at pile's surveil already used: section 51). It returns the cards milled; every
mill loop of the engine uses it: `Ext::Mill`, `MillTwoWhileShareColor`, `MayMillThenTakeCreature` (its
pile is the cards put into the graveyard), `MillAttackPump`, `LetDrawElseMill`, `MillThenLandToHand`;
which of them force is as before (the two that did).

**Tests.** `a_mill_takes_the_top_cards_together_and_shuffles_blightsteel_in_after_cr_701_13a`
(Barrowgoyf's mill of 2 over the Colossus and a Test Bear, 24 shuffle seeds: the Bear milled every time,
the Colossus in the library, offered once; on main the second card came from the shuffled library),
`a_replayed_mill_offers_each_milled_card_once` (256 pairs of worlds, the second replaying the first's
keys: the same keys, the Bear offered once; on main one replay panics in `ask`, "ChooseGraveyardCard:
duplicate action ids", the h2h's message).

### 74.3 The chance-node fuzz (`FUZZ_CHANCE=n`)

`engine/tests/fuzz.rs` had no forced outcome anywhere: random play never replays a key, and section 10's
`force_chance` checks (tests/az.rs) replay single transitions of mid-game states. `FUZZ_CHANCE=n`
(one decision in `n`, its own generator; the games are the same with or without it) runs a **chance
walk**: two worlds of the decider, each dealt as a simulation's (uniform or, one time in two, by random
weights: the belief-weighted search), walk one random path while they are at one node of the tree
(the same next decider and legal actions, equal keys so far); at each step one world takes the action
freely and the other replays its keys (`force_chance` for the whole search transition, single-option
decisions answered, as `tree::transition` does), the roles swapping at random; a replaying world whose
keys or next actions differ is in another node, and plays on alone for 20 steps. After every step
both worlds' invariants and knowledge hold and the legal actions are sorted and unique; every option
of the replaying world's decision completes whenever the force changed its outcome (one time in four
otherwise); a panic is reported with the walk's path and its forced keys. It prints the walks, their
steps at one node, the replays whose outcome the force changed (the replaying world, unforced, would
have had other keys) and the walks split by the keys; with 100 games or more some replay must have
taken a forced outcome. Games only (the h2h's games are best-of-one).

Found on main (release, `FUZZ_CHANCE=2`): the first failure of each 1,000-seed chunk of the interactions
pool's seeds 0-2,999 - 81, 1238 and 2304, all 74.1's class (a stale Citadel cast, "no legal target for a
required target": Force of Negation, Invert Polarity; the completion check reached it before the walk's
random step); the walk's first version (it stopped at a split) found 81 and nothing in 6,000 default-pool
and 2,000 Delver games. On this branch those seeds pass.

**Not fixed here.** Interactions seed 523 (`FUZZ_POOL=interactions FUZZ_CHANCE=2 FUZZ_FIRST=523
FUZZ_GAMES=1`): a Toxic Deluge cast from the Citadel's top under Thalia, Guardian of Thraben, the X life
option 5 offered and then "PayMana: no way to pay {1}" - the farm's `PayMana` bucket (its config's
`expected`), a cost check that disagrees with the payment, reached in a forced world but not caused by
the force (the state is an ordinary legal one). Not in the default or Delver pools.

### 74.5 Found by the fuzz: Urza's Bauble's look beside a known twin

The Delver pool's seed 16246 (`FUZZ_POOL=delver FUZZ_FIRST=16246 FUZZ_GAMES=1 cargo test --profile fuzz -p
engine --test fuzz fuzz_random_games`, with or without `FUZZ_CHANCE`: the information-set check of a
checkpoint, not the walk): `same keys, different views` of the player whose Urza's Bauble looked at a card
at random in the other's hand. That player already knew one card of the hand, and the look marked the
card seen as known (`learn`) - in a world where it saw the other copy of that identity, it now "knew" two;
where it saw the known one, one. A hand's cards are not told apart (section 10), so seeing "a Lightning
Bolt" beside the Bolt already known says nothing new: the two worlds were one node (the same
public key) with different knowledge, encodings and searches. **Cause**: the look's knowledge, older than
71.1 (which keyed the look public for the owner; the looker's own key was always its own). **Fix**
(`Ext::LookAtRandomHandCard`): no card is learned when the looker already knows another card of that
hand with the identity seen. **Who**: every pool with Urza's Bauble, the Delver mirror included (one in
the 60): a search of the looker with a card of the other's hand already known (an earlier look, an
Island returned by Daze) merged worlds that knew one or two copies. A search-quality fix; no network input or
layout change. **Test**: `a_random_look_at_a_twin_of_a_known_card_knows_no_more_than_one` (48 worlds of
the looker, a known Bolt and a second one in the hand: equal keys, equal views, one Bolt known whenever
a Bolt was seen; fails on 38a0fa1, i.e. main's look).

## 78. CUDA graphs of the token network's inference (zero-core `feat/token-graphs`, opt-in)

Branch `token-graphs` (from main 1605436), zero-core `feat/token-graphs` 2b79780 (code 3d5875e, docs
2b79780; from c15e3d0; its docs/az.md 10.6 has the design, the numerics and every measurement),
2026-10-31. Nothing live changed:
the runs, their pinned worktrees and the Mac untouched; checkpoints copied read-only to
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/token-graphs/`.

### 78.1 Why, and what

The desktop GPU's eager inference of the Delver line's token network (128 x 4, the belief head) is
bound by its ~445-585 kernels and 13-15 host syncs a forward, not by its arithmetic (62.2, zero-core
az.md 10.5); it is the desktop's self-play share and every head-to-head and Elo match run on the RTX
5090 (a 2,400-game paired h2h at 32 simulations: ~80 minutes on 2026-10-31). zero-core's
`TokenGraphRunner` captures the network's inference in CUDA graphs: the host packs each batch
(present slots, token counts and positions), one graph per padded (rows: multiple of 64, tokens:
multiple of 16) shape runs a static-shape forward (156 kernels, no sync) with the belief head's
predictions and value-only rows; float32; the answers are eager's to float32 rounding.

### 78.2 How to turn it on (off by default)

* **h2h**: `python -m mtgz.az.h2h A B ... --device cuda --graphs 1` (both sides; `--a-graphs` /
  `--b-graphs` for one side). The output then has `graphs_a` / `graphs_b` (each side's share of batches
  through the graphs: 1.0). Note for the line's matches: `--select` replaces a side's run rule, so pass
  the leaf view as the A/B driver does (`--a-leaf-value-view root --b-leaf-value-view root`).
* **A run** (its desktop self-play and evaluations): the env `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1` on the command that
  starts it - `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1 MTGZ_SUPERVISE_STALL=7200 python tools/launch_hidden.py
  "$RUN/supervisor_console.txt" python tools/supervise.py "$RUN" ...`: the supervisor passes its
  environment to the run, whose `stdout.txt` then says `zero.infer: token network CUDA graphs on ...`
  for each evaluator. No run setting (zero-core's run.py is being changed on another branch); the
  Mac's workers are not affected (they infer on their CPU). It needs the run's pinned build to have
  zero-core 3d5875e or later - a re-pin, the orchestrator's call.
* **bench**: `python -m mtgz.az.bench infer | selfplay ... --device cuda --graphs 1`.
* Off: `ZERO_CUDA_GRAPHS=0` turns the env off (said on stderr); on a CPU evaluator the env is said
  and ignored; `--graphs 1` with `--device cpu` is an error.

### 78.3 Measured (the desktop GPU shared with r3-2b-beliefsearch's training and self-play and another session's h2h; eager and graphs interleaved)

| what | eager | graphs | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| inference, leaves/s at batches of 64 / 144 / 192 / 512 | 3,034 / 4,291 / 5,305 / 6,871 | 21,790 / 27,054 / 25,680 / 26,690 | 7.2x / 6.3x / 4.8x / 3.9x |
| h2h, 200 games, 32 simulations, 200 in flight (batches of 36) | 1,753.7 s | 261.3 s | 6.7x |
| self-play at the line's settings (192 in flight, batches of ~145), leaves/s | 2,195, 2,004 | 6,457, 8,028 | 3.4x |
| h2h, 2,400 paired games (the A/B driver's shape, 1,024 in flight) | ~80 min (that morning's; not interleaved) | 27.8 min | ~2.9x |

* **Numerics** (iteration 328 on the 8,192 held-out rows, batches of 1-1,024): max abs. differences
  priors 2.9e-6, value 9.5e-7, margin 2.4e-6, belief 5.1e-7 (means 1e-7 or less), the same at every size;
  replays deterministic.
* **Equivalence**: iteration 328 against itself, A graphs, B eager, 400 paired games: **A 0.4975 +-
  0.0043** (pairs' se), 197 of 200 deals split, the 3 others 1 for A and 2 for B.
* bfloat16 (measured, not offered): no faster, and 10^4 x the differences.
* From ~192 rows a batch the host's copy of the 37,620-float rows bounds the graphs (~27k leaves/s); a
  sparse feed from the driver is the next step (zero-core az.md 10.6).

## 80. The exhaustive lookahead per information set in Rust, a lookahead player (zero-core `feat/lookahead`, opt-in)

Branch `lookahead` (from main e057c87), zero-core `feat/lookahead` (from main c6b959b; its docs/search.md
3.9 has the design and the API), 2026-11-01, approved by the user that day. Nothing live changed: the
main line r3-2b-beliefsearch is stopped (the user's call), its pinned worktrees, the Delver Lab (:5360),
the Delver AI publisher, the other experiment (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead-teacher/`) and the Mac
untouched; the network is a read-only copy of iteration 475 with its run's config in
`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead/models/r3-2b-beliefsearch/`. Off by default; no merge, no push.

### 80.1 Why

The Delver Lab's x-ply lookahead (delver-lab `delverlab/xply.py`, `xply_is.py`, Python over the bindings)
found lines the network's MCTS misses - Mishra's Bauble first at a turn-1 spot, with a card-dependent
follow-up -: it ignores the prior (every option expanded), decides our moves per information set (the
value of information) and searches every reply. It walks every node in Python and values the leaves on
the CPU (~1,500 positions/s): ~5-30 s a 6-ply decision. The goal: fast enough to play whole evaluation
games with it (a lookahead player), later to produce self-play targets, and to speed up the lab.

### 80.2 What (zero-core docs/search.md 3.9)

`crates/search/src/lookahead.rs` ports the lab's lookahead exactly: plies = decisions with >= 2 options of
either seat (single-option ones stepped by the transition, mana payments - `minor_decision` - the network's
top prior, no ply); horizons `plies`, 'turn', 'next_turn' (`max_plies` 40, `cut` counted); every option or
top-k by prior (`topk_root`, `topk_from_turn`); our decisions per information set (members grouped by an
exact hash of `encode(R)` and the legal options, one choice per group, the max of the group's average) or
per world; the opponent per world by 'min' (best reply), 'expect' (policy-weighted) or 'top'; worlds dealt
from the root decider's view by the seat's root belief (tilt 1 / clip 20 / mix 0.25 for the Delver line's
evaluation seat), explicit seeds in the position API; leaves the value head on `encode(R)`
(root-view), terminals `result()`; a node budget with stages (top-k 4 below the root, then shallower,
then the seat's MCTS) and counters. It is a seat type of zero-core's driver (seat key `lookahead`): its
leaf and prior rows go through the same batches as MCTS leaves, so every game in flight shares one GPU
batch. Leaf values are shared by observation (`dedup`: worlds R cannot tell apart after the same moves
share one row; exact up to float rounding).

What MTG needs: `SearchGame::active_seat` (the active player, for 'next_turn'; engine/src/az/mod.rs, test
`active_seat_is_the_active_player` in tests/az.rs), the existing `minor_decision` (PayMana / PayPool) and
`determinize_with` (the belief head's deal); observation hashing is zero-core's generic hash of the
encoding (the lab's key), no MTG hook. `mtgz/az/lookahead.py`: zero.lookahead with MTG's `reveal` (the
draws / looks a line's move showed, from its chance keys) for the position API's lines. h2h: zero.h2h's
flags pass through `python -m mtgz.az.h2h`.

### 80.3 How to use it

* **A match**: `ZERO_TOKEN_GRAPHS=1 python -m mtgz.az.h2h A B --a-lookahead plies=4,worlds=8,opp=min,budget=100000
  --sims 32 --chance-k 0 --device cuda --graphs 1 --paired --spec "$SPEC" --threads 12 [--conc N --groups G
  --max-rows 1024]`: side A decides by the lookahead (its MCTS settings - the run's evaluation seat, read from
  the checkpoint's run config - deal its worlds by the belief and play its final fallback), B by MCTS. The
  output adds `lookahead_a`, `lookahead_tag_a`, `look` (decisions, nodes, rows, fallbacks per stage, peak live
  games, the search threads' lookahead time).
* **A position** (the lab's call): `from mtgz.az import lookahead as LA; LA.evaluate_position(game, ev,
  {'plies': 6, 'worlds': 8, 'opp': 'min'}, seeds=range(8), belief_tilt=1, belief_clip=20, belief_mix=0.25)`
  -> per root option the value per world, mean +- sd, the modal principal line with labels and reveals, the
  counters; `worlds=[...]` instead of `seeds` takes worlds dealt elsewhere (the parity runs feed the lab's
  code and this one the same worlds).
* Settings: `plies`, `horizon`, `max_plies`, `worlds`, `topk`, `topk_root`, `topk_from_turn`, `opp`
  (min | best | expect | policy | top), `mode` (infoset | world), `budget`, `fallback_topk`, `fallback_plies`,
  `fallback` (mcts | prior), `rows`, `dedup` - an unknown or bad one is an error.

### 80.4 Parity with the lab's Python lookahead

`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead/scripts/parity.py`: for each position the worlds are dealt once (8, by the
Rust deal with the run's evaluation belief - tilt 1, clip 20, mix 0.25 -, deal seeds 0-7) and fed to both:
the lab's `xply_is.run` (information sets) / `xply.run` (per world) with its own `EngineOps` / `NetOps`
(imported read-only from delver-lab; `NetOps`'s `L.evaluate` is position_lab's, copied verbatim) and
`zero.lookahead.evaluate_position(..., worlds=...)`; the same network (iteration 475's copy), CPU eager.
Positions: the turn-1 canary openings of game seeds 1754, 2100, 5103, 6347 (the lab's `opening_spot` rule:
Volcanic Island or a fetch, Mishra's Bauble, Tamiyo and fillers, on the play) and the user's spot - replay
`20261031-204931_001.json.gz` frame 3 = gen 418 game 2 decision 4, P2's turn-1 main phase (Pass, Cast
Mishra's Bauble, Play Polluted Delta / Thundering Falls / Volcanic Island). Settings: both modes, the three
opponent models, 4 and 6 plies, every option (the top-k option is the same code; the lab's information-set
solver caps the root, its per-world tree does not: the harness sets `topk_root` per mode).

| | configurations | identical (values to 1e-5, the choice, every counter) |
|---|---:|---:|
| infoset, min / expect / top, 4 and 6 plies | 30 | 30 |
| world, min / expect / top, 4 and 6 plies | 30 | 29 |

* **Values**: per root option and world, max |difference| 3.6e-7 (means 2.6e-7, sds 1.3e-7) - the network's
  float rounding at other batch shapes (the lab evaluates in chunks of 512 rows, the Rust in rounds of up
  to 512).
* **Counters**: nodes (836-1,929 at 4 plies, 3,949-17,598 at 6), leaves, prior rows, value rows, minor
  steps, groups: identical in all 60.
* **The one difference** (seed 6347, per world, min, 6 plies): options 39 and 0 within 6e-8 of each other
  (0.56776302 / 0.56776296 in Python, equal in Rust): the choice flipped by float rounding, not a difference
  of semantics.
* **Lines**: the modal principal line the same for 244 of 252 options (the rest: near-ties deeper in the
  tree; the lab's modal key also includes its reveal annotations).
* **Dedup on** (the default; the table ran with it off): the 6-ply information-set runs at all five
  positions again identical (values to 1.8e-7), the lab's value rows = the rows sent + the shared ones, 57-71%
  of the leaves shared. The whole table again on the final build (ff33648, dedup on, the sparse sink and hash):
  the same 59 of 60, the same near-tie.
* Time (CPU, the same network, 8 torch threads, the desktop shared): the 60 runs took 161 s in the lab's
  Python and 99 s in Rust - on the CPU both are bound by the network (the GPU numbers are 80.5).

### 80.5 Throughput

**One position at a time** (the position API, the lab's call: one game in flight; the GPU's token graphs,
`scripts/bench_look.py`; 13 positions - the 5 parity spots on turn 1 and 8 of gen 418 #2 from turn 3 on, >= 4
options; 8 worlds, best reply; the desktop shared with this branch's own h2h):

| plies | branching | s / decision (turn 1 / mid-game) | nodes / decision | nodes / s | value rows shared |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | every option | 0.19 (0.13 / 0.22) | 2,113 | 11,271 | 75% |
| 4 | top-k 4 | 0.10 (0.08 / 0.11) | 1,352 | 13,709 | 70% |
| 5 | every option | 0.37 (0.25 / 0.45) | 6,252 | 16,723 | 74% |
| 5 | top-k 4 | 0.24 (0.18 / 0.28) | 3,562 | 14,728 | 68% |
| 6 | every option | 0.80 (0.46 / 1.02) | 18,142 | 22,650 | 72% |
| 6 | top-k 4 | 0.53 (0.40 / 0.61) | 9,357 | 17,824 | 67% |

The lab's Python took 7-10 s for the user's spot at 6 plies (17,598 nodes, CPU); the same lookahead here
0.64-1.2 s on the GPU. One position is bound by the lookahead's own CPU work on one thread (clones,
transitions, encodings and their hashes: ~40-60 us a node), not by the network.

**Many games in flight** (the driver, `scripts/bench_driver.py`: the h2h's shape - the lookahead seat against
the run's MCTS evaluation seat, paired games, sparse batches, 4 groups, 12 search threads; best reply):

| plies | branching | 1 game in flight: decisions / s (s a decision) | 64 in flight: decisions / s | nodes / s | rows / s | evaluators' share |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | every option | 17.3 (0.058) | 104 | 83k | 29k | 0.50 |
| 4 | top-k 4 | 18.1 (0.055) | 126 | 76k | 29k | 0.67 |
| 5 | every option | 12.5 (0.080) | 65 | 143k | 48k | 0.45 |
| 5 | top-k 4 | 13.6 (0.074) | 87 | 139k | 48k | 0.56 |
| 6 | every option | 5.6 (0.177) | 40 | 242k | 79k | 0.55 |
| 6 | top-k 4 | 8.6 (0.117) | 55 | 225k | 79k | 0.64 |

(60 s from the games' start each - mostly the first turns, ~580-6,000 nodes a decision; the desktop otherwise
idle.) Many games in flight multiply the decisions per second by 6-7: the GPU batches every game's rows
together (79k rows/s at 6 plies, against ~27k leaves/s for MCTS's batches of a few hundred rows in 78.3).
The speed-ups that got there (zero-core, opt-in): **sparse batches** (each row's ~150 non-zeros instead of
37,620 floats: the batches' assembly into fresh memory had been 59% of a 4-ply match's wall time; a 32-game
match 165 s -> 89 s, the same games), **4 driver groups** (89 s -> 65 s), the evaluator's `max_rows` pieces
two in flight, the graphs' host copy over 4 threads for big dense batches, leaf values shared by observation
(57-81% of the leaves), encoding in place in the batch buffer.

**CPU only** (eager CPU network, 8 torch threads, 8 positions - the 5 of turn 1 and 3 mid-game -, the desktop
idle): 4 plies 0.15 s a decision (GPU 0.12), 6 plies 1.04 s (GPU 0.58; 28,872 nodes a decision at these
positions): one position is mostly the lookahead's own CPU work, the GPU's edge is in batching many games.


### 80.6 First lookahead player against the MCTS player

The same network for both sides (iteration 475's copy), the run's spec, `--chance-k 0`, paired games. B = the
run's evaluation seat: 32 simulations, the 'cq' rule with select_min_visits 4 and select scale 0.3, root-view
leaves, the root belief (tilt 1, mix 0.25). A = the same seat with `--a-lookahead`: per information set, 8
worlds dealt by its belief, every option, the stated opponent model and budget (fallback: top-k 4 below the
root, then 2 plies fewer, then the seat's MCTS). Scores are A's (+- 1 se of the pair scores).

| A (the lookahead side) | pairs | A's score | Elo | wall / 100 games (in flight) | A's decisions; nodes / rows a decision | fallbacks (top-k / MCTS) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 4 plies, best reply, budget 100k | 100 | **0.315 +- 0.030** | -135 | 693 s (200; dense) | 23,875; 852 / 262 | 6 / 0 |
| 4 plies, policy-weighted, budget 100k | 100 | **0.390 +- 0.034** | -78 | 540 s (200; dense) | 22,598; 821 / 348 | 7 / 0 |
| 6 plies, best reply, budget 150k | 50 | **0.470 +- 0.046** | -21 | 877 s (64) | 13,193; 6,638 / 2,118 | 80 / 0 |
| 6 plies, policy-weighted, budget 150k | 50 | **0.370 +- 0.045** | -93 | 910 s (64) | 10,979; 6,974 / 3,249 | 77 / 0 |
| guarded, 4 plies, 16 worlds, policy-weighted, 5 pp | 300 | **0.515 +- 0.015** | +10 | 365 s (100) | 71,427; 1,880 / 640; **1.9% overridden** | 15+ / 0 |
| guarded, 6 plies, 16 worlds, policy-weighted, 5 pp, budget 300k | 50 | **0.460 +- 0.035** | -28 | 2,583 s (64) | 12,387; 13,445 / 5,506; **2.3% overridden** | 112 / 0 |

(The first two ran on dense batches before 80.5's speed-ups, the rest on sparse batches with 4 driver groups;
"wall / 100 games" is the match's wall time per 100 games with that many in flight on the shared desktop.)

* **The pure lookahead player loses to MCTS at 32 simulations** at 4 plies by 80-135 Elo and at 6 plies by
  20-90: it picks the best of every option's lookahead value, and those values carry the value head's noise -
  the max over many of them is biased upward (the optimizer's curse). The teacher experiment
  (`E:/mtg-zero-scratch/lookahead-teacher/results/summary.json`, another session's) measured the same from the
  other side: on 203 non-trivial decisions of generations 380-454 the 6-ply lookahead disagrees with the
  network's 8 x 64 MCTS at 37-42% and its moves played out worse there (-1.0 +- 0.6 pp best reply, -1.1 +- 0.7
  policy-weighted), predicting +2.4 pp; large predicted differences were well calibrated.
* **The guarded player** (the coordinator's ask after that finding; `guard`, docs/search.md 3.9 in zero-core)
  keeps the MCTS move unless the lookahead's best option beats the MCTS move's lookahead value by more than 5
  pp: at 4 plies it changes 1.9% of its decisions and scores 0.515 +- 0.015 over 300 pairs (0.555, 0.500, 0.490
  in three batches of 100 - the first one's +38 Elo was luck): even with MCTS-32, +10 Elo within 1 se; at 6
  plies (2.3% changed) 0.460 +- 0.035 over 50 pairs - no better. The few moves the lookahead is very sure of
  do not add measurable strength at these sample sizes.
* Best reply beats policy-weighted at 6 plies (0.47 against 0.37) and loses at 4 (0.315 against 0.39): at 6
  plies the lookahead sees the opponent's reply and our answer to it; at 4 the pessimistic reply ends many
  lines one ply after it.

### 80.7 What a 1,300-game evaluation would take

From the matches above and 80.5 (the desktop as it was: sometimes two matches sharing it; a game is ~115-125
lookahead decisions plus as many MCTS ones; 1,300 games = 650 pairs):

| the lookahead side | per 100 games (in flight) | 1,300 games |
|---|---:|---:|
| 4 plies, 8 worlds | ~150-200 s (64-100; sparse, 4 groups) | ~35-45 min |
| 5 plies, 8 worlds | ~1.6x 4 plies (80.5's decisions / s) | ~1-1.2 h |
| 6 plies, 8 worlds | 877-910 s (64) | ~3.2 h |
| guarded, 4 plies, 16 worlds | 365 s (100) | ~1.3 h |
| guarded, 6 plies, 16 worlds | 2,583 s (64) | ~9.3 h |

More games in flight (128-256) should shorten the 6-ply runs further (the batches grow; memory: ~11 KB a live
member game, the largest 6-ply decision held 230k at once - 2.5 GB). Top-k 4 below the root cuts 6 plies by
~30% (80.5).

### 80.9 What next (proposals, not done)

* The lookahead as a **training target**: not as the policy (its pure moves lose), maybe as a guarded
  correction or a value target at the root; needs its own A/B.
* **Fewer noisy maxima**: a lower-variance leaf (a few MCTS simulations per leaf instead of the raw value),
  the prior as a tie-breaker / regulariser at our decisions, or more worlds where the root options are close.
* **Speed**: within-decision parallelism (one position is single-threaded: the lab's latency), sparse batches
  for MCTS self-play and evaluation (their batches are bound by the same host copies, 78.3).
